searchDocs.title: Season math​
searchDocs.content: The season index is a calendar-month index, not a rolling 30-day window: BattlePassState.seasonIndex(now) = year*12 + (month-1), computed in the timezone defined by BattlePassConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset (a fixed seconds-from-UTC offset, pre-launch default US Eastern -5*3600, mirroring QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset). Being a fixed offset, month boundaries do not track daylight saving. The underlying day math (daysFromCivil) is a pure-integer proleptic-Gregorian calculation (Howard Hinnant's algorithm) so client and server always agree without relying on os.date's host timezone handling. BattlePassState.seasonExpiresAt(now) returns the unix timestamp of the first of the next month (in the same offset timezone) and is sent to the client so it can drive a countdown without any client-side date math. The server re-checks online players for a rollover — and refreshes cached premium status — every BattlePassConfig.ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS (default 60s).  The quest system's Season scope (see Quests — Season quests) uses this exact same seasonIndex as its period key, so a battle pass season and its season-long quests always start and end together.

searchDocs.title: EXP earning​
searchDocs.content: There is no gameplay source that awards battle pass EXP directly. Instead, BattlePassManager subscribes to Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted — fired by QuestManager.grantReward on every quest reward grant, manual claim or rollover auto-sweep alike — and reads the optional Reward.BPExp field off the quest's reward table:  Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted:Connect(function(player, reward) if reward and reward.BPExp then BattlePassManager.AddExp(player, reward.BPExp, "Quest") end end)   Any quest can feed the pass just by adding a BPExp number to its Reward table — no new signal or wiring per quest. The shipped pool leans on this for its dedicated Scope = "Season" quests: three quests (SeasonJunk, SeasonKills, SeasonDistance) with the whole set active for the entire month (not rotated/shuffled like Daily/Weekly), each paying 0 coins/exp but 3000 BPExp — see QuestConfig.Quests. Regular Daily/Weekly quests also carry smaller BPExp amounts (e.g. JunkDailyA pays 200), so ordinary questing keeps the pass moving too.

searchDocs.title: Tier track + bulk claim​
searchDocs.content: BattlePassConfig.Tiers[level] (level = 1..MAX_LEVEL, MAX_LEVEL = 60) is a { Free: Reward?, Premium: Reward? } pair. A Reward is either { Type = "Coins", Amount } or { Type = "Item", ItemId } (an empty ItemId = "" marks a milestone slot not filled in yet). The shipped defaults: regular tiers pay Coins on both rows scaling gently with depth (Free = 100 + (level-1)*10, Premium = 150 + (level-1)*15); tiers 15/30/45/60 are milestones — a chunkier 500-coin Free reward plus an (empty, to be filled) Premium accessory Item slot. BattlePassConfig.SeasonOverrides[seasonIndex][level] sparsely shadows the base Tiers entry for one specific season only (e.g. swap in a different accessory for one month while keeping the rest of the track the same); BattlePassState.tierReward(level, row, seasonIndex) resolves the override first, falling back to the base table, and is used identically by the server (grant) and client (display) so the two can never disagree.  Level is derived, never stored: BattlePassState.levelFromExp(exp) walks MAX_LEVEL down to 1 and returns the highest level whose cumulative EXP threshold (BattlePassConfig.ExpPerLevel — a flat per-level number or a { [level]: number } table) is met; BattlePassState.progress(exp) additionally returns (level, expIntoLevel, expForNextLevel) for a progress bar (the last two are 0 once level >= MAX_LEVEL).  There is only one claim entry point: Packets.ReqClaimBattlePass (no payload) invokes BattlePassManager.ClaimBattlePass(player), which bulk-banks every unlocked-but-unclaimed reward across both rows in one call — there's no per-tier claim. Premium-row rewards are only granted while the player is currently premium. Claimed flags (ClaimedFree[level] / ClaimedPremium[level]) are set before the grant executes (the same idempotent-guard pattern as QuestManager.ClaimQuest), so a re-entrant call finds nothing outstanding and returns NOTHING_TO_CLAIM rather than double-paying. Returns (ok, reasonCode, freeCount, premiumCount, coinsGranted); counts/coins are 0 on any failure. Result codes (BattlePassResultCodes): OK = 0, NO_PROFILE = 1, NOTHING_TO_CLAIM = 2.

searchDocs.title: Premium (subscriptions)​
searchDocs.content: Premium is never persisted — it's live-resolved from MarketplaceService:GetUserSubscriptionStatusAsync(player, BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID) and cached in-memory per session (premiumCache, keyed by Player). The cache is (re)populated at three points: on join (before the first sweep/replicate), on MarketplaceService.PromptSubscriptionPurchaseFinished (the prompt closing doesn't guarantee a successful purchase, so status is always re-resolved rather than assumed), and on the periodic rollover tick (bounding staleness to ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS). resolvePremium yields (a web call) so it only ever runs from spawned contexts — never from the synchronous AddExp/ClaimBattlePass paths, which read the cache. On a false→true transition (a fresh subscribe), onPurchaseFinished retroactively runs a sweep granting the Premium row for every tier already reached this season, so buying mid-season immediately feels rewarding instead of only affecting future tiers. Packets.ReqPromptPremium (no payload, server-initiated) calls MarketplaceService:PromptSubscriptionPurchase — the prompt must originate server-side.  While BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID = "" (the pre-launch default), premium is never granted and the subscription APIs are skipped entirely — resolvePremium short-circuits to false and ReqPromptPremium returns false without calling MarketplaceService, so pre-launch never spams errors for a subscription that doesn't exist yet.

searchDocs.title: Rollover + auto-grant sweep​
searchDocs.content: ensureCurrent (called at the top of AddExp and ClaimBattlePass, on join, and on the rollover tick) compares the profile's stored SeasonIndex against BattlePassState.seasonIndex(os.time()). On a mismatch it first auto-grants every reached-but-unclaimed tier from the old season (Free always; Premium only if the player is currently premium) via the same sweep helper the manual claim uses — nothing earned is lost just because a player never opened a claim UI before the month rolled. It then resets Exp = 0, ClaimedFree = {}, ClaimedPremium = {}, and advances SeasonIndex to the current value. Coins and items already granted by the sweep persist wherever they live (the coin wallet, a future inventory) — only the pass's own tier/EXP bookkeeping resets.

searchDocs.title: Item seam​
searchDocs.content: Item-type rewards fire Signals.OnBattlePassItemGranted(player, itemId) — a seam with no consumer this cycle, reserved for a future inventory/accessory system. Milestone tiers ship with an empty Premium Item slot (ItemId = ""); granting one is a no-op (no signal fires) and logs a one-time warning (warnedEmptyItem, a module-level flag) reminding a developer to fill BattlePassConfig with a real asset before launch. The claimed flag is still set even for an empty slot, so it's marked claimed and never re-offered.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: BattlePassClient is a GUI-agnostic read-model, same shape as QuestClient/PerkClient: it caches the authoritative BattlePassStateSync snapshot and derives per-tier TierView descriptors (Level, FreeReward, PremiumReward, IsUnlocked, IsFreeClaimed, IsPremiumClaimed) using the same BattlePassState.tierReward the server grants from. Exposes GetProgress (level, expIntoLevel, expForNextLevel), GetLevel, IsPremium, GetSeasonExpiresAt, GetTiers (all 60, in order), GetClaimableSummary (a preview of what a Claim() would bank right now — counts + coin total, without actually claiming), and fire-and-forget Claim() / PromptPremium() commands. A Changed signal fires on every snapshot update for consumers to repaint. No GUI ships this cycle — a future screen requires BattlePassClient and subscribes to Changed.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant QM as QuestManager (server) participant BPM as BattlePassManager (server) participant Client as BattlePassClient (owning client) Note over QM: quest CLAIM or auto-sweep QM->>QM: grantReward() — CoinManager.AddCoins, XPManager.AddXP QM->>BPM: Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted:Fire(player, quest.Reward) alt reward.BPExp present BPM->>BPM: AddExp(player, reward.BPExp) — ensureCurrent() first BPM->>BPM: profile.Data.Exp += amount alt derived level rose BPM->>BPM: Signals.OnBattlePassLevelUp:Fire(player, newLevel) end BPM->>Client: BattlePassStateSync (season, exp, level, progress, claimed, premium, expiresAt) end Note over Client,BPM: bulk CLAIM Client->>BPM: ReqClaimBattlePass() BPM->>BPM: ensureCurrent(); sweep(1..level) — Free always, Premium if isPremium BPM->>BPM: claimed flags set BEFORE grant (idempotent guard) BPM-->>Client: (ok, reasonCode, freeCount, premiumCount, coinsGranted) BPM->>Client: BattlePassStateSync (reconciled snapshot)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — BattlePassConfig.luau is the tuning surface: STORE_NAME, SUBSCRIPTION_ID, ResetTimezoneOffset, MAX_LEVEL, ExpPerLevel, ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS, Tiers, SeasonOverrides.  Shared — BattlePassState.luau is pure, side-effect-free: seasonIndex/seasonExpiresAt (season math), levelFromExp/progress (level derivation), tierReward (base+override reward resolution). Both server and client require it directly so they never disagree — the same pattern as QuestState.  Shared — BattlePassResultCodes.luau is the frozen result-code enum returned by ClaimBattlePass (OK=0, NO_PROFILE=1, NOTHING_TO_CLAIM=2).  Server — BattlePassManager.luau owns the PlayerBattlePass ProfileStore profile (one session per player, key = UserId), place-agnostic (runs in both lobby and gameplay places, mirroring QuestManager/PerkManager). Exposes AddExp, ClaimBattlePass, GetLevel, IsPremium, and Initialize (wires the profile lifecycle, the ReqClaimBattlePass/ReqPromptPremium handlers, the OnQuestRewardGranted EXP feed, the PromptSubscriptionPurchaseFinished hook, and the combined rollover/premium-refresh tick). Registers a flush callback with PersistenceRegistry for BindToClose safety.  Client — BattlePassClient.luau is the GUI-agnostic data layer (see Client above).

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: All tuning lives in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/BattlePassConfig.luau.  Field	EffectSTORE_NAME	ProfileStore key — change this only if you intentionally want to wipe all saved battle pass progress (see Tune Battle Pass). SUBSCRIPTION_ID	The Roblox subscription id whose active status unlocks Premium. Empty ("") disables premium entirely and skips the subscription APIs. ResetTimezoneOffset	Fixed seconds-from-UTC offset the calendar-month boundary is measured in (mirrors QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset). No DST tracking. MAX_LEVEL	Top tier of the track (60). ExpPerLevel	BP EXP required per level — a flat number or a { [level]: number } table. ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS	How often the live server tick re-checks online players for a season rollover and refreshes cached premium status. Tiers[level].Free / .Premium	Base reward per tier per row. SeasonOverrides[seasonIndex][level]	Sparse per-season tier reward shadowing, keyed by BattlePassState.seasonIndex.  QuestConfig.Quests[id].Reward.BPExp (optional) is how a quest feeds the pass; Scope = "Season" quests are the dedicated monthly source (see Quests — Season quests).

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved battle pass data BattlePassConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerBattlePass") must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places — it's the shared ProfileStore key that lets session-locking hand off cleanly across the teleport boundary. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile: all season progress and claimed flags become unreachable.  An empty ItemId slot grants nothing — and is still marked claimed A milestone Item reward with ItemId = "" is a placeholder. Granting it fires no OnBattlePassItemGranted signal (nothing to grant) but still flips the claimed flag, so the player never sees it offered again even after you fill in a real ItemId later — fill milestone slots before launch.

searchDocs.title: Placement → mount → fire​
searchDocs.content: Place — the cannon is a placeable (PlaceableItems/Cannon + PlaceableTools/Cannon). Placement, stash, and move are inherited from the placement system; the placed clone lands in workspace/PlacedObjects with a PlaceableName = "Cannon" attribute.Mount — CannonController attaches a ProximityPrompt to each placed cannon'sMountPromptPart. Triggering it sends ReqMountCannon(model); the server validates proximity + single-occupancy and records the gunner. Mounting locks the gunner's movement and shows a ballistic arc preview.Fire — input sends ReqFireCannon(muzzle, aimDir). The server validates occupancy, cooldown, and overheat, then simulates the shell from its own muzzle CFrame with a gravity Acceleration. On impact it applies Damage × (1 + CannonDamageBonus) viaCombatService.ApplyAOE and broadcasts CannonFired (muzzle flash + barrel snap + sound) and ExplosionAt (boom).

searchDocs.title: Overheat​
searchDocs.content: Each shot adds HeatPerShot; heat decays at HeatDecayPerSec. Reaching MaxHeat locks the cannon for OverheatLockTime. Heat (0–1) and Overheated are attributes on the placed Model (no packet); CannonGuiController reads them to drive the gunner's heat bar.

searchDocs.title: Server authority & anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Occupancy, cooldown, overheat-lock, and shell origin are all re-validated server-side; the server fires from its own muzzle, so a forged origin/aim cannot help. Single occupant per cannon (a live occupant blocks takeover; a dead one is replaced). CannonDamageBonusis read server-side from the server-written PartyPerkBuffs folder per shot — unforgeable. Faction routing is inherited from CombatService, so EnemyNPC rigs must be in a hostile faction to take player damage.

searchDocs.title: EnemyShip forward seam​
searchDocs.content: CannonServer.applyCannonAOE damages Humanoids via CombatService and decrements a numeric Health attribute on in-radius models tagged EnemyShip (linear falloff, destroy at ≤0). This is inert until the future enemy-ship spec tags ships; it requires no change to the perk hook.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: UserInputService:GetMouseDelta() (every RenderStep, when look is active) └─> yaw -= delta.X * CameraConfig.MouseLookBaseSpeed * sensitivity pitch -= delta.Y * CameraConfig.MouseLookBaseSpeed * sensitivity pitch = CameraRig.ClampPitch(pitch, MinPitch, MaxPitch) (sensitivity comes from SettingsClient.Get("CameraSensitivity"), live-updated via Signals.OnSettingChanged) Scroll wheel (UserInputService.InputChanged, MouseWheel) └─> targetDistance = clamp(targetDistance + step, CameraMinZoomDistance, maxDistanceForMode()) RunService RenderStep "Camera" (Priority = Camera) ├─ if buildModeActive: return (PlacementCameraController owns the camera) ├─ reassert camera.CameraType = Scriptable if something else changed it ├─ occlusion raycast from the offset focus toward the desired camera position │ └─> renderDistance smoothed toward occludedDistance (BoomSmoothingSpeed * dt) ├─ CameraRig.Compose(subject.Position, offsetHolder.Value, yaw, pitch, renderDistance, lookOffset) │ └─> camera.CFrame, camera.Focus └─ HRP facing: lerp toward camera yaw (aim) or move direction (locked/free-look) External signal fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true/false) └─> CameraController sets aimMode, calls applyState() ├─ offsetSpring:SetTarget(ShootingOffset or ThirdPersonOffset) ├─ angleSpring:SetTarget(ShootingLookAngle or ThirdPersonLookAngle) ├─ MouseBehavior = LockCenter + cursor hidden (aim / locked 3P) │ or Default + cursor shown (free-look OR GUI cursor request) ├─ reticleImage.Visible = aimMode └─> Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled:Fire(aimMode) LeftAlt key pressed (ContextActionService, non-aim only) └─> freeLookMode toggles -> applyState() (while freeLookMode is true, mouse-look only runs while RMB is held) Signals.RequestMouseIcon(visible) └─> guiRequestsMouse = visible -> applyState() (frees/hides the cursor and suspends look independent of free-look) Signals.OnBuildModeChanged(isActive) └─> buildModeActive = isActive (render step becomes a full no-op while true; reclaims Scriptable on resume)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: The camera system is client-only — there is no server component.  CameraController.client.luau  Owns all camera state and the render step. Two orthogonal booleans select the mode (aim wins over free-look):  aimMode — set exclusively via Signals.RequestShootingCamera. No player keybind activates aim directly; only tools (GrabHook on equip), weapons (WeaponController on weapon equip/unequip), and systems (PlacementClient on build-mode entry) fire this signal.freeLookMode — toggled by LeftAlt via ContextActionService:BindAction("ToggleCameraMode", ...); inert while aimMode is true (the action sinks the input but silently no-ops).  Two more flags participate in lookActive()/applyState() without being a "mode" of their own:  guiRequestsMouse — set by Signals.RequestMouseIcon; frees and shows the cursor and suspends mouse-look, independent of freeLookMode.buildModeActive — set by Signals.OnBuildModeChanged; see Placement camera.  On every CharacterAdded a new MotionMaster.Spring (offsetSpring) is created bound to a plain { Value, Parent = true } holder (offsetHolder), not directly to humanoid.CameraOffset — the spring drives offsetHolder.Value, which the render step then feeds into CameraRig.Compose as the screen-relative offset. The spring's Omega/Zeta come from CameraConfig; it is destroyed on CharacterRemoving. The render step runs at Camera priority via RunService:BindToRenderStep("Camera", Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value, ...).  CameraRig.luau (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/CameraRig.luau)  Pure, stateless camera math shared by nothing else today but kept separate so it's independently testable/reviewable:  CameraRig.ClampPitch(pitch, minPitch, maxPitch): number — math.clamp wrapper.CameraRig.Compose(focusPosition, offset, yaw, pitch, distance, lookOffset): (CFrame, Vector3) — rotates offset into the yaw/pitch look frame, adds it to focusPosition to get the adjusted focus, then backs the camera off distance studs along the look vector. Returns (cameraCFrame, adjustedFocusPosition); the caller assigns these to camera.CFrame and camera.Focus respectively.

searchDocs.title: Per-mode look angle​
searchDocs.content: lookOffset is an optional Vector2 (radians, X=pitch, Y=yaw) that rotates the look direction about the fixed camera position — the camera position and the occlusion raycast (which fires before Compose runs, off targetDistance/renderDistance) are untouched. nil/zero is a no-op, matching the pre-existing camera behavior exactly.  CameraConfig.ShootingLookAngle and CameraConfig.ThirdPersonLookAngle supply this in degrees (X=pitch, +up/−down; Y=yaw, +left/−right); CameraController blends the active mode's angle with a second MotionMaster.Spring — mirroring offsetSpring/offsetHolder exactly (retargeted on the same applyState() calls that retarget the offset spring, created/destroyed alongside it) — converts the blended value to radians, and passes it into CameraRig.Compose every frame. Because aim/shot raycasts read the live camera through screen center rather than a separate aim-vector, aiming stays consistent under any angle with no additional math to keep in sync.

searchDocs.title: Modes​
searchDocs.content: Locked third-person (default) — mouse always drives yaw/pitch (lookActive() returns true); MouseBehavior = LockCenter, cursor hidden; the HRP lerps to face humanoid.MoveDirection while moving.  Aim — entered only via Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true). Shoulder offset (CameraConfig.ShootingOffset) via the offset spring, reticle visible, mouse locked+hidden, HRP lerps to face the camera's yaw (not movement direction) so aiming and strafing look correct together. Exiting fires Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled(false).  Free-look — toggled by LeftAlt when not aiming. Cursor is freed and shown (MouseBehavior = Default), but lookActive() only returns true while the right mouse button is held (UserInputService:IsMouseButtonPressed(Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton2)) — a faithful port of the old default-camera free-look behavior. HRP still lerps to face movement direction, same as locked third-person.  Signals.RequestMouseIcon is orthogonal to all three modes: while guiRequestsMouse is true (and aimMode is false), the cursor is freed/shown and lookActive() returns false regardless of freeLookMode, for GUIs (e.g. the workbench) that need a clickable cursor.

searchDocs.title: Sensitivity​
searchDocs.content: sensitivity is read once at startup from SettingsClient.Get("CameraSensitivity") and kept live-updated by subscribing to Signals.OnSettingChanged (filtering on key == "CameraSensitivity"). Every frame that lookActive() is true, raw pixel delta from UserInputService:GetMouseDelta() is scaled by CameraConfig.MouseLookBaseSpeed * sensitivity before being applied to yaw/pitch. See Settings for how CameraSensitivity is defined, synced, and persisted.

searchDocs.title: Zoom​
searchDocs.content: Scroll wheel input (UserInputService.InputChanged, filtered to Enum.UserInputType.MouseWheel and not gameProcessed) adjusts targetDistance by CameraConfig.ScrollZoomStep per notch, clamped to [CameraConfig.CameraMinZoomDistance, maxDistanceForMode()]. maxDistanceForMode() returns ShootingCameraMaxZoomDistance in aim mode or ThirdPersonCameraMaxZoomDistance otherwise — the same per-mode ceiling switch the old CameraBoomController did off OnShootingCameraToggled, now just a local function call since everything lives in one script.

searchDocs.title: Occlusion​
searchDocs.content: Folded into CameraController's own render step (previously a second script, CameraBoomController.client.luau, now deleted). Each frame: a raycast runs from the offset focus point (subject.Position + offset rotated into the look frame) toward the desired camera position, excluding the local character (RaycastParams.FilterType = Exclude, RespectCanCollide = true). If it hits, occludedDistance is clamped to hitDistance - CameraConfig.BoomBuffer (floored at CameraMinZoomDistance); otherwise it's just targetDistance. A separate renderDistance is lerped toward occludedDistance at BoomSmoothingSpeed * dt per frame and is what actually gets passed to CameraRig.Compose — targetDistance (the zoom-wheel target) is never touched by occlusion, so releasing from behind a wall smoothly zooms back out to the player's chosen distance.

searchDocs.title: Placement camera​
searchDocs.content: While build mode is active, PlacementCameraController.client.luau — a separate script, not part of CameraController — takes exclusive ownership of the camera:  Sets Camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable and drives Camera.CFrame every frame: fixed height and pitch above the player (PlacementConfig.TopDownHeight/TopDownPitch), locked to whatever yaw the player was facing when build mode started.Eases into and out of the top-down angle via an exponential chase-lerp (alpha = 1 - exp(-CameraTransitionSpeed * dt), same idiom as PlacementSystem's FreeModeLerpSpeed/RotationLerpSpeed) rather than snapping instantly. On exit there's no live Custom-camera CFrame to blend toward, so it eases toward an approximation reconstructed from the camera's offset relative to the player's HumanoidRootPart at the moment build mode was entered, applied to the player's current position — then hands off to Enum.CameraType.Custom once that blend has settled (EXIT_SETTLE_TIME, ≈0.2s at the default speed). Any residual approximation error is invisible: the instant Custom resumes control, it corrects to the true position.Also fades any PlacementConfig.OccluderTag-tagged parts (e.g. roofs) to OccluderTransparency for the duration, restoring their original transparency on exit.Fires Signals.RequestMouseIcon(true) on PC (gated on UserInputService.MouseEnabled and UserInputService.KeyboardEnabled) so CameraController frees and shows the cursor instead of locking it to screen-center. This is required because the placement camera doesn't rotate with mouse movement, so mouse.UnitRay (used by PlacementClient for the placement raycast) needs a cursor that can actually move to aim anywhere but straight down at the player.Restores Enum.CameraType.Custom immediately (hard cut, no blend) on CharacterRemoving — a backstop in case build mode didn't cleanly exit first, e.g. character death — the mouse-icon request and occluder fade are restored at the same point (skipped if a build-mode exit already restored them moments earlier).  CameraController and PlacementCameraController now both own the Scriptable camera at different times, and coordinate via Signals.OnBuildModeChanged. Unlike the old default-camera (Custom) architecture — where CameraController never touched Camera.CFrame/Camera.CameraType and so ran harmlessly underneath the placement camera regardless of what it did — CameraController is now itself a Scriptable-camera owner and would fight PlacementCameraController for the same properties every frame if left running. CameraController subscribes to Signals.OnBuildModeChanged and sets buildModeActive accordingly; its render step's first statement is if buildModeActive then return end, a full no-op (no CFrame, Focus, or CameraType writes) for the duration of build mode. On resume it reasserts camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable (guarded — only writes if the current value isn't already Scriptable, to avoid a redundant property set every frame).  Accepted ~0.2s exit-stutter PlacementCameraController's own exit-blend keeps writing camera.CFrame for EXIT_SETTLE_TIME (≈0.2s at the default CameraTransitionSpeed) after build mode ends, before it hands CameraType back to Custom. Since CameraController resumes its own Scriptable writes immediately when OnBuildModeChanged(false) fires, there is a brief window where both scripts could in principle write Camera.CFrame on the same frame-ish timescale, producing a small visual stutter at the exact moment of exiting build mode. This is a known, accepted residual limitation — not a bug to be silently fixed — because eliminating it would require either a new cross-module "exit fully settled" signal or coupling CameraController to PlacementCameraController's private EXIT_SETTLE_TIME constant, both judged not worth the coupling for a sub-quarter-second cosmetic blip.

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: All knobs are in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/CameraConfig.luau:  Field	Value	DescriptionShootingOffset	Vector3(1.75, 1, 0)	Screen-relative offset target in aim mode, fed to CameraRig.Compose ThirdPersonOffset	Vector3(0.5, 0.3, 0)	Screen-relative offset target in default mode ShootingLookAngle	Vector2(0, 0)	Look angle target in aim mode, degrees (X=pitch, +up/−down; Y=yaw, +left/−right), fed to CameraRig.Compose ThirdPersonLookAngle	Vector2(0, 0)	Look angle target in default mode, degrees (X=pitch, +up/−down; Y=yaw, +left/−right) OffsetSpringOmega	22	Natural frequency of the offset spring OffsetSpringZeta	0.75	Damping ratio of the offset spring RotationLerpSpeed	12	Per-second rate for the 1 - exp(-rate*dt) HRP rotation lerp ReticleImage	asset id string	Image shown in the crosshair GUI during aim mode ReticleScale	0.0296	Crosshair size as a fraction of viewport height MouseLookBaseSpeed	0.006	Radians of yaw/pitch rotation per pixel of mouse delta, at sensitivity = 1 MinPitch	math.rad(-75)	Lower pitch clamp passed to CameraRig.ClampPitch MaxPitch	math.rad(75)	Upper pitch clamp passed to CameraRig.ClampPitch ScrollZoomStep	1.5	Studs of targetDistance change per scroll notch DefaultZoomDistance	9	Initial targetDistance/renderDistance on spawn BoomEnabled	true	Set to false to disable occlusion clamping entirely BoomBuffer	0.5	Studs subtracted from hit distance before applying zoom clamp BoomSmoothingSpeed	10	Lerp speed for renderDistance chasing occludedDistance CameraMinZoomDistance	6	Hard floor for targetDistance/renderDistance ShootingCameraMaxZoomDistance	9	Ceiling in aim mode ThirdPersonCameraMaxZoomDistance	9	Ceiling in third-person/free-look mode

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Aim mode is signal-only There is no keybind that activates aimMode directly. Only external systems fire Signals.RequestShootingCamera. If a new tool or system needs to enter aim mode it must fire this signal — do not read or write the aimMode local directly.  Do not use TweenService to animate the camera offset. offsetSpring is a MotionMaster.Spring driver bound to offsetHolder.Value; bypassing it will produce conflicting states and the spring will override any TweenService tween on the next frame.CameraController and PlacementCameraController both write Camera.CameraType/Camera.CFrame and must never run their write paths in the same frame — that's what buildModeActive (via Signals.OnBuildModeChanged) exists to prevent. Do not add a third script that writes Camera.CFrame without wiring it into this same coordination.The offset spring is re-created on every CharacterAdded and destroyed on CharacterRemoving. Holding a reference to an old spring past the character death will produce a dangling driver pointing at a destroyed Humanoid.freeLookMode frees and shows the mouse cursor, but — unlike the old default-camera implementation — does not re-enable humanoid.AutoRotate; CameraController always drives HRP facing itself (toward camera yaw in aim, toward move direction otherwise) and sets humanoid.AutoRotate = false unconditionally (skipped entirely while humanoid.Sit is true). Any system that expects rotation to be script-driven should listen to OnShootingCameraToggled rather than polling AutoRotate.A GUI that needs a clickable cursor fires Signals.RequestMouseIcon:Fire(true); while set (and not aiming) the camera holds MouseBehavior = Default and shows the cursor, restoring LockCenter on Fire(false). The PC gate lives in the producer (WorkbenchGuiController, PlacementCameraController), so the camera frees the mouse whenever asked regardless of platform.CameraSensitivity changes take effect on the very next frame via Signals.OnSettingChanged — there is no need to re-fetch SettingsClient.Get manually or restart the character.

searchDocs.title: API​
searchDocs.content: Function	DescriptionDamageNumbers.Show(worldPosition, amount, styleName?)	Spawn a number. No-op if disabled or amount <= 0. styleName defaults to the config default; unknown names fall back to it. DamageNumbers.SetEnabled(value)	Toggle spawning of new numbers (for a settings menu). In-flight numbers finish. DamageNumbers.IsEnabled()	Returns the current toggle state. DamageNumbers.Init()	Build + pre-warm the pool. Idempotent; lazy-runs on first Show otherwise. Called once by DamageNumbersController.

searchDocs.title: Behaviour​
searchDocs.content: Each number is a pooled BillboardGui (GenericPoolInstance). On Show it acquires an entry, applies a named style (color/font/size/stroke), offsets the spawn by a random jitter so rapid hits fan out, then animates withMotionMaster:  Pop — UIScale.Scale from Pop.StartScale to 1 with a back-out overshoot.Rise — BillboardGui.StudsOffsetWorldSpace.Y drifts up by Rise.Heightover the lifetime.Fade — text/stroke transparency goes to 1 during the finalFade.Duration.  When the rise finishes, the entry's Janitor is destroyed and the part returns to the pool. The billboard uses world-space (Scale) sizing, so numbers shrink with camera distance and cull past Billboard.MaxDistance.

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: All tuning is inConfigs/DamageNumberConfig: Styles (named presets — normal, crit,heal out of the box), Pop/Rise/Fade/Lifetime timing, Jitter, Poolsizing, and Billboard size/distance. Add a new look by adding a Stylesentry and passing its name to Show.

searchDocs.title: Out of scope​
searchDocs.content: No combat wiring, Packets, or Signals — a damage source (client predicted or a server damage broadcast) calls Show directly. The settings menu just calls SetEnabled. The toggle is not persisted.

searchDocs.title: Data model​
searchDocs.content: The PlayerCoins profile stores a single value, Coins. STORE_NAME("PlayerCoins") and the UserId key are identical in every place of the universe, so the lobby and gameplay share one DataStore record; ProfileStore session-locking serializes the teleport handoff. All bounds live inConfigs/CoinConfig.luau (STARTING_BALANCE, MAX_BALANCE).

searchDocs.title: API (server-authoritative)​
searchDocs.content: CoinManager (ServerStorage) is the sole authority:  CoinManager.GetCoins(player): number — current balance, 0 if no profile.CoinManager.AddCoins(player, amount, reason?) — award coins; no-op ifamount <= 0 or no profile; clamps to MAX_BALANCE. reason is an optional source tag logged server-side.CoinManager.DeductCoins(player, amount): boolean — atomic spend; returnsfalse with no mutation on amount <= 0, missing profile, or insufficient funds.CoinManager.RefundCoins(player, amount) — return an exact amount of coins (e.g. a perk-unlock refund on respec). Unlike AddCoins, this is notscaled by the Fortune perk's CoinGainBonus — a refund must return exactly what was paid, or unlock→respec cycling could mint coins. No-op onamount <= 0 or missing profile; clamps to MAX_BALANCE.CoinManager.Initialize() — wires the profile lifecycle; called once byCoinSystemLoader in both places.

searchDocs.title: Sources​
searchDocs.content: The first implemented coin source is quest rewards: QuestManager's shared reward path (used by both a manual ReqClaimQuest claim and the rollover auto-grant sweep) calls CoinManager.AddCoins(player, quest.Reward.Coins, "Quest:"..questId) for each completed quest paid out. Like any other earned coins, this is scaled by the Fortune perk's CoinGainBonus (unlikeRefundCoins — see Sinks below). Quests also pay an exp reward viaXPManager.AddXP(player, quest.Reward.Exp), a separate system with its own profile. See Quests system.  The Battle Pass is a second coin source: its bulk-claim sweep calls CoinManager.AddCoins(player, reward.Amount, "BattlePassFree:"..level)for Free-row Coins tiers and "BattlePassPremium:"..level for Premium-row Coins tiers. Like quest rewards, these are earned coins and are scaled by the Fortune perk's CoinGainBonus. The battle pass's Premium row is gated by a Roblox subscription (BattlePassConfig.SUBSCRIPTION_ID, live-checked viaMarketplaceService:GetUserSubscriptionStatusAsync) rather than a one-time purchase — it is the game's premium monetization channel, distinct from the coin economy itself (the subscription unlocks a reward row; it does not grant coins directly).

searchDocs.title: Sinks​
searchDocs.content: The first implemented coin sink is perk unlocking: PerkManager.UnlockPerkcalls CoinManager.DeductCoins(player, perk.UnlockCost) to pay a perk's one-time unlock cost (see Perks — Unlock gate). Respec reverses this — PerkManager.Respec calls CoinManager.RefundCoins(player, perk.UnlockCost) for each perk it re-locks, an exact, un-inflated refund (contrast with AddCoins, which scales by CoinGainBonus) so that unlocking then respeccing repeatedly cannot mint coins.

searchDocs.title: Replication​
searchDocs.content: Every successful mutation fires CoinStateSync (balance: U32) to the owning client. CoinController re-fires it as Signals.OnCoinsChanged(balance) for a future coin HUD. There is no client→server packet — earning and spending are fully server-driven.

searchDocs.title: Out of scope (future work)​
searchDocs.content: Additional earning sources (gameplay-session completion), additional sinks (a shop + purchase packet), and the coin HUD are separate systems that call theCoinManager API; they are not part of the wallet module. Perk unlocking (seeSinks above) is the first implemented sink; daily/weekly quest rewards (see Sources above) are the first implemented source.

searchDocs.title: Flow​
searchDocs.content: Trigger — game:BindToClose (automatic) or DisruptionCoordinator.BeginMaintenance(manual admin command, fanned to every server via MessagingService).Notify — server broadcasts the DisruptionBegan packet; each client shows a non-blocking countdown via NotificationManager.Flush — PersistenceRegistry.FlushAll force-saves every active profile (Coins, Perks, Armor, Settings, XP). profile:Save() is used, notEndSession(), so players stay connected until the teleport.Teleport — TeleportService:TeleportAsync(LOBBY_PLACE_ID, …) with retry.Drain — the coordinator yields until the server empties orMAX_DRAIN_SECONDS; leftover players disconnect with data already saved.

searchDocs.title: Correctness​
searchDocs.content: ProfileStore session-locking is the backstop: even if a save is in flight when a player reaches the lobby server, that server's StartSessionAsync waits for the old lock to release, so no data is lost. The explicit flush just tightens the window and gives a "saved before we move you" ordering.

searchDocs.title: Configuration​
searchDocs.content: All tunables live in DisruptionConfig (LOBBY_PLACE_ID, NOTICE_SECONDS,FLUSH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, MAX_DRAIN_SECONDS, TELEPORT_RETRIES,MESSAGING_TOPIC, ADMIN_USER_IDS, ADMIN_COMMAND, copy fields). SetLOBBY_PLACE_ID to your lobby's PlaceId; while it is 0 the teleport is skipped and players disconnect (data still flushed).

searchDocs.title: Known limitation​
searchDocs.content: Direct teleport to the lobby can bounce if the lobby place is also restarting during a universe-wide Roblox update. The reliable path is the manual maintenance command, which drains the game place while the lobby stays up.

searchDocs.title: Components​
searchDocs.content: DisruptionCoordinator (server) — trigger funnel + drain sequence.PersistenceRegistry (server) — force-save registry; managers register in Initialize.DisruptionController (client) — the on-screen notice.DisruptionConfig — tunables. DisruptionBegan — the broadcast packet.

searchDocs.title: EnemySpawnGroup​
searchDocs.content: A spawn group is a Model in the DataModel tagged with the CollectionService tag EnemySpawnGroup. The group's identity is its GroupName string attribute; if the attribute is absent the model's .Name is used. The tag is all that is required — any Model (a pirate ship, an outpost building, a plain Part wrapped in a Model) becomes a valid group.  Because spawn-point attachments are descendants of the group Model, their .WorldPosition moves automatically with the model's CFrame. Placing the group on a moving ship and then calling SpawnWave will place enemies relative to the ship's current pose at spawn time, with no code changes.

searchDocs.title: EnemySpawnPoint​
searchDocs.content: Each spawn point is an Attachment tagged EnemySpawnPoint, parented anywhere beneath the group model. Two optional per-point attributes control selection and jitter:  Attribute	Type	Default	PurposeRadius	number	archetype DefaultRadius → DEFAULT_POINT_RADIUS	Radial jitter disc radius in studs Weight	number	1	Base selection weight before the cumulative-inverse falloff  Points are visually editable in Studio — add, remove, or move an attachment and the spawner picks it up immediately (the cache is rebuilt on first use per group, and a CollectionService.GetInstanceRemovedSignal listener invalidates the group if the root model is untagged or removed).

searchDocs.title: EnemyAssets folder​
searchDocs.content: Enemy Model assets live in ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/. Each child Model must have:  A Humanoid (authoritative stats are applied at spawn time from the archetype config, but the Humanoid must exist for health/death tracking)A PrimaryPart or HumanoidRootPart (used for pivot placement and SpawnVerification spacing tests)  At module load, EnemySpawnerConfig validates every archetype's Model name against EnemyAssets children and emits a warn for any missing model. Building before art is ready is fully supported: register a placeholder dummy (any Model with a Humanoid) in EnemyAssets under the expected name.

searchDocs.title: Public API​
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawner is a server-only module (ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemySpawner.luau). Call EnemySpawner.Init() once from the system loader before using the rest of the API.  EnemySpawner.Init()   Called once by EnemySpawnerSystemLoader.server.luau at server start. Creates workspace.ActiveEnemies if absent and wires the group-cache invalidation listener.    EnemySpawner.SpawnWave(groupName: string, request: SpawnRequest): WaveHandle   Spawns request.count enemies across the named group's points using the selection algorithm below. composition is either a single archetype name ("PirateGrunt") or a weighted table ({ PirateGrunt = 3, PirateBrute = 1 }) — the weight table is rolled per enemy. If request.interval > 0, spawns are staggered in a task.spawn loop (drip-feed); the WaveHandle is returned immediately and OnCleared waits for both all spawns to be attempted and all registered enemies to die. If request.seed is set, the internal Random is re-seeded for deterministic reproduction.  export type SpawnRequest = { count: number, composition: string | { [string]: number }, interval: number?, -- seconds between spawns; nil/0 = all at once seed: number?, -- optional deterministic RNG seed }     EnemySpawner.SpawnAt(groupName: string, pointName: string, archetypeName: string): Model?   Direct escape hatch: place exactly one archetype at the named attachment (matched by Attachment.Name), still subject to verification. Returns the placed Model or nil if verification fails after MaxRetries or the point/archetype is not found.    EnemySpawner.ResetGroup(groupName: string)   Clears the group's cumulative per-point spawn counts. Call this at the start of each new encounter so point weighting begins fresh. Deaths do not reduce a point's count; only ResetGroup does.

searchDocs.title: Per-enemy spawn algorithm​
searchDocs.content: For each enemy in a wave the spawner runs:  Select a point — weighted random over the group's EnemySpawnPoint attachments. Effective weight is point.Weight / (cumulativeCount + 1) ^ WeightFalloff, where cumulativeCount is the number of enemies spawned from that point this encounter. Points that have spawned fewer enemies this encounter are proportionally more likely; a point with count 0 carries its full base weight. Counts are per-encounter — ResetGroup resets them; enemy deaths do not. Jitter — candidate position = point world position + a uniform random offset within a disc of the point's Radius on the XZ plane. The disc uses sqrt(NextNumber()) * radius so the distribution is uniform over the area rather than biased toward the centre. Verify — the candidate is passed to SpawnVerification with the archetype's body size, an ignore list containing the group model and the ActiveEnemies folder, and the current list of living enemies. Retry-then-skip — steps 2–3 repeat up to Verification.MaxRetries times. If no valid position is found, the enemy is skipped (a warn is emitted) and the wave continues. The wave never hard-fails; it never places a broken enemy. Place — if the global cap (GLOBAL_MAX_ENEMIES) is already met, the enemy is skipped with a warn. Otherwise the archetype Model is cloned from ServerStorage.EnemyAssets, archetype stats are applied (Humanoid.MaxHealth/Health/WalkSpeed), the model is tagged EnemyNPC (or FriendlyNPC if archetype.Faction == "Friendly") so Factions resolves it for CombatService and NpcCollisionService, the model is pivoted to the verified ground-snapped CFrame, parented to workspace.ActiveEnemies, and the point's cumulative count is incremented. The spawned model is registered with the wave handle, and Signals.OnEnemySpawned fires with the placed position and archetype name.

searchDocs.title: SpawnVerification​
searchDocs.content: SpawnVerification (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SpawnVerification.luau) is a stateless pure-geometry validator with no server-only dependencies. It lives in SharedModules so it is independently testable and reusable from a future client-side preview. All v1 callers are server-side.  SpawnVerification.Verify( candidate: Vector3, bodySize: Vector3, ignoreList: { Instance }, livingEnemies: { Model } ): VerifyResult -- { ok: boolean, position: Vector3?, reason: string? }   Checks are run cheapest-first with short-circuit on failure:  Ground below — workspace:Raycast straight down from candidate + (0, 2, 0) up to MaxGroundDrop studs, excluding ignoreList. No hit returns { ok = false, reason = "void" }. On hit, the Y position is snapped to the floor: snapped.Y = hit.Position.Y + bodySize.Y / 2. Clear of walls / headroom — workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox of HeadroomSize centred on the snapped position, excluding ignoreList. Any solid collidable part returns { ok = false, reason = "blocked" }. This catches both embedded-in-wall and under-floor cases. Spacing — if any model in livingEnemies has its pivot within MinEnemySpacing studs of the snapped position, returns { ok = false, reason = "crowded" }.  A successful check returns { ok = true, position = snapped } where position is the ground-snapped placement CFrame origin.

searchDocs.title: WaveHandle lifecycle​
searchDocs.content: SpawnWave returns a WaveHandle backed by a Janitor. The handle tracks every spawned enemy's death and removal.  export type WaveHandle = { OnCleared: Signal<()>, -- fires once: all enemies dead AND wave complete GetAlive: (self) -> number, -- count of enemies still alive GetEnemies: (self) -> { Model }, -- list of enemies still alive Despawn: (self) -> (), -- destroy remaining enemies + remove from tracking Destroy: (self) -> (), -- Despawn + Janitor teardown }   Each spawned enemy's Humanoid.Died and AncestryChanged (for despawn-without-death) are connected via the handle's Janitor. OnCleared fires once when the alive count reaches zero and the wave has been marked complete (all drip-feed spawns attempted). Killing enemies before the last drip-feed slot fires will not trigger OnCleared prematurely.  Typical orchestrator pattern:  local wave = EnemySpawner.SpawnWave("PirateShip", { count = 6, composition = { PirateGrunt = 3, PirateBrute = 1 }, interval = 0.5, }) wave.OnCleared:Connect(function() resumeEncounter() end)   Despawn lets an orchestrator abort a wave early (encounter cancelled, train resumes) and cleanly destroy remaining enemies. Calling Despawn when all enemies are already dead is safe (no-op). Destroy implies Despawn and additionally tears down the Janitor, disconnecting all event connections.

searchDocs.title: Key files​
searchDocs.content: File	Rolesrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EnemySpawnerConfig.luau	Archetype registry, global tuning constants, Verification.* knobs; validates model names against ServerStorage.EnemyAssets at load src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SpawnVerification.luau	Stateless ground/wall/spacing validator; returns a ground-snapped position on success src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemyWave.luau	WaveHandle factory: Janitor-backed enemy tracker, OnCleared signal, Despawn/Destroy src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemySpawner.luau	Server service: group registry, point selection, jitter, placement, SpawnWave/SpawnAt/ResetGroup, drip-feed scheduling, global cap src/ServerScriptService/EnemySpawnerSystemLoader.server.luau	Thin bootstrap: calls EnemySpawner.Init() once per server src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau	Contains OnEnemySpawned signal registration

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: All tuning lives in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EnemySpawnerConfig.luau. The module is accessible from both client and server; the archetype validation block is guarded by RunService:IsServer() since ServerStorage is inaccessible on the client.  Field	Default	EffectGLOBAL_MAX_ENEMIES	40	Hard cap on total active enemies across all groups. Exceeding the cap skips spawns with a warn. Lower temporarily to verify the cap in Studio. DEFAULT_POINT_RADIUS	6	Fallback jitter disc radius (studs) when neither the point Radius attribute nor the archetype DefaultRadius is set. WeightFalloff	1.0	Exponent k in effectiveWeight = baseWeight / (count + 1) ^ k. At 1.0 weight halves each time a point is used. Raise to flatten selection (less adaptive); lower toward 0 to disable cumulative penalisation. Verification.MaxGroundDrop	25	Maximum downward raycast distance (studs) to find a floor below the candidate. Candidates with no solid ground within this distance are rejected as "void". Verification.HeadroomSize	Vector3.new(3, 6, 3)	Box dimensions used for the wall/headroom overlap check centred on the snapped candidate. Should match or slightly exceed the tallest enemy body. Verification.MinEnemySpacing	4	Minimum distance (studs) between a new candidate and any already-living enemy pivot. Candidates closer than this are rejected as "crowded". Verification.MaxRetries	8	Number of jitter re-rolls before an enemy is skipped with a warn. Higher values increase spawn success at the cost of time per enemy. Archetypes	(see below)	Per-archetype table: Model (child name in EnemyAssets), Health, WalkSpeed, DefaultRadius, optional Faction ("Enemy" / "Friendly"; defaults to "Enemy").

searchDocs.title: Archetype example​
searchDocs.content: EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes = { PirateGrunt = { Model = "PirateGrunt", Health = 100, WalkSpeed = 14, DefaultRadius = 6 }, PirateBrute = { Model = "PirateBrute", Health = 300, WalkSpeed = 10, DefaultRadius = 4 }, }   Adding a new archetype: add an entry here, create the corresponding Model in ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/, and the spawner picks it up at next load. No code changes elsewhere are needed.

searchDocs.title: EnemySpawnGroup model​
searchDocs.content: Select any Model in the workspace (pirate ship, outpost, or a plain wrapped Part).Tag it EnemySpawnGroup via the Studio Tag Editor (or CollectionService:AddTag).Optionally set a GroupName string attribute on the model root. If absent, model.Name is used.

searchDocs.title: EnemySpawnPoint attachments​
searchDocs.content: Under the group model, insert one or more Attachment instances:  Insert an Attachment anywhere in the model hierarchy (directly on a Part, inside a nested model, etc.).Tag it EnemySpawnPoint.Optionally add a Radius (number) attribute for this point's jitter disc.Optionally add a Weight (number) attribute to bias selection toward or away from this point.  The attachment's position in Studio is the spawn point's world-space origin at runtime. Move attachments freely; the spawner reads .WorldPosition live at spawn time.

searchDocs.title: EnemyAssets folder​
searchDocs.content: In Studio, create a folder named EnemyAssets inside ServerStorage. Under it, place enemy Models. Each model must have a Humanoid and a PrimaryPart (or HumanoidRootPart). The name of the model must match the Model field in the corresponding archetype entry in EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes.  Minimum viable setup for testing before art is ready:  Insert a default Roblox Dummy (rig_type = R15 or R6) into ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/.Rename it to PirateGrunt.The archetype validation at load will stop warning; SpawnWave will clone the dummy.

searchDocs.title: Collision and combat wiring​
searchDocs.content: No additional Studio wiring is required for collision passthrough or combat. Spawned enemies are tagged EnemyNPC (or FriendlyNPC), and:  NpcCollisionService adds them to the Character collision group so players pass through them.CombatService.ApplyToModel resolves them via Factions so weapon hits deal damage.  Both services detect the tags automatically on CollectionService.GetInstanceAddedSignal.  placeAt also calls EnemyBrain.Register(model, archetypeName) immediately after placement, arming any archetype that has a matching EnemyCombatConfig profile so it paths toward and fires at players. Archetypes with no EnemyCombatConfig profile entry are unaffected — Register no-ops and they remain passive, exactly as before this hook was added. See Enemy Combat for the full director, weapon, and config breakdown.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: WaveHandle OnCleared requires both conditions OnCleared fires only when the alive count is zero AND all drip-feed spawns have been attempted (MarkComplete has been called internally). In an instant wave (interval = 0) this means OnCleared can fire during SpawnWave itself, before it returns, if no enemies are placed (e.g. every enemy was skipped). Always set up OnCleared connections before calling SpawnWave, or use the returned handle and do not assume it is deferred.  Cumulative counts survive across waves; ResetGroup does not EnemySpawner.ResetGroup(groupName) resets the per-point counts for the named group so point selection begins fresh. If you call SpawnWave a second time without resetting, previously-used points start at a cumulative disadvantage. For repeating encounter patterns (waves 1, 2, 3…), decide explicitly whether to reset between waves or let cumulative weighting carry across the full encounter.  GLOBAL_MAX_ENEMIES counts workspace.ActiveEnemies children The cap is the live child count of workspace.ActiveEnemies. If enemies are not parented there (e.g. manually cloned models outside the spawner), they do not count toward the cap, which may allow over-cap situations. Always spawn enemies through EnemySpawner; do not manually parent enemy models into ActiveEnemies.  SpawnVerification is in SharedModules but is server-only in v1 SpawnVerification is in ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ so it has no server-only dependencies and can be used from a future client-side preview (e.g. displaying valid spawn zones in a director tool). In v1, all calls happen server-side via EnemySpawner. Do not call it on the client in production without auditing the ignoreList and livingEnemies arguments for client-visible data.  Archetype validation warns but does not error If a model is missing from EnemyAssets at load time, EnemySpawnerConfig emits a warn but does not error. The spawner itself will also warn (and skip the enemy) at spawn time if the model is still absent. Register placeholder models early to keep the Output clean during development.

searchDocs.title: Future directions​
searchDocs.content: Off-screen spawn preference — an additional weighting term in step 1 of the selection algorithm that demotes EnemySpawnPoints currently inside any player's camera frustum. Enemies would appear from behind cover or at the edge of vision. The term slots into the effective-weight formula without changing the rest of the algorithm.Reachability pre-check — PathfindingService:CreatePath from the verified candidate position to the nearest player, rejecting candidates in sealed-off areas. This is the deferred line-of-sight check in SpawnVerification, done properly. Build alongside the enemy pathfinding AI system.Encounter director — a layer above the spawner that scales count/composition/interval by wave number, player count, or Tech Tree progress. The spawner stays a dumb placement service; the director owns escalation and pacing. Lives as a separate module; EnemySpawner requires no changes.

searchDocs.title: The EnemyBrain director​
searchDocs.content: EnemyBrain (ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemyBrain.luau) is a single module-level loop, not one script per enemy. EnemyBrain.Init() connects one RunService.Heartbeatlistener and accumulates dt until TICK_INTERVAL (1 / TICK_HZ, TICK_HZ = 10) has elapsed, then calls tick() once. Every registered enemy is iterated in that single tick — there are no per-enemy RunService connections, task.spawn loops, orwhile true do task.wait() end patterns. This keeps the cost of N enemies roughly linear and avoids N independent scheduler entries.  Each registered enemy is a Record (an in-memory table, not an Instance) keyed by itsModel in a module-level records dictionary:  type Record = { model: Model, humanoid: Humanoid, root: BasePart, profile: Profile, -- EnemyCombatConfig.Profile cleaner: Janitor.Janitor, target: Player?, -- movement waypoints: { PathWaypoint }, waypointIndex: number, pathGoal: Vector3?, nextRepathAt: number, -- firing fireState: "Idle" | "Bursting" | "Cooldown", shotsLeft: number, nextShotAt: number, nextBurstAt: number, telegraphUntil: number?, }   Every tick, for every record that is still alive and rooted, EnemyBrain:  Reacquires a target if the current one is missing or dead — nearestPlayerscans Players:GetPlayers() for the closest player with a living Humanoid and aHumanoidRootPart. Targeting is pure distance; there is no aggro persistence, threat table, or line-of-sight requirement to pick a target (LOS only gatesfiring, see below).Steps movement (stepMovement) — independent of firing.Steps firing (stepFiring) — independent of movement.  This is the two-concern (move ‖ fire) model: an enemy can be walking toward the player and shooting at the same time (run-and-gun), because neither step blocks or depends on the other completing first within the tick.

searchDocs.title: Movement and path-compute budgeting​
searchDocs.content: stepMovement holds the enemy still (Humanoid:MoveTo(currentPosition)) once it is within profile.CloseDistance (default 30) of the target — this is the "comfort band": ranged enemies stop closing once they're inside a distance they consider safe to shoot from, rather than walking into melee range. Outside that band, it paths toward the target's HumanoidRootPart position.  Paths are computed via PathfindingService:CreatePath / ComputeAsync, but noton every tick for every enemy. A shared pathBudget of PATH_BUDGET_PER_TICK (1)ComputeAsync calls is allocated per tick and decremented as enemies consume it — with a 10 Hz tick this caps fresh pathfinding compute at ~10 calls/sec total acrossall enemies, naturally staggering large waves instead of bursting 40 simultaneousComputeAsync calls in one frame. An enemy only requests a new path when it has none yet, REPATH_INTERVAL (1.0s) has elapsed since its last compute, or the target has drifted more than REPATH_THRESHOLD (8 studs) from the path's original goal — so most ticks for most enemies do no path computation at all, they just step along existing waypoints (WAYPOINT_REACHED = 3 studs advances to the next one). IfComputeAsync fails or the budget is exhausted, the enemy falls back to beelining straight at the goal with Humanoid:MoveTo — pathfinding failure is non-fatal, it just degrades to dumb-walk.

searchDocs.title: Melee firing​
searchDocs.content: stepFiringMelee is a simple range-gated, single-swing cooldown: if the target is within profile.Range (default 8 studs), call EnemyWeapon.MeleeSwing and roll a fresh cooldown (rollCooldown, uniform between AttackCooldownMin/Max). There is no melee combo system for enemies (unlike the player's ClassicSword combo inWeapons) — every swing is identical.

searchDocs.title: Ranged firing: the burst/cooldown state machine​
searchDocs.content: stepFiringRanged drives a three-state machine per enemy: "Idle" → "Bursting" →"Cooldown" → back to "Idle".  No target, out of range, or no line of sight: firing is suspended and movement keeps closing/repositioning. Critically, if the enemy was mid-burst ("Bursting") when any of these interruptions occurs, its state is reset to "Idle" rather than left to resume later: if rec.fireState == "Bursting" then rec.fireState = "Idle" end This reset exists specifically so that re-engagement always rolls a brand-new burst (startBurst) instead of resuming a stale partial burst whosenextShotAt/shotsLeft may be long expired or, for a sniper, whose Telegraphwindow has already elapsed. Without the reset, a player could duck behind cover for a moment to skip past a sniper's aim-telegraph and pop back out already inside the weapon's nextShotAt window — defeating the reaction-window fairness the telegraph exists to provide. The fix applies identically to the out-of-range case (LOS-break and range-break share the same reasoning) so the dodge counter-play stays consistent regardless of why the enemy lost its shot. "Cooldown": holds fire until now >= nextBurstAt, then transitions to"Idle". "Idle": immediately calls startBurst, which rolls shotsLeft betweenBurstMin/BurstMax, sets fireState = "Bursting", and sets nextShotAt = now + Telegraph (0 for non-snipers). For a sniper (Telegraph > 0), this delay before the first shot is the player's reaction window — telegraphUntil is exposed on the record so a future client-side "enemy is aiming at you" cue could read it, though nothing currently renders it. "Bursting": once now >= nextShotAt and shotsLeft > 0, fires one shot (fireOneShot — routes to EnemyWeapon.Lob or EnemyWeapon.FireProjectiledepending on profile.FireMode), decrements shotsLeft, and schedules the next shot at now + ShotInterval. When shotsLeft reaches 0, transitions to"Cooldown" and rolls the next burst's start time.  Line of sight is checked every tick a ranged enemy considers firing (hasLineOfSight): a raycast from the muzzle origin to the target's root, excluding the shooter's own model, treats a hit against the target's own character as clear (not blocked) and anything else solid as blocked. This stops enemies shooting through walls; it is a fairness check, not a cover-seeking AI — enemies make no attempt to flank around an obstruction, they simply hold fire and let stepMovement keep closing the distance.

searchDocs.title: Fairness rationale (why ranged fire feels dodgeable)​
searchDocs.content: No ammo, ever. Enemies have no magazine or reload — the only throttle on rate of fire is the burst/cooldown rhythm in EnemyCombatConfig. This is a deliberate simplification versus the player's ammo system (Weapons); the challenge lever is burst size and cooldown length, not resource starvation.No hitscan. EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile always launches a travelling FastCast2 projectile at a finite ProjectileSpeed; damage applies on Hit after real flight time elapses, so a player who strafes out of the bullet's path after it's fired takes no damage, exactly like dodging a player-fired bullet.No target leading. Both FireProjectile and Lob aim at the target'scurrent position (targetPos) at the moment of firing, never a predicted future position. Combined with finite projectile speed and Spread (an aim-error cone in degrees, via WeaponValidation.applySpread), this makes every ranged archetype dodgeable by lateral movement, not just by breaking LOS.Sniper telegraph as a reaction window. PirateSniper's Telegraph = 0.6inserts a fixed delay between entering "Bursting" and the first (and only) shot, giving the player six-tenths of a second of visible aim-up before the highest single-hit damage in the game (Damage = 40) fires. The reset-on-interrupt fix above (see the burst/cooldown state machine) ensures this window cannot be bypassed by ducking LOS or range right before the shot and popping back — the telegraph always re-applies on re-engagement.

searchDocs.title: EnemyWeapon​
searchDocs.content: EnemyWeapon (ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnemyWeapon.luau) is the enemy attackaction — it owns no timing or ammo state (that's EnemyBrain's job) and instead reuses the exact same player damage layer end to end:  EnemyWeapon.MuzzleOrigin(model, profile) — returns the world position fire should originate from. If the rig has a descendant Attachment named "Muzzle"(an authored weapon model), its WorldPosition is used. Otherwise it falls back to the root part's CFrame offset by profile.MuzzleOffset (default (0, 1.5, -1)) — an art-less first pass that still produces a sensible shoulder-height, slightly forward origin.EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile(model, profile, origin, targetPos) — fires one travelling bullet through a dedicated module-level FastCast2.new() caster (bulletCaster, separate from the player gun caster in WeaponServer, but wired the same way: LengthChanged steps an optional cosmetic part, Hit resolves the struck model via WeaponValidation.resolveHumanoidModel and applies damage viaCombatService.ApplyToModel(model, humanoid, damage, "Bullet", enemyModel)). FiresPackets.WeaponFired on both a real hit and a miss-timeout backstop (task.delayguarded by a data.fired flag so a real hit and the timeout can never both resolve), so the tracer always renders even when nothing is struck. The optional cosmetic bullet comes from ServerProjectile.spawnRocket(profile.Weapon, ...) — nil-safe; if no WeaponAssets/<Weapon> template exists, fire still works, just without a visible bullet model.EnemyWeapon.Lob(model, profile, origin, targetPos) — reuses the player grenade path: ServerProjectile.spawnThrowable(weapon, origin, unit, speed, "Bounce", { model }) for a server-replicated physics throw, biased upward (+ Vector3.yAxis * 0.5) so it arcs rather than fires flat. Afterprofile.FuseTime, detonates via CombatService.ApplyAOE and firesPackets.ExplosionAt, then destroys the charge instance.EnemyWeapon.MeleeSwing(model, profile) — one swing from the rig's current root CFrame, reusing WeaponValidation.queryMeleeTargets (the same box-overlap query the player melee handler uses) over profile.Range/HitboxSize, applying damage via CombatService.ApplyToModel(..., "Melee", enemyModel) to every struck target and firing Packets.WeaponImpact on a landed hit.  In every case the attacker argument passed to CombatService is the enemy Model, not a Player — CombatService/Factions already supports a non-Player attacker (the Faction of a Model is resolved by its EnemyNPC/FriendlyNPCCollectionService tag), so no changes were needed to the damage router itself to support enemies attacking players. Factions.canDamage("Enemy", "Player") is trueby default; the reverse and same-faction pairs are not, which is what prevents enemies from ever damaging each other or friendly NPCs by the same mechanism that prevents player-on-player damage. See Weapons → CombatService andArchitecture → Backbone for the faction model itself.

searchDocs.title: EnemyCombatConfig profiles​
searchDocs.content: EnemyCombatConfig (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EnemyCombatConfig.luau) holds one Profile per archetype name, keyed identically to the archetype names used in EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes. An archetype with no entry here stays passive — EnemyBrain.Register looks upEnemyCombatConfig.GetProfile(archetypeName) and simply returns without arming the enemy if it's nil. This is the only "is this archetype armed" check in the system — see Studio setup below for the common mistake this invites.  export type Class = "Ranged" | "Melee" export type FireMode = "Projectile" | "Lob" export type Profile = { Class: Class, Weapon: string, -- FX/sound key (WeaponFx) + WeaponAssets cosmetic name Damage: number, -- Ranged-only FireMode: FireMode?, -- "Projectile" | "Lob"; nil for melee ProjectileSpeed: number?, -- studs/s; finite + dodgeable Spread: number?, -- aim-error cone (degrees) Range: number?, -- max distance the enemy will fire from CloseDistance: number?, -- pathfind until generously inside Range, then hold MuzzleOffset: Vector3?, -- HRP-relative origin until a "Muzzle" attachment exists -- Burst rhythm (no ammo) ShotInterval: number?, BurstMin: number?, BurstMax: number?, BurstCooldownMin: number?, BurstCooldownMax: number?, Telegraph: number?, -- sniper: seconds aiming before the shot -- Lob-only AOERadius: number?, FuseTime: number?, -- Melee-only HitboxSize: Vector3?, AttackCooldownMin: number?, AttackCooldownMax: number?, -- Optional animation asset ids (server rig) FireAnimId: string?, SwingAnimId: string?, }   EnemyCombatConfig.FindByWeapon(weaponName) linear-scans Profiles for a matchingWeapon key — used by WeaponFxto resolve enemy weapon FX by name, the mirror of how it resolves player weapons viaWeaponConfig.

searchDocs.title: Shipped archetypes​
searchDocs.content: Archetype	Class	Weapon (FX key)	Damage	Fire mode	Projectile speed	Spread	Range / Close	Burst (shots)	Shot interval	Cooldown	TelegraphPirateGruntSMG	Ranged	EnemySMG	6	Projectile	140	5°	80 / 35	2–5	0.10s	1.2–2.5s	— PiratePistoleer	Ranged	EnemyPistol	8	Projectile	150	3°	60 / 30	3–5	0.18s	1.5–3.0s	— PirateSniper	Ranged	EnemySniper	40	Projectile	320	1°	200 / 120	1–1	0s	3.0–4.5s	0.6s PirateGrenadier	Ranged	EnemyGrenade	50 (AOE r16)	Lob	60	—	90 / 50	1–1	—	3.5–5.0s	— PirateBrute	Melee	EnemyCleaver	18	—	—	—	8 (swing reach)	—	—	1.0–1.6s	—  PirateGrenadier's FuseTime is 2.0s; MuzzleOffset for all ranged archetypes is(0, 1.5, -1) except PirateGrenadier's (0, 2, -1). These archetype names are combat profiles only — they still need a corresponding entry inEnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes to ever be spawned in the first place (seeStudio setup).

searchDocs.title: WeaponFx bridge and the widened WeaponFired packet​
searchDocs.content: Player weapon FX (impact/explosion sounds) are looked up by weapon name inWeaponConfig. Enemy weapons are a different name (EnemySMG, not SMG) living in a different config module, so a single client FX controller needs a single resolver that checks both. WeaponFx.resolve(weaponName) (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/WeaponFx.luau) checks WeaponConfig[weaponName] first, then falls back toEnemyCombatConfig.FindByWeapon(weaponName), returning { ImpactSound?, ExplodeSound? } either way (or an empty table if neither matches). WeaponEffectsController.client.luaucalls this for WeaponFired/WeaponImpact/ExplosionAt instead of indexingWeaponConfig directly — this is the only client-side change needed to render enemy weapon FX through the existing tracer/spark/explosion rendering code.  This works because the WeaponFired packet's shooter field was widened fromPlayer to Instance so it can carry either a Player (player guns) or an enemyModel (EnemyWeapon fire):  local WeaponFired = Packet( "WeaponFired", Packet.Instance :: Instance, -- shooter (Player or enemy Model) Packet.String, -- weaponName Packet.Vector3F32, -- origin (muzzle) Packet.Vector3F32, -- endpoint (hit position or max-range point) Packet.Boolean8 -- isHit )   WeaponEffectsController ignores WeaponFired only when shooter == player (the local player's own gun already drew its own tracer client-side); an enemy Modelshooter is never equal to a Player instance, so enemy shots always render for every client, including the player they're aimed at. See the WeaponFired row in theNetworking Map for the full packet contract — it was already updated for this widening and does not need further changes here.

searchDocs.title: Lifecycle and cleanup​
searchDocs.content: EnemyBrain.Register(model, archetypeName) is idempotent (returns immediately if the model is already registered) and requires the model to have both a Humanoid (viaFindFirstChildOfClass) and a root part (PrimaryPart or HumanoidRootPart) — if either is missing, registration silently no-ops and the enemy stays unarmed (the movement/melee/ranged loop never runs for it). On success, one Janitor is created per record (cleaner) and two connections are added to it, both tagged"Disconnect":  humanoid.Died → EnemyBrain.Unregister(model)model.AncestryChanged (fires when parent becomes nil) → EnemyBrain.Unregister(model)  EnemyBrain.Unregister(model) removes the record from the module-level recordstable and calls cleaner:Destroy(). This covers both lifecycle exits an enemy can take: dying (Humanoid.Died) and being despawned without dying (wave Despawn/Destroy, or any other code that removes the model from the DataModel — seeEnemySpawner → WaveHandle lifecycle). There is no Destroy/Cleanup distinction here (unlike some other Janitor-owning modules in this codebase) because an unregistered enemy record has no further use — the Janitor is always fully torn down.  Within tick() itself, a record whose root.Parent is falsy or whosehumanoid.Health <= 0 is skipped for that tick (continue) rather than acted on — the actual removal from records happens asynchronously via the Died/AncestryChanged connections above, so there's a brief window (within the same frame) where a dead enemy's record can still exist but is simply not ticked.

searchDocs.title: Edge cases​
searchDocs.content: Case	BehaviorNo target found (no living, rooted player)	stepMovement halts the enemy in place (MoveTo(currentPosition)); stepFiringRanged resets fireState to "Idle" so the next valid target starts a fresh burst. Target dies or leaves mid-burst	Next tick's targetRoot lookup fails, rec.target is re-acquired via nearestPlayer (or left nil if no one is left), and a stale "Bursting" state is abandoned the same way as the out-of-range/LOS-blocked cases. Target goes out of Range mid-burst	Firing is suspended; a "Bursting" state resets to "Idle" (see the telegraph-reset fix); movement keeps closing. Line of sight blocked mid-burst	Same reset-to-"Idle" behavior as out-of-range; the enemy holds fire and lets movement reposition rather than trying to flank. Friendly fire (enemy vs. enemy, enemy vs. friendly NPC)	Physically impossible by design — CombatService.ApplyToModel gates every hit through Factions.canDamage, and Enemy -> Enemy / Enemy -> Friendly are not in the allow table. An enemy's projectile or melee swing that strikes another enemy or a friendly NPC deals no damage. Wave despawn while enemies are armed	EnemyWave's Despawn/Destroy removes the enemy Model from the DataModel, which fires model.AncestryChanged with a nil parent, which calls EnemyBrain.Unregister — the brain record and its Janitor are torn down in the same tick the model is destroyed, with no dangling references. Archetype has no EnemyCombatConfig profile	EnemyBrain.Register returns early; the enemy spawns and is fully visible/collidable but never moves toward or fires at players (it is exactly as passive as before this feature existed). Enemy model missing Humanoid or root part	EnemyBrain.Register returns early without warning (mirrors EnemySpawner's existing tolerance for placeholder/incomplete rigs during early development).

searchDocs.title: EnemyAssets rig requirements​
searchDocs.content: An enemy Model in ServerStorage/EnemyAssets/ needs the same minimum viable rig thatEnemySpawner already requires for spawning at all: a Humanoid and a PrimaryPart or HumanoidRootPart. EnemyBrain.Registerre-checks both of these independently and silently skips arming the enemy if either is missing — so a rig that spawns fine but never moves or fires is almost always missing one of these two parts.

searchDocs.title: Optional Muzzle attachment​
searchDocs.content: For a visually accurate origin, add an Attachment named exactly Muzzle anywhere in the rig's descendant hierarchy (typically welded to a held weapon model's barrel tip). EnemyWeapon.MuzzleOrigin finds it via model:FindFirstChild("Muzzle", true)(a recursive search) and fires from its WorldPosition. Without one, fire still works — it falls back to the root part's CFrame offset by the profile'sMuzzleOffset (roughly shoulder height, slightly forward), which is a perfectly playable art-less placeholder. Add the attachment (and a welded weapon model, and optional FireAnimId/SwingAnimId) whenever art is ready; no code changes are needed either way.

searchDocs.title: Arming an archetype: the two-registry relationship​
searchDocs.content: This is the most common setup mistake, so it's worth stating explicitly: an archetype needs entries in BOTH registries to be a functioning armed enemy.  EnemySpawnerConfig.Archetypes[name] — required for the archetype to spawn at all (Model name, Health, WalkSpeed, DefaultRadius, optional Faction). SeeEnemy Spawner → Archetype example.EnemyCombatConfig.Profiles[name] — required for the spawned enemy to be armed (move toward and fire at players). Keyed by the same archetype name as above.  An archetype with only #1 spawns, walks nowhere on its own, and never fires — useful for cosmetic/decorative NPCs or placeholder testing before combat tuning is ready. An archetype with only #2 (a profile with no matching spawner entry) is simply dead config — EnemySpawner.placeAt is the only call site for EnemyBrain.Register, so a profile with no way to spawn the archetype never gets used. There is no validation or warning today if these two registries drift out of sync (e.g. renaming an archetype in one but not the other) — check both tables by hand when adding or renaming an archetype.

searchDocs.title: Verifying combat in Studio​
searchDocs.content: No additional Studio-side wiring is required beyond the two config entries above and the rig requirements — EnemyBrain.Init() is called once automatically byEnemyCombatSystemLoader.server.luau at server start, the same pattern asEnemySpawnerSystemLoader.server.luau calling EnemySpawner.Init(). Spawn a wave with an archetype that has both registry entries and the enemy should path toward the nearest player and open fire once in range.  Telegraph and burst values are tuned by feel, not measured ProjectileSpeed, Spread, Telegraph, and the burst/cooldown ranges directly control how dodgeable and how punishing each archetype is. There is no automated test for "is this fair" — these are Studio-playtest-and-adjust knobs, the same asPATH_BUDGET_PER_TICK/REPATH_INTERVAL/REPATH_THRESHOLD/TICK_HZ at the top ofEnemyBrain.luau. Adjust archetype values in EnemyCombatConfig directly; avoid touching EnemyBrain's tick/path constants unless movement itself feels laggy or pathfinding spikes with large waves.  Cosmetic bullet/throwable templates are optional, not required EnemyWeapon.FireProjectile's cosmetic bullet (ServerProjectile.spawnRocket) andEnemyWeapon.Lob's throwable charge (ServerProjectile.spawnThrowable) both look up a template by profile.Weapon in ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets. If the named template doesn't exist yet, both functions are nil-safe — the shot/lob still fires, damages, and broadcasts its FX packet; it just has no visible travelling model. AddWeaponAssets/EnemySMG (etc.) whenever art is ready; this is a drop-in, no code change.  Re-engagement always restarts the burst from scratch By design (see the telegraph-reset fix), an enemy that loses LOS or range mid-burst does not "remember" how many shots it had left — it goes back to "Idle" and rolls an entirely new BurstMin–BurstMax count next time it can see and reach the target. This is intentional fairness behavior, not a bug: do not "fix" it by trying to persist shotsLeft/nextShotAt across an interruption, as that would let a player skip past a sniper's telegraph window by breaking LOS for a single frame.
