searchDocs.title: Channel model​
searchDocs.content: Channels run fully independently, each with its own roll table, cadence, and state. Two channels exist today:  Encounter — PirateAttack and Outpost share this channel and are mutually exclusive (only one can be active at a time on Encounter).Ambient — BiomeChange runs on its own channel, so it can roll and activate while an Encounter event is in progress.  Each channel is a state machine: Idle → Active → Cooldown → Idle.  Idle — every time the odometer crosses a RollInterval boundary, the channel rolls its weighted table once. If the roll picks a real event, the channel goes Active. Idle processes every roll boundary crossed since the last tick (so a long pause/lag spike doesn't skip rolls).Active — the chosen handler's Start(ctx, finish) is running. A MaxActiveDistance watchdog (if > 0) force-finishes a handler that never calls finish(). Other channels keep rolling independently while this one is Active.Cooldown — after finish(), the channel stays quiet until PostEventDelay odometer studs have passed, then returns to Idle with lastRollAt reset to the current odometer (so the next roll is a full RollInterval away, not immediately).

searchDocs.title: The virtual odometer​
searchDocs.content: The train has no physical speed/odometer value of its own — TrainFuelManager only tracks Running/Braked/Stalled state. EventOrchestrator owns its own distance counter instead:  A task.spawn loop ticks every EventConfig.TickInterval seconds (0.25s by default — ample precision for event cadence and cheaper than a per-frame Heartbeat).While running is true, it accumulates EventConfig.CruiseSpeed * dt into the odometer and then ticks every channel.running is driven by Signals.SetTrainState (fired by TrainFuelManager on every brake/stall flip). Accumulation pauses on brake, stall, and the pre-game freeze — nothing rolls until the train is actually moving.Signals.SetTrainStarted firing true (first un-brake of a round) calls EventOrchestrator.Reset(), zeroing the odometer and returning every channel to Idle — including force-finishing any handler that's currently Active via its finish().

searchDocs.title: Weighted roll + pity​
searchDocs.content: Each channel's Table is a list of RollEntrys — either a real event ({ Event = "PirateAttack", Weight = 50 }) or the no-op entry ({ Nothing = true, Weight = 20 }). On each roll:  Build the eligible candidate set: real entries are excluded if their handler's optional CanTrigger(ctx) returns false (or if no handler is registered for that Id); the Nothing entry is excluded outright when pity is forcing a real event.Pick one candidate by weight (Random:NextNumber(0, total) against cumulative weight).If the pick is Nothing (or nothing was eligible), the channel's emptyRollStreak increments and it stays Idle.If the pick is a real event, emptyRollStreak resets to 0 and the channel activates that event's handler.  Pity: once emptyRollStreak >= PityRolls, the next roll excludes the Nothing entry, forcing a real event to fire. This bounds the maximum distance a channel can go without a real event to roughly (PityRolls + 1) * RollInterval studs.

searchDocs.title: EventHandler interface​
searchDocs.content: export type EventContext = { odometer: number, -- current odometer value at roll/activation time rng: Random, -- orchestrator-owned Random instance channel: string, -- the channel name this activation belongs to janitor: Janitor.Janitor, -- per-activation Janitor; destroyed automatically on finish() } export type EventHandler = { Id: string, -- unique; must match an EventConfig table entry Channel: string, -- which channel this handler is registered under CanTrigger: ((ctx: EventContext) -> boolean)?, -- optional eligibility guard, checked at roll time Start: (ctx: EventContext, finish: () -> ()) -> (), -- begin the event; call finish() exactly once when done }   Handlers register via EventOrchestrator.RegisterHandler(handler). A duplicate Id is ignored with a warn.Start is called inside a pcall; a throwing handler is logged and the channel is force-finished into Cooldown so one bad event can't wedge the channel.finish is guarded by a per-activation nonce — late or duplicate calls (e.g. a watchdog firing after the handler already finished normally) are no-ops.ctx.janitor is destroyed automatically the moment finish() resolves, so handlers should hang any connections/instances/cleanup off it rather than tearing down manually.A load-time validation pass (validate() in EventOrchestrator.Init) warns if a config table references an Id with no registered handler, or a handler's Channel doesn't match the channel it's listed under (or targets an unknown channel entirely). These are warnings, not hard errors — matches the EnemySpawnerConfig missing-model convention.

searchDocs.title: EventConfig knobs​
searchDocs.content: All tuning lives in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/EventConfig.luau.  Field	Scope	EffectCruiseSpeed	global	Virtual odometer rate in studs/sec, accumulated only while the train is running. TickInterval	global	Seconds between odometer-loop ticks (task.wait cadence). Weight	per roll-table entry	Relative chance this entry (event or Nothing) is picked on a roll. RollInterval	per channel	Odometer studs between roll attempts on this channel. PostEventDelay	per channel	Quiet studs after an event's finish() before the channel resumes rolling. PityRolls	per channel	Number of consecutive empty rolls before the Nothing entry is excluded, forcing a real event. StartGrace	per channel	Odometer offset before the channel's first roll (keeps players from being ambushed the instant the train starts moving). MaxActiveDistance	per channel	Watchdog: if an Active handler hasn't called finish() within this many odometer studs, the orchestrator force-finishes it with a warn. 0 disables the watchdog.  Current channel values (Encounter vs. Ambient) and the per-event parameter tables (EventConfig.Events.PirateAttack / .Outpost / .BiomeChange) live directly in the config module — see it for exact numbers, since those are expected to be tuned independently of this page.

searchDocs.title: Signals​
searchDocs.content: EventOrchestrator fires two signals from the Signals bus (see the signals map):  Signals.OnGameEventStarted(eventId: string) — fired right before the handler's Start is invoked.Signals.OnGameEventEnded(eventId: string) — fired inside finish(), after the activation's Janitor has been destroyed.  Neither has a consumer yet; both are reserved for a future music/analytics hook to react to event lifecycle without coupling to the orchestrator.

searchDocs.title: Public API​
searchDocs.content: EventOrchestrator.RegisterHandler(handler: EventHandler)   Registers a handler module. Call before Init() (from the system loader).  EventOrchestrator.Init()   Builds channel state from EventConfig.Channels, runs the validation pass, subscribes to Signals.SetTrainState / Signals.SetTrainStarted, and starts the odometer loop. Idempotent — a second call warns and is ignored.  EventOrchestrator.Reset()   Zeroes the odometer, force-finishes any Active channel (via its handler's finish), and returns every channel to Idle with lastRollAt reseeded from StartGrace. Called automatically on Signals.SetTrainStarted(true).  EventOrchestrator.GetState()   Returns a snapshot (odometer, running, per-channel phase/lastRollAt/emptyRollStreak/activeId/cooldownUntil) for debugging/inspection.

searchDocs.title: The three event handlers (stubs)​
searchDocs.content: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/Events/ holds one module per event, each implementing EventHandler. All three are intentionally thin — their full behavior is deferred to later, per-event specs:  PirateAttackEvent (Channel = "Encounter") — calls EnemySpawner.SpawnWave with the group/wave composition from EventConfig.Events.PirateAttack, hangs the returned WaveHandle off ctx.janitor (so a force-finish despawns survivors), and calls finish when WaveHandle.OnCleared fires. This is the one handler with "real" wiring; wave difficulty/rewards are a later spec.OutpostEvent (Channel = "Encounter") — picks a side via ctx.rng, sets a workspace attribute (ActiveOutpostSide), and calls finish after a fixed distance window (approximated as time at CruiseSpeed, since the odometer isn't directly accessible inside a handler). Approach telegraph, stop-by prompt, and outpost contents are a later spec.BiomeChangeEvent (Channel = "Ambient") — picks a different biome than the current one and sets a workspace attribute (CurrentBiome); the event finishes immediately since the biome persists until the next swap. Client-side skybox/music/VFX reacting to the attribute is a later spec.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Reset force-finishes Active handlers, not Cooldown EventOrchestrator.Reset() only calls activeFinish() for a channel currently in the Active phase. A channel in Cooldown is simply snapped back to Idle — there's no handler running to finish. This matters if a round resets mid-cooldown: the cooldown window is discarded rather than honored.  OutpostEvent's window is time-based, not distance-based Because a handler doesn't have direct access to the live odometer tick, OutpostEvent approximates its Window (studs) as Window / EventConfig.CruiseSpeed seconds and uses task.delay. If the train brakes or stalls during the window, the outpost will still end on the original wall-clock timer rather than pausing with the odometer. This is called out as a stub limitation in the handler's own doc comment.  Channels are independent; "Encounter" exclusivity is per-channel, not global PirateAttack and Outpost cannot overlap because they share the Encounter channel. But BiomeChange on Ambient can roll and activate at any time, including while an Encounter event is Active. If a future event needs true global exclusivity across channels, that's not modeled here and would need an explicit cross-channel guard (e.g. a CanTrigger that inspects another channel's state).

searchDocs.title: Future directions​
searchDocs.content: See the design spec's "Out of scope" section: full Pirate-attack behavior (wave composition/difficulty/rewards), full Outpost behavior (approach telegraph, stop-by prompt, contents, departure), full Biome-change behavior (client skybox/music/VFX, biome registry, transitions), any client HUD/banner, and persistence of event history across sessions.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Player equips GrabHook tool • mouse.TargetFilter = PlacedObjects folder (so placed items don't occlude aim) • Signals.RequestShootingCamera:Fire(true) ──► CameraController enters aim mode RenderStepped (every frame while equipped) • GetAimedJunk(): Spherecast from handle attachment toward mouse.Hit - radius = Physics.HitboxRadius (2 studs) - max distance = Physics.MaxDistance (150 studs) - angle gate: must be within 90° of character forward vector • if junk found → ShowForceField(junkPart, junkId) [highlight effect] • if aim lost for > 0.08 s grace → HideForceField Player clicks (tool.Activated) • cooldown check (Physics.Cooldown = 1.1 s) • Signals.TryClaimJunk:Fire(id, hitPoint) ──────────────────────────► JunkController → Packets.ReqJunkClaim → JunkService (server) ← BeginJunkRetract (broadcast) • FireGrappleAndAttach(targetPart, hitPoint, junkId, token): 1. Instance.new("Attachment") on junk part ("HookAttachment") 2. GrabHookVisuals.CreateBeam(handleAtt, junkAtt, targetPart) 3. GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile → three-phase animation: FLIGHT: junkAtt.WorldPosition lerps toward junk at Physics.Speed (200 studs/s) beam curves oscillate (Amplitude=12, Frequency=40, Decay=4) LATCH: single transition frame, curves flattened to 0 RETRACT: targetPart.Position lerps back to handle at Physics.RetractSpeed (50 studs/s) 4. on retract complete → Signals.TryFinalizeJunk:Fire(id) ─────────► JunkController → Packets.ReqJunkFinalize → JunkService ← JunkCollected (broadcast) • SoundManager.PlaySFXAt("GrabHookFire") — replicated to all clients • SoundManager.PlayLooped("GrabHookLoop") with fade-in/out scheduling Player unequips tool • fireToken incremented (invalidates all pending task.delay callbacks) • loopHandle:Destroy() • Signals.RequestShootingCamera:Fire(false) ──► CameraController exits aim mode

searchDocs.title: Net Cast perk (multi-catch)​
searchDocs.content: The NetCast perk (see Perks) raises hook capacity beyond 1. netCapacity() reads PerkBuffs/<UserId>.NetCapacityBonus client-side: capacity = 1 + NetCapacityBonus. At capacity 1 (no perk levels) the tool is byte-for-byte identical to the base single-hook path (GetAimedJunk + Signals.TryClaimJunk). At capacity ≥ 2:  Aim — GetAimedJunks(rootPart, capacity) replaces the single spherecast with workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox at GrabHookConfig.Physics.NetHitboxRadius (4 studs) along the aim line, returning up to capacity NetTargets ({ id, part, hitPos }) sorted by distance.Fire — one tool.Activated still means one cooldown, one GrabHookFire sound, and one loop sound, but drives a beam per target. Claim ids are batched through Signals.TryClaimJunkBatch:Fire(ids) (consumed by JunkController, which invokes Packets.ReqJunkClaimBatch) instead of the per-junk TryClaimJunk. Finalize remains per-junk (Signals.TryFinalizeJunk / ReqJunkFinalize) once each beam's retraction completes.Server clamp — JunkService.ClaimJunkBatchForPlayer never trusts the client's capacity or positions: it re-reads NetCapacityBonus from the published buff folder, clamps to GrabHookConfig.Physics.NetMaxTargets (5, hard cap), and reconstructs each junk's position from the junk odometer (SpawnPos + MOVE_DIRECTION * (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer)) before reserving it.Reticle — on equip, if netCapacity() >= 2, fires Signals.RequestReticleScale(CameraConfig.NetReticleScale) (1.6×) so CameraController enlarges the aim reticle; otherwise fires RequestReticleScale(1). Unequip always fires RequestReticleScale(1) unconditionally, so the reticle never gets stuck enlarged.Highlighting — the force-field highlight loop shows one force field per currently-aimed NetTarget instead of a single one when capacity ≥ 2.

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (GrabHook.client.luau)  Runs entirely as a LocalScript inside the Grabhook Tool under StarterPack.GetAimedJunk(rootPart) performs a Spherecast from the handle's Attachment.WorldPosition toward mouse.Hit.Position. Junk ID is resolved by invoking GetJunkIdFromPart via BindableCore (registered by JunkController).A force-field highlight (ReplicatedStorage/ForceField template cloned to workspace) tracks the currently aimed junk part on every RenderStepped tick. A 0.08-second grace window prevents flickering when the spherecast briefly misses.On activation: fires Signals.TryClaimJunk (JunkController handles the network call), increments fireToken to version all pending callbacks, then calls FireGrappleAndAttach.FireGrappleAndAttach creates an Attachment on the target junk part, creates a Beam via GrabHookVisuals.CreateBeam, and calls GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile. When retraction completes, it fires Signals.TryFinalizeJunk and plays a positional pickup sound at the character's CollisionPart/UpperTorso/HumanoidRootPart anchor resolved by CharacterAnchor.Loop sound (GrabHookLoop) is scheduled with a LoopStartDelay (0.15 s) fade-in and timed fade-out matched to the total hook animation duration.  Server (JunkService.server.luau)  Validates ReqJunkClaim: reconstructs junk world position from SpawnPos + MOVE_DIRECTION * (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer), checks player distance against GrabHookConfig.Physics.MaxDistance + 15 studs, enforces per-player cooldown, and reserves the junk.Validates ReqJunkFinalize: checks reservation ownership and the 5-second timeout, marks the junk collected, broadcasts JunkCollected, and gives the corresponding tool to player.Backpack.See Junk for the full server-side claim/finalize detail.  Shared (GrabHookVisuals.luau)  CreateBeam(att0, att1, parent) — instantiates a Beam and copies all properties from GrabHookConfig.Visuals onto it.AnimateProjectile(beam, startAtt, targetPart, hitPos, onCleanup) — three-phase RenderStepped loop (Flight / Latch / Retract). Aborts if targetPart leaves workspace (e.g. pool reclaim). Calls onCleanup when retraction completes or on abort.AnimateObserver(beam, startAtt) — simpler decay loop for other players watching the retraction animation, started by JunkController on BeginJunkRetract.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Server proximity check uses a latency slack of 15 studs The claim check compares the player's position against the reconstructed junk position with GrabHookConfig.Physics.MaxDistance + 15. The extra 15 studs compensates for network latency. Increasing MaxDistance without adjusting the slack (or vice versa) can allow or block claims unexpectedly.  Shift-lock / aim camera interplay. Equipping the GrabHook fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true) to enter aim mode. Unequipping fires (false) to exit. If you add another system that also drives RequestShootingCamera, ensure the signals do not conflict (last writer wins).mouse.TargetFilter = PlacedObjects prevents placed items from blocking the aim raycast. If new workspace folders are added for collidable world geometry that should also be ignored, add them to the filter.fireToken versioning. Incrementing fireToken on unequip cancels all pending task.delay callbacks (sound fade-out, finalize). Never skip the token check inside scheduled callbacks or sounds will play on the next hook cycle.Force-field template must exist. GrabHook.client uses ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForceField") at startup. If the template is missing, the script will yield indefinitely.Beam and attachment cleanup. AnimateProjectile destroys both the Beam and the HookAttachment on cleanup. If you add more attachments or constraints to the junk part during a hook cycle, extend the CleanupJunkModel function in JunkController to remove them on pool return.CharacterAnchor resolves the positional SFX anchor. The pickup sound plays at CollisionPart → UpperTorso → HumanoidRootPart (first found). SingleCollider avatars that lack HumanoidRootPart but have CollisionPart are handled correctly.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Server (HealthManager) Client (HealthController) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── PlayerAdded → create HealthRecord{ Health = MaxHealth, LastDamageTime = 0, LastSyncTime = 0, LastSyncedHealth = MaxHealth } CharacterAdded → reset Health to MaxHealth humanoid.MaxHealth = HealthConfig.MaxHealth humanoid.Health = record.Health ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient(player, health) ──────► Packets.HealthStateSync .OnClientEvent → Signals.OnHealthValueChanged :Fire(health) │ ▼ HealthStaminaGuiController (drives health bar) RunService.Heartbeat (server): if regen eligible (alive, not full, past RegenDelay): record.Health += HealthRegen * dt humanoid.Health = record.Health if periodicSync (0.1 s) or full: ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient ─────────────────► HealthManager.ApplyDamage: validate AttackType / AOEVariant clamp amount to [0, MaxHealth] amount *= (1 - clamp(ArmorBaseReduction * (1 + ArmorEfficiency), 0, 0.75)) -- crafted armor x Armor perk record.Health -= amount record.LastDamageTime = os.clock() humanoid.Health = record.Health ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient ─────────────────────► HealthManager.HealPlayer: record.Health = min(MaxHealth, record.Health + amount) humanoid.Health = record.Health ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient ─────────────────────►

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (HealthController.client.luau)Minimal bridge: listens to Packets.HealthStateSync.OnClientEvent and re-fires Signals.OnHealthValueChanged with the received health value. It owns no state. HealthStaminaGuiController (not part of this system) consumes OnHealthValueChanged to animate the HUD bar.  Server (HealthManager.luau)Bootstrapped by HealthSystemLoader.server.luau via HealthManager.Initialize(). Maintains a HealthRecord per player (Health, LastDamageTime, LastSyncTime, LastSyncedHealth). The regen heartbeat is capped at MAX_HEALTH_STEP_DT = 0.1 seconds per step to prevent delta-time spikes from applying burst healing. Syncs are batched: regen fires HealthStateSync at most every HEALTH_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 seconds, or immediately when health reaches full. On PlayerRemoving the record is deleted; no stale data persists across sessions.  Shared (HealthConfig.luau)Three fields read by both HealthManager (server logic) and indirectly by HealthController/GUI (via the synced value): MaxHealth, HealthRegen, RegenDelay. RegenEnabled is a kill-switch for the entire regen loop.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Non-CombatService damage bypasses HealthManager HealthManager.ApplyDamage is now called by CombatService (which WeaponServer and NpcCollisionService route through). However, any damage source that writes directly to Humanoid.Health — such as default Roblox fall damage or unrouted hazards — will bypass HealthManager's internal record, causing the HUD to show a stale value and skipping armor mitigation. Before shipping such a source, either disable it or listen to Humanoid.HealthChanged and reconcile the record (see audit note H3 in the source).  One-way mirror: HealthManager writes record.Health → humanoid.Health but never reads back from the Humanoid. Any external write to humanoid.Health is invisible to the manager until a HealthStateSync event corrects the client. Keep all health mutations going through HealthManager.ApplyDamage or HealthManager.HealPlayer.  Armor mitigation: applyDamageInternal combines crafted armor with the Armor perk as the final scale on amount before health is subtracted. It reads ArmorState/<UserId>.ArmorBaseReduction (written by ArmorManager from the player's tier) and PerkBuffs/<UserId>.ArmorEfficiency (the Armor perk), computing reduction = clamp(ArmorBaseReduction * (1 + ArmorEfficiency), 0, ArmorConfig.MaxReductionCap). Both are read per hit, so crafting a tier or allocating/respeccing the perk takes effect on the next damage event; with no armor the perk does nothing. Coverage is bounded by the chokepoint — damage that bypasses HealthManager.ApplyDamage also bypasses armor. See Perks for the cap rationale and the attacker-bonus-then-armor multiplication order.  Character respawn resets health: CharacterAdded unconditionally resets record.Health to MaxHealth. If a partial-health respawn mechanic is ever needed, this reset must be conditional.  Sync rate: HealthStateSync is sent at most every 0.1 seconds during regen. For combat situations where granular damage feedback matters, callers to ApplyDamage should be aware that each call forces an immediate sync — avoid calling it in tight per-frame loops.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: JunkService (server) — spawn loop • selectRandomJunk() — weighted tier + pity type selection • assigns id (U16), records SpawnOdometer + SpawnPos • SpawnJunk:Fire(id, modelName, startPos) ──────────────────────────► JunkController (client) • pools[poolName]:RetrieveObject(startPos) • adds to activeJunks + junkMap SetJunkSpeed:Fire(targetSpeed) ─────────────────────────────────────► JunkController (client) (on train state change or player join) • first receipt: snap currentSpeed • subsequent: start smoothstep ramp ┌── Shared speed ramp (same smoothstep on both sides) ──────────────────────────────┐ │ JunkService Heartbeat: junkOdometer += currentSpeed * dt │ │ JunkController PreSimulation: advance each junk's DistanceTraveled │ │ Despawn when (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer) > DESPAWN_DISTANCE (server) │ │ when DistanceTraveled > DESPAWN_DISTANCE (client) │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Player fires GrabHook → Signals.TryClaimJunk:Fire(id, hitPos) • JunkController → Packets.ReqJunkClaim:Fire(id, hitPos) ──────────► JunkService • proximity check vs junkOdometer • cooldown check • reserves junk for player • BeginJunkRetract:Fire(id, hitPos, retractTime, player) ◄── BeginJunkRetract ─────────────────────────────────────────────── • remove from activeJunks; move to retractingJunks • if localPlayer: GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile drives movement • if other player: observer lerp on RenderStepped Player fires Signals.TryFinalizeJunk:Fire(id) • JunkController → Packets.ReqJunkFinalize:Fire(id) ───────────────► JunkService • verifies reservation + timeout • marks Collected, awards Tool to Backpack • JunkCollected:Fire(id, player) → all clients ◄── JunkCollected ────────────────────────────────────────────────── • pool:InsertObject (returns model)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (JunkController.client.luau)  Builds per-model GenericPoolInstance pools at startup, one per model name found in JunkAssets, with initial size 5, max 60, expand by 10.On SpawnJunk: checks MAX_CLIENT_JUNKS = 250 cap, retrieves model from pool, sets Transparency = 0, parents to workspace/JunksVisuals, records in activeJunks and junkMap.PreSimulation loop: advances the smoothstep speed ramp, moves each active junk by currentSpeed * dt along MOVE_DIRECTION, applies per-junk random rotation, increments DistanceTraveled. Despawns via RemoveJunkLocal when DistanceTraveled > DESPAWN_DISTANCE.On BeginJunkRetract: removes the junk from simulation, moves it to retractingJunks. The local player's animation is driven by GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile; other players see an observer lerp on RenderStepped. An 8-second safety-net timeout returns the model to the pool if JunkCollected never arrives.On JunkCollected: cleans up rope attachments and beams on the model, returns it to the pool.Bridges claim/finalize signals from GrabHook.client to Packets.ReqJunkClaim / Packets.ReqJunkFinalize via Signals.TryClaimJunk and Signals.TryFinalizeJunk.Exposes GetJunkIdFromPart(part) via BindableCore so GrabHook.client can resolve a junk ID from a raycast hit part.  Server (JunkService.server.luau)  Weighted tier selection: each tier's weight is multiplied by GlobalModifiers.TierMultipliers[tier]; a random number selects the tier by accumulated weight.Type selection with pity: if spawnsSinceLastEnergy >= ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD (8), an Energy type junk is forced; otherwise weighted by SpawnChance * TypeMultiplier. The pity counter resets on every Energy spawn.Records SpawnOdometer (value of junkOdometer at spawn time) and SpawnPos for each active junk. The junk's current world position is reconstructed on claim as SpawnPos + MOVE_DIRECTION * (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer).Distance-based despawn on Heartbeat: removes any junk where (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer) > DESPAWN_DISTANCE. This mirrors the client-side DistanceTraveled check.Claim validation (ReqJunkClaim): reconstructs junk world position, checks distance against GrabHookConfig.Physics.MaxDistance + 15 studs (latency slack), enforces per-player cooldown, reserves junk, computes retract time, and fires BeginJunkRetract to all clients.Finalize validation (ReqJunkFinalize): checks reservation ownership and 5-second timeout, marks collected, fires JunkCollected to all clients, and gives the tool to the player's Backpack.SetTrainState(isMoving) and SetTrainStarted(started) are wired to Signals.SetTrainState and Signals.SetTrainStarted for external control.Junk counter wraps at 65535 (U16 boundary) to keep IDs compact in the SpawnJunk packet.  Shared (SpawnHelper.luau)  SpawnHelper:Init() caches all BasePart children of workspace/SpawnVolumes weighted by volume.SpawnHelper.GetRandomPoint() picks a random world position inside one of the spawn volumes using volume-weighted selection.

searchDocs.title: Disabling spawn volumes​
searchDocs.content: Spawn volumes can be grouped and toggled at runtime without touching the workspace. Author an optional SpawnGroup string attribute on a BasePart under workspace/SpawnVolumes; every part sharing the same value forms a togglable group. Parts with no SpawnGroup attribute are ungrouped and always active — they're never affected by a toggle.  SpawnHelper exposes three methods on top of Init / GetRandomPoint:  SpawnHelper:SetGroupEnabled(groupName: string, enabled: boolean) — enables or disables every volume in groupName. warns on an unrecognized group name (typo guard) but still records the state.SpawnHelper:IsGroupEnabled(groupName: string): boolean — true unless the group is currently disabled; unknown or ungrouped names always read true.SpawnHelper:GetGroups(): { string } — the distinct SpawnGroup values authored across the spawn volumes, for validation/debug.  The pirate-ship event uses this to disable the ship-facing group during the at-range cannon phase: junk stops spawning toward the ship, and any junk already floating there clears out via the normal distance-despawn instead of being force-removed, so the area is clean by the time players board.  If every group with volumes ends up disabled, GetRandomPoint() returns nil (no enabled volumes remain) and the spawn loop simply idles until a group is re-enabled — no junk spawns, but nothing errors.

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: Module: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JunkConfig.luau  Field	Default	EffectMAX_SERVER_JUNKS	200	Hard cap on server-side active junk entries MAX_CLIENT_JUNKS	250	Client silently drops SpawnJunk events beyond this count MOVE_DIRECTION	Vector3.new(1,0,0)	World direction all junk travels DESPAWN_DISTANCE	700 studs	Odometer delta at which junk is removed (both sides) DEFAULT_SPAWN_RATE	0.5 s	Seconds between junk spawns when train is moving STOPPED_SPAWN_RATE	1.5 s	Seconds between spawns when train is stopped DEFAULT_JUNK_SPEED	10 studs/s	Junk movement speed when train is moving STOPPED_JUNK_SPEED	5 studs/s	Junk movement speed when train is stopped SPEED_RAMP_DURATION	1.5 s	Smoothstep ramp time on speed change ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD	8	Non-energy spawns before Energy is guaranteed BaseModifiers.GlobalSpawnRateMult	1.0	Global spawn rate multiplier (runtime-adjustable) Tiers[n].Weight	varies	Relative spawn weight for each tier (Tier 5 is 0 = disabled) Tiers[n].Types[t].SpawnChance	varies	Relative spawn chance for each type within a tier Tiers[n].Types[t].Yield	varies	Item count awarded on collection  Model lists (Tiers[n].Types[t].Models) are auto-populated from ReplicatedStorage/JunkAssets/TierN/TypeName folder contents at require time.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Both sides integrate the same ramp — keep them in sync The server (junkOdometer) and client (DistanceTraveled) both use the identical smoothstep ramp over SPEED_RAMP_DURATION. If you change the ramp formula in one place, change it in the other. Drift causes the server's proximity check to reject valid claims.  Reservation timeout is 5 seconds If a client claims junk but never finalizes (e.g. disconnects mid-retract), the reservation expires after 5 seconds (RESERVATION_TIMEOUT). Another player can then claim the same junk. The client has an 8-second safety net (RETRACT_RECLAIM_TIMEOUT) that returns the model to the pool if JunkCollected never arrives — this value must exceed RESERVATION_TIMEOUT plus round-trip time.  Pool cleanup is mandatory. Every path that removes a junk from activeJunks or retractingJunks must call CleanupJunkModel then pool:InsertObject. Skipping cleanup leaks HookAttachment or Beam instances on the model, which will appear on the next retrieval.workspace/JunksVisuals folder must exist. JunkController uses WaitForChild to find it; the folder should be created in the place file or by a server startup script.Junk ID wraps at 65535. This is intentional for the NumberU16 wire type in SpawnJunk. Long-running servers are safe because entries are removed before the counter can collide.Tier 5 weight is 0. Items in Tier 5 will never spawn under default config. Set the weight above 0 to enable them.SpawnHelper:Init() must be called before the spawn loop. JunkService calls it at startup; if no SpawnVolumes parts exist in workspace, GetRandomPoint will always return nil and no junk will spawn.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Any client script fires: Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(type, message, duration?, executedFunction?) └─> NotificationManager (sole subscriber) ├─ validate type against NotificationConfig.Types ├─ enforce MaxConcurrent cap (evict oldest non-executed toast if needed) ├─ build Frame in NotificationGui.MainContainer │ ├─ icon ImageLabel (per-type asset ID + color from NotificationConfig) │ ├─ time-left bar (timed toasts only; linear MotionMaster tween) │ └─ text label with gradient-sweep reveal ├─ SoundManager.PlaySFX(NotificationConfig.SfxNames[type]) ├─ intro animations via MotionMaster (size expand + fade in) └─ schedule close: ├─ timed: task.delay(duration or Device.Duration, closeEntry) └─> executed: task.spawn(executedFunction) -> closeEntry on return (optional ExecutedFunctionTimeout safety close) Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() └─> closeEntry() on all active toasts simultaneously

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: The notification system is client-only. There is no server component.  NotificationController.client.luau  A three-line bootstrap that calls NotificationManager.Init() once. After Init runs, NotificationManager subscribes to Signals.RequestNotification and Signals.RequestClearNotifications. No other setup is required.  NotificationManager/init.luau  Manages the full toast lifecycle:  Creates (lazily) a ScreenGui named NotificationGui with a UIListLayout container anchored to the top-centre of the screen. The top offset is NotificationConfig.TopOffsetScale (a fraction of viewport height). New toasts are inserted at the top of the stack; LayoutOrder is a negated monotonic counter so newer toasts sort above older ones.Executed-function toasts (executedFunction ~= nil) sit above timed toasts in a reserved LayoutOrder band.Font size and padding are viewport-responsive: scaled by math.min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) / BaseScreenMin, clamped to [0.7, 1.3].Text width is measured via TextService:GetTextSize after accounting for icon width, time-bar width (timed toasts only), and padding gaps, so the label never clips its content.Close animations run a MotionMaster tween that shrinks the frame to UDim2.fromOffset(0, 0); the Janitor per entry destroys the frame when the tween completes.A debounced viewport resize handler (requestResize) re-measures and re-tweens all live toasts when the window size changes.

Types and per-type assets:  Type	Notes"success"	Green background "info"	Blue background "warn"	Amber background "alert"	Red background "default"	Dark grey background  Each type has entries in NotificationConfig.ImageIds, NotificationConfig.Colors, NotificationConfig.BaseTransparency, and NotificationConfig.SfxNames. searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Use Signals — never require NotificationManager directly Feature controllers must fire Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(type, message, duration?, executedFunction?) to show a toast. Requiring NotificationManager directly and calling internal functions breaks the decoupled contract, creates a hard dependency on a client-only module, and will error if accidentally required server-side.  type must exactly match one of the five lowercase strings in NotificationConfig.Types. An unrecognised type is silently dropped (no toast, no error).duration overrides the device default (NotificationConfig.Device.Desktop.Duration or .Mobile.Duration). Pass nil to use the default.Passing executedFunction makes the toast persist until the function returns (or ExecutedFunctionTimeout elapses). The function runs in a pcall-protected task.spawn — errors are suppressed and the toast still closes. Keep the function short; it runs on the client main thread.When MaxConcurrent is reached, the oldest timed toast is force-closed. Executed-function toasts are never evicted by the cap — they stay until their function returns. Avoid queuing many long-running executed toasts simultaneously.Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() closes all active toasts immediately regardless of type or remaining duration. Use it only for hard resets (e.g. character death, scene transitions).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Player presses MoveButton / StashButton (GUI) └─> PlaceableActions.bind() fires ReqMovePlaceable / ReqStashPlaceable packet └─> PlaceableActionsServer.OnServerInvoke ├─ cooldown check (per-player, os.clock) ├─ ancestry check (model.Parent == workspace.PlacedObjects) ├─ attribute check (PlaceableName attribute on model) ├─ tool template check (ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools/<Name>) ├─ proximity check (HRP distance <= MaxActionDistance) ├─ atomic claim (model.Parent = nil, race guard) ├─ clone Tool -> player.Backpack ├─ Move only: humanoid:EquipTool(newTool) ├─ BroadcastPlaceablePoof:Fire(cframe, placeableName, isMove) └─ model:Destroy() + record cooldown timestamp └─> All clients receive poof broadcast └─> PlaceableActions (client) plays shrink tween + SFX

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — PlaceableActions.luau  PlaceableActions.bind(model, gui) wires MoveButton and StashButton into the packet system and returns a Binding with a single Unbind() method. On success the module fires Signals.OnPlaceableMoved or Signals.OnPlaceableStashed so other systems can react without polling.  The poof handler is also client-only and lives in this file. On receiving BroadcastPlaceablePoof it clones the matching model from ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableItems, strips scripts/collisions/shadows from the clone, parents it to workspace.PlaceablePoofs, then runs a parallel MotionMaster.Sequence that shrinks every BasePart to near-zero while fading it out. The clone self-destructs when the sequence completes.  Server — PlaceableActionsServer.server.luau  Owns the OnServerInvoke handlers for ReqStashPlaceable and ReqMovePlaceable. Runs every validation step listed in the data-flow diagram. The atomic claim pattern (model.Parent = nil followed by a re-read) prevents two simultaneous requests from granting the same item twice. Returns boolean — false on any failed check, true on full success.  On a successful Move, the handler also calls PlaceableRevertStore.Set(player, { cframe = cframe, placeableName = placeableName, tool = newTool }), recording the item's original CFrame under the granted tool instance. This lets the build-mode cancel (RequestPlacementRevert) revert the item to its original spot if the player presses X without re-placing. The entry is cleared when the player re-places via PlaceItem, when the revert fires and consumes it, or when the player leaves the server.

searchDocs.content: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PlaceableActions.luau — client bind/unbind helper + poof visual renderer; auto-connects poof broadcast on the client sidesrc/ServerScriptService/PlaceableActionsServer.server.luau — server validation, atomic claim, Tool grant, BroadcastPlaceablePoof dispatchsrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau — PlaceableActions sub-table with all tuning knobssrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau — ReqStashPlaceable, ReqMovePlaceable, BroadcastPlaceablePoof packet definitions

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: All three values live in PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions:  Field	Default	DescriptionCooldown	0.4 s	Per-player minimum gap between accepted stash/move requests PoofDuration	0.25 s	Duration of the shrink-to-nothing tween on poof MaxActionDistance	24 studs	Server-side re-check of player proximity to the placed model

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Three requirements must all be present A placeable supports Stash/Move only when all three of the following exist simultaneously: A Model in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<Name> (already required for placement).A Tool template in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> with a PlaceableName attribute set to the same name string.ImageButton instances named exactly MoveButton and StashButton somewhere inside the GUI that PlaceableActions.bind is called with. Either may be omitted, but the missing one will log a warning and that action will be silently unavailable to the player. If PlaceableTools/<Name> is missing the server returns false and nothing is destroyed — no item is lost — but the player gets no feedback.  The server proximity check (MaxActionDistance) is a second guard independent of the ProximityPrompt range. Keep them in sync when tuning the in-world prompt.Stash/Move discards all per-instance state on the placed model. The granted Tool is always a fresh clone from the template. If per-instance state matters, snapshot attributes before the action reaches the server.Any nearby player can stash any placement — ownership is not tracked. Add per-instance owner attributes and an ownership check in handleAction if griefing becomes a concern.Call binding:Unbind() when the GUI closes. Failing to unbind leaves the Janitor alive and button listeners connected to a GUI that may already be gone.

searchDocs.title: Point economy​
searchDocs.content: Each level-up grants 1 Personal point AND 1 Party point.Available points = playerLevel - sum(spent in that pool).Points cannot go negative; the pool is floored at 0.Respec costs nothing and returns all points in the chosen pool — it also re-locks each unlocked perk in that pool and refunds its UnlockCost in coins; see Unlock gate.Points carry across places because PerkManager uses the same DataStore key (PlayerPerks) everywhere in the universe.

searchDocs.title: Unlock gate​
searchDocs.content: Every perk declares a one-time UnlockCost (coins) and UnlockLevel (player level) gate in PerkConfig. A perk with both 0 is a free starter, auto-unlocked: PlayerHP (Vitality) and JunkRarity (Salvage Luck).Unlock is permanent: it persists on the PlayerPerks profile as an Unlocked map ({ [perkId]: boolean }), alongside PerkLevels and a PerkSchemaVersion guard.Migration: the first load after this shipped wipes all existing PerkLevels/Unlocked once (clean slate — derived points return automatically). Guarded by PerkSchemaVersion < 1 (then set to 1), so it fires exactly once per profile; starters are re-seeded immediately after so play never begins with zero unlocked perks.Respec (PerkManager.Respec) now fully resets the chosen pool: it clears PerkLevels and Unlocked for every perk in that pool, refunds each unlocked perk's UnlockCost via CoinManager.RefundCoins — an exact, un-inflated refund, not scaled by the Fortune perk's CoinGainBonus (unlike CoinManager.AddCoins) — then re-seeds free starters so the pool isn't left fully locked.Unlocking a perk changes no buffs (its level is still 0), so PerkManager.UnlockPerk does not fire Signals.OnPerkStateChanged; PerkEffectsDispatcher is untouched by an unlock.Allocating a point on a locked perk returns PERK_LOCKED (PerkState.canAllocate checks unlocked[perkId] before the level/point checks). Unlock-specific reason codes are ALREADY_UNLOCKED, LEVEL_REQUIRED, and NOT_ENOUGH_COINS (checked in that order by PerkState.canUnlock, after UNKNOWN_PERK).The client-facing PerkView descriptor (PerkClient.luau) gains IsUnlocked, UnlockCost, UnlockLevel, and MeetsUnlockLevel fields. PerkClient.Unlock(perkId) is the fire-and-forget command that sends ReqUnlockPerk; reconciliation arrives via the next PerkStateSync.

searchDocs.title: Party-max resolution​
searchDocs.content: Party perks (Salvage Luck, Fuel Efficiency, Thrift, Shield Capacity, Heavy Ordnance) apply to the entire server, but only the highest level held by any single player is active. If Player A has Salvage Luck 6 and Player B has Salvage Luck 3, the server resolves at 6. PerkEffectsDispatcher recomputes the max on every allocate, respec, player join, and player leave.

searchDocs.title: Buff contract​
searchDocs.content: PerkEffectsDispatcher is the sole writer of the buff folders. Other systems read only — never write.  Folder	Scope	Updated whenReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId>	Personal, per-player	On allocate/respec, player join, player leave ReplicatedStorage/PartyPerkBuffs	Party, server-max	Same as above  Attribute keys match PerkConfig.BuffKey:  Perk	BuffKey	Value formula	ConsumerVitality	HPBonus	0.04 * level	HealthManager Regeneration	RegenBonus	0.10 * level	HealthManager Quick Reel	ReelSpeedBonus	0.05 * level	GrabHook Power	DamageBonus	0.03 * level	WeaponServer (chokepoint: scaledDamage, applied after headshot multiplier, all 5 player-attack sites) Fortune	CoinGainBonus	0.05 * level	CoinManager.AddCoins (math.max(1, math.floor(amount * (1 + bonus))) — 1-coin minimum) Armor	ArmorEfficiency	0.025 * level	HealthManager (chokepoint: applyDamageInternal) — multiplies the crafted-armor base reduction: clamp(ArmorBaseReduction * (1 + ArmorEfficiency), 0, 0.75). No armor equipped ⇒ no reduction. Net Cast	NetCapacityBonus	1 * level (max level 4)	GrabHook / JunkService — hook capacity = 1 + NetCapacityBonus (server-clamped to GrabHookConfig.Physics.NetMaxTargets = 5). See GrabHook. Salvage Luck	JunkTierRarityBonus	0.08 * level	JunkService (via ApplyTierMultiplier) Efficiency	FuelEfficiencyBonus	0.04 * level	TrainFuelManager drain multiplier — stacks multiplicatively with ResearchBuffs.FuelEfficiency (see Research Bench) Thrift	WeaponCostReduction	0.03 * level	(deferred — no weapon cost mechanic exists; declared in config, intentionally unwired) Shield Capacity	TrainShieldBonus	0.05 * level	TrainShieldManager.recomputeMax — multiplicative on top of BASE_SHIELD + ResearchBuffs.MaxHP; see Train Shield Heavy Ordnance	CannonDamageBonus	0.06 * level	CannonServer (applyCannonAOE, applied as Damage × (1 + CannonDamageBonus) per shot). Consumed by the Cannon system at the server shell-damage line.  Perks marked (deferred) have no planned consumer yet.  Armor damage mitigation. Crafted armor (see ArmorConfig / ArmorManager) publishes a per-player ArmorState/<UserId>.ArmorBaseReduction — the base fraction of incoming damage removed by the player's current armor tier. The Armor perk no longer reduces damage on its own; it is an efficiency multiplier on that base. HealthManager.applyDamageInternal reads both per hit and computes reduction = clamp(ArmorBaseReduction * (1 + ArmorEfficiency), 0, 0.75), then scales amount by (1 - reduction) as the final step before subtracting from health. With no armor (tier 0 → base 0) the perk contributes nothing. Because the attacker's DamageBonus is already applied upstream in WeaponServer, attacker bonus and defender mitigation multiply independently: base * (1 + DamageBonus) * (1 - reduction). Coverage is every path routed through CombatService/HealthManager (Melee/Bullet/AOE and NPC hits); damage written directly to Humanoid.Health bypasses the sink and is not mitigated (see Health).

searchDocs.content: PerkController (client) PerkManager (server) PerkEffectsDispatcher (server) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ── JOIN ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── profile loaded (migrateAndSeed: one-time wipe + seedStarters) replicate(player): ◄── PerkStateSync(levels, unlocked, personalAvail, partyAvail, playerLevel) ───────── perkLevels / unlocked / available updated repaint() publish personal buffs (0s) publishParty() ── UNLOCK ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── player requests unlock ──── ReqUnlockPerk(perkId) ──────► UnlockPerk: canUnlock (level+coins) → DeductCoins → Unlocked[perkId]=true replicate(player) (no OnPerkStateChanged — buffs unchanged) ◄── PerkStateSync(levels, unlocked, personalAvail, partyAvail, playerLevel) ────── ◄── (success, reasonCode) ────────── ── ALLOCATE ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── player clicks + optimistic: level++, avail-- repaint() ──── ReqAllocatePerk(perkId) ──────► AllocatePoint: canAllocate → mutate Signals.OnPerkStateChanged:Fire(player) replicate(player): ◄── PerkStateSync(levels, unlocked, ...) ────── reconcile to authoritative state │ repaint() └──────────────────────────► publishPersonal(player) publishParty() ◄── (success, reasonCode) ────────── ── LEVEL UP ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── XPManager: level increases Signals.OnPlayerLevelUp:Fire(player, newLevel) PerkManager: replicate(player) ◄── PerkStateSync(levels, unlocked, personal+1, party+1, newLevel) ────── repaint() — new points visible

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — PerkConfig.luau is the single tuning surface: 12 perk declarations with Category, BuffKey, PerLevel, MaxLevel, DisplayName, Description, display Order, an optional ValueKind, and per-perk UnlockCost/UnlockLevel (both nil/0-default; a perk with both 0 is a free starter). Tune values here — do not hard-code them in logic. PerkConfig.STORE_NAME is the ProfileStore key, identical across all places.  ValueKind controls GUI effect-string formatting in PerkClient.effectFor: nil/"percent" (the default, used by every perk except Net Cast) renders Description with %d replaced by the whole-percent bonus (floor(PerLevel * level * 100 + 0.5)); "count" (used only by Net Cast) renders %d as a raw total, baseline 1 plus the bonus (1 + floor(PerLevel * level + 0.5), i.e. 1 + NetCapacityBonus) instead of a percentage — so "Grab up to %d junk at once" reads as "Grab up to 3 junk at once" at level 2 (1 baseline + 2 bonus), not a percent value.  Shared — PerkResultCodes.luau is the frozen result-code enum (OK=0, NO_PROFILE=1, UNKNOWN_PERK=2, AT_MAX_LEVEL=3, NO_POINTS=4, PERK_LOCKED=5, ALREADY_UNLOCKED=6, LEVEL_REQUIRED=7, NOT_ENOUGH_COINS=8). Used by both the server handler and the client UI.  Shared — PerkState.luau is a pure, side-effect-free module: spent(perkLevels, category), available(perkLevels, category, playerLevel), isUnlocked(unlocked, perkId), canUnlock(unlocked, perkId, playerLevel, coins), and canAllocate(perkLevels, unlocked, perkId, playerLevel). The server uses it for authoritative validation; the client uses it to gate the + button and the unlock control.  Server — PerkManager.luau owns the PlayerPerks ProfileStore (one session per player), storing PerkLevels, Unlocked, and PerkSchemaVersion. On load, migrateAndSeed wipes PerkLevels/Unlocked exactly once if PerkSchemaVersion < 1 (then bumps it to 1), then seeds free starters into Unlocked via seedStarters. UnlockPerk validates with PerkState.canUnlock, deducts UnlockCost via CoinManager.DeductCoins, and replicates — it does not fire OnPerkStateChanged (buffs are unaffected by an unlock). AllocatePoint and Respec validate, mutate PerkLevels/Unlocked, fire OnPerkStateChanged, and replicate; Respec additionally clears Unlocked for the pool and refunds each perk's UnlockCost via CoinManager.RefundCoins (exact, un-inflated) before re-seeding starters. Initialize wires PlayerAdded, PlayerRemoving, the three packet handlers (ReqAllocatePerk, ReqUnlockPerk, ReqRespecPerks), and OnPlayerLevelUp re-replicate. GetPerkLevels(player) returns the live reference for PerkEffectsDispatcher.  Server — PerkSystemLoader.server.luau calls PerkManager.Initialize() once per server.  Server — PerkEffectsDispatcher.server.luau is the sole writer of both buff folders. It listens to OnPerkStateChanged, PlayerAdded, and PlayerRemoving, then calls publishPersonal (per-player attributes) and publishParty (server-max across all players). Also bridges Junk Rarity to Signals.ApplyTierMultiplier (which JunkService already consumes).  Client — PerkClient.luau is the GUI-agnostic data layer (owns no GUI). It caches the authoritative PerkStateSync snapshot (perkLevels, unlocked, personalAvailable, partyAvailable, playerLevel), watches the replicated PartyPerkBuffs folder, and exposes queries returning PerkView descriptors — now including IsUnlocked, UnlockCost, UnlockLevel, and MeetsUnlockLevel — via GetPerks/GetActivePerks/GetAvailablePoints/GetPerk. Commands: optimistic-prediction Allocate/Respec/CanRespec, plus Unlock(perkId) (no optimistic coin prediction — the server owns the balance; the next PerkStateSync reflects success or failure), and a Changed signal. "Active" is category-aware: a Personal perk is active at the player's Level > 0; a Party perk is active at its server-wide ActivePartyLevel > 0. Perk screens are authored separately, require PerkClient, and subscribe to Changed to repaint.  Client — PerkController.client.luau is a one-line bootstrap that calls PerkClient.Init() once on join so the data layer is warm before any GUI opens.

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: All tuning lives in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PerkConfig.luau.  Field	EffectPerks[id].PerLevel	Buff value added per level (fraction; applied as PerLevel * level). Perks[id].MaxLevel	Cap on levels in this perk. Perks[id].DisplayName	Shown in the perk panel header. Perks[id].Description	Shown in the perk row; %d is replaced with the whole-percent bonus. Perks[id].UnlockCost	One-time coin cost to unlock this perk, paid via ReqUnlockPerk (0/nil = free starter). Leveling stays point-based; this is not spent again. Perks[id].UnlockLevel	Minimum player XP level required to unlock (0/nil = none). STORE_NAME	ProfileStore key — change this only if you intentionally want to wipe all saved perk + unlock data.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Points are derived, not stored Available points are never stored directly — only PerkLevels, Unlocked, and PerkSchemaVersion persist. Available points = level - spent. Never add a separate stored point counter — it will desync.  Party perk levels shown in the GUI are per-player, not the resolved active level The + button and level display in the Party tab show how many points this player has invested. The (active N) sub-label shows the server-resolved max. Both are expected: a player at level 3 in a party where someone else is at level 7 sees Lv 3/10 (active 7).  PerkEffectsDispatcher must run before PerkManager on join PerkEffectsDispatcher seeds its folder at boot. PerkManager fires OnPerkStateChanged after profile load, which triggers a republish. The ordering is correct because both are ServerScriptService scripts and PerkManager.Initialize() is called from PerkSystemLoader, which yields on ProfileStore:StartSessionAsync before firing the signal.  HPBonus subscription attaches once at join HealthManager subscribes to the HPBonus attribute change in PlayerAdded, not CharacterAdded. If PerkBuffs/<UserId> does not exist at join time (the dispatcher hasn't seeded yet), the subscription is skipped for that session. In practice the dispatcher seeds synchronously at boot, so the folder exists before any player's PlayerAdded fires normally.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Player equips tool │ ▼ PlacementClient (client) • SetBuildMode(true) • SetGhostModel(template) • fires ClientToggleGhost ──────────────────► PlacementServer (server) • validates itemName exists • relays ServerToggleGhost → other clients • Heartbeat: CalculatePlacement (raycast) • UpdateGhostPosition → CheckValidity • fires ClientUpdateGhost (CFrame) ─────────► PlacementServer • type-checks CFrame • relays ServerUpdateGhost → other clients • mouse click / confirm signal • fires PlaceItem (origin, dir, rotation, mode) ► PlacementServer • cooldown check • distance checks (origin + final pos) • isolated PlacementSystem per request • CalculatePlacement + CheckValidity • Clone + finalizeModel → PlacedObjects • destroy tool • ServerToggleGhost(false) → all clients

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (PlacementClient.client.luau)  Creates one PlacementSystem instance (grid size 2, tag BuildArea).On tool equip: calls SetBuildMode(true), SetGhostModel(template), fires ClientToggleGhost.Fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(false) on build mode entry to disable the aim camera.PlacementCameraController.client.luau takes over the camera (CameraType.Scriptable, near-top-down, follows the player, yaw locked at entry) for the duration of build mode, easing in and out of the angle rather than snapping, and fades any PlacementOccluder-tagged geometry. See Camera.Heartbeat loop (rate-limited to GhostUpdateHz, default 20 Hz): raycasts, calls UpdateGhostPosition, fires ClientUpdateGhost with the result CFrame.Fires Signals.OnBuildValidityChanged when validity changes so UI and audio can react.Grid/free toggle, rotation, confirm, cancel, and ghost-lock are all driven by signals wired to BuildModeGuiController.Listens to ServerToggleGhost / ServerUpdateGhost and calls SetOtherGhost to render other players' ghost previews.  Server (PlacementServer.server.luau)  Relays ClientToggleGhost to other players after confirming the item name exists in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems.Relays ClientUpdateGhost (CFrame type-checked) to other players.On PlaceItem: enforces per-player cooldown (PLACE_COOLDOWN = 0.4 s), character/tool guards, ray-origin distance (MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE = 50 studs), final-position distance (MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE = 60 studs), and collision validity — all using an isolated PlacementSystem instance with a ServerStorage-parented ghost that is never replicated.On success: clones the template, calls finalizeModel (makes CollisionBox invisible + non-collidable, visual parts opaque, and tags the CollisionBox with PlacementObstruction so future placements collide with it), parents to workspace/PlacedObjects, destroys the player's tool, and broadcasts ghost-clear to all clients. If the placer's own character ends up overlapping the placed item (their character was excluded from the obstruction check — see Gotchas), they are teleported horizontally clear of it, clamped to stay within the same BuildArea part.  Shared (PlacementSystem.luau)  Handles ghost model lifecycle, grid-snap vs free-placement position calculation, collision-box derivation, obstruction validity check, and other-player ghost rendering.IS_CLIENT guards prevent Texture and TweenPlus calls from running on the server.SetBuildMode is client-only (creates grid Texture instances on build area parts); the server sets IsBuildMode = true directly.

searchDocs.title: Cancelling build mode​
searchDocs.content: Pressing X (configurable via PlacementConfig.CancelKey) or the on-screen Cancel button (mobile) fires Signals.RequestPlacementCancel. Both paths reach the same cancelPlacement function in PlacementClient, which immediately snaps build-mode visuals off and sends a RequestPlacementRevert RemoteFunction call to the server.  Escape is intentionally not used — Roblox reserves it for the in-game menu.  The server checks PlaceableRevertStore to determine the outcome:  Session type	OutcomeFresh placement (item was never placed before)	Server returns false → client calls humanoid:UnequipTools() and the tool returns to the Backpack Move session, original spot is free	Server re-places the item at its original CFrame, destroys the tool, returns true → item reverts, no unequip needed Move session, original spot is occupied	Server returns false → client falls back to unequip  See Placeable Actions for how a Move session records the revert entry, and the Networking Map for the RequestPlacementRevert packet definition.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Anti-exploit — do not relax the server thresholds MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE = 50, MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE = 60, and PLACE_COOLDOWN = 0.4 in PlacementServer are the primary defences against remote placement exploits. Raising these values substantially would allow clients to place items anywhere in the world or spam unlimited items.  Model structure is required. Every entry in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems must have a CollisionBox (BasePart) child. Without it, PlacementSystem warns and falls back to bounding-box collision, which can cause floating or incorrect validity checks.Obstruction is tag-driven, not folder-driven. Build placement only avoids a volume if it is tagged PlacementObstruction. Placed items are tagged automatically on their CollisionBox by finalizeModel. Any static world model that placement must respect (e.g. TrainShieldGeneratorPlaceholder, ResearchBenchPlaceholder) must have a CollisionBox BasePart tagged PlacementObstruction by hand. Tag the CollisionBox part only, never the whole model — sibling sub-models like TrajectoryPoints would otherwise become map-wide placement blockers.CollisionBox part must not be named RootPart or tagged PlacementIgnore. Those names cause the part to be treated as invisible/non-collidable in the ghost.Each PlaceItem event creates an isolated PlacementSystem. This is intentional — it prevents concurrent requests from different players from corrupting shared state. Do not cache a server-side PlacementSystem across requests.SetBuildMode must only be called on the client. Calling it on the server would create Texture instances in workspace and replicate them to all clients.Ghost relay is observer-only. GhostModels folder and its contents exist only on the client; the server never sees them. The server's validity check correctly skips that folder for this reason.Cutscene and combat gates (isInCutscene, isInCombat) in PlacementClient are not yet wired to any external system — they are TODO integration points.Own-character exclusion is per-instance, not global. PlacementSystem.new(buildAreaTag, gridSize, excludePlayer)'s third argument controls which player's Character is skipped by BuildObstructionFilter. The client always passes its own Players.LocalPlayer; the server passes the requesting player for both PlaceItem and RequestPlacementRevert. Other players' characters are never excluded — they still block placement as before.Push-out only ever needs to consider the placer's own character. Because every other player's character remains an obstruction, no other player can ever end up overlapping a freshly finalized item — pushCharacterClearOfBox in PlacementServer only acts on the requesting/reverting player. The platform it clamps into comes from PlacementSystem.LastBuildAreaPart, which is only ever populated by CalculatePlacement's raycast (the PlaceItem path). The revert/Move-cancel path re-places at a stored CFrame and never calls CalculatePlacement, so LastBuildAreaPart is nil there; PlacementServer falls back to a small dedicated helper, findBuildAreaBelow, which raycasts straight down from the revert position (filtered to the BuildArea tag, the same idiom CalculatePlacement uses) to resolve the platform part so push-out on revert is still clamped to the platform.

searchDocs.title: Data model​
searchDocs.content: The profile stores a single value, TotalXP (lifetime cumulative). Level and progress are derived from it via XPCurve.luau, so re-tuning the curve never desyncs saved data.

searchDocs.title: Curve​
searchDocs.content: xpToNext(L) = round(CURVE_COEFF * L ^ CURVE_EXP) + CURVE_OFFSET (defaults5, 1.5, 45), cap MAX_LEVEL = 100. Total to level 100 ≈ 202,000 XP. All constants live in Configs/XPConfig.luau.

searchDocs.title: Earning (party-shared)​
searchDocs.content: XP is shared with the whole party; one party occupies one server, so every player in the server receives the full award.  Distance: while the train is in its "go" state (running — not braked, not stalled), the party earns DISTANCE_XP_PER_TICK every DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS. Driven off Signals.SetTrainState. The train starts braked, so no XP accrues before the first un-brake.Kills: any EnemyNPC death awards KILL_XP to the party (attribution- agnostic). Wired in XPSystemLoader.

searchDocs.title: Components​
searchDocs.content: Configs/XPConfig.luau — tuning constants.XPCurve.luau — pure level/progress math.XPManager.luau (ServerStorage) — profile lifecycle, award API (AddXP,AddPartyXP), replication. Runs in both places.XPSystemLoader.server.luau — gameplay-only earner wiring.XPController.client.luau — replication bridge → Signals.OnXPChanged, and the level-up toast via Signals.RequestNotification.

searchDocs.title: Cross-place (lobby ↔ gameplay)​
searchDocs.content: DataStores are universe-wide. Both places use the same STORE_NAME and key (tostring(UserId)), so XP/Level are shared automatically; ProfileStore session-locking serializes the teleport handoff. The lobby place must runXPManager.Initialize() and XPController (for display + clean handoff) but NOT XPSystemLoader — no earners in the lobby. The lobby mirror is a separate deployment, not part of this repo.

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (ProximityPickupController.client.luau)Listens to two packets only; creates no UI and does no proximity math. PickupItemReady applies a HoverEffect (bob + Y-spin) to the handle via a Janitor-managed cleanup handle, and wires AncestryChanged so the effect stops cleanly when the part is destroyed. PickupItemClaimed stops the hover effect, then for the local claimer plays a pickup SFX (via SoundManager.PlaySFXAt using CharacterAnchor to resolve the player's position) and tweens the handle toward the camera using MotionMaster.Play; for all other clients it destroys the handle immediately.  Server (ProximityPickupServer.luau)RegisterItem(part, metadata, callback, keepModel?) is the sole public registration entry. It generates a GUID itemId, tags the part "PickupItem", creates an invisible anchored sphere zone in workspace.PickupZones, and fires PickupItemReady to all clients. zone.Touched is the primary claim trigger (any player, shared-loot semantics). Claim(part, player) is the programmatic path used by the shredder's auto-collect loop. Both paths call the same executeClaimAsync which transitions the record to "Claimed", destroys the zone, broadcasts PickupItemClaimed, then after FLOAT_DURATION calls the callback and cleans up. _TryMerge runs after MERGE_DELAY and absorbs a newly registered handle into a nearby same-type unclaimed survivor, accumulating Quantity on the survivor.  Dropped-tool server (DroppedToolService.server.luau)Bootstraps two PhysicsService collision groups: DroppedMaterial (Tools that leave the player's hand) and DroppableSurface (tagged geometry). DroppedMaterial is set non-collidable with Default and collidable with DroppableSurface so dropped items fall through characters and walls but land on tagged floors. A workspace.DescendantAdded listener catches craft-material Tools parented directly to workspace (the Roblox default Backspace drop path) and delegates to DropLandingHelper.waitForLanding, which polls GetTouchingParts plus velocity until the handle settles on a DroppableSurface. Landing triggers RegisterItem with keepModel = true (the Tool itself is the inventory object, not a clone).  Shared (ProximityPickupConfig.luau)All tunable constants for radius, animation durations, merge behaviour, and the landing poll cadence.
