searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Shared loot — not owner-only Any player who steps into the pickup sphere claims the item, regardless of who dropped it or who the shredder owner was. The auto-collect timer (AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY in ShredderConfig, 45 s) returns unclaimed floor materials to the owner via ProximityPickupServer.Claim. If owner-only pickup is ever needed, the RegisterItem signature must be extended with an owner: Player? parameter and the zone.Touched handler must gate on it (see audit comment PP6 in ProximityPickupServer).  DroppableSurface tagging — no code change needed. Any BasePart tagged "DroppableSurface" in CollectionService is automatically assigned the DroppableSurface collision group at runtime via GetInstanceAddedSignal. To make a new floor or shelf surface catchable, tag it in Studio only.  Collision groups are registered in one place. CollisionGroups.luau (ServerStorage/SharedModules) is the sole registrar and owns the full collidability matrix. Besides DroppedMaterial/DroppableSurface, it defines Character (every character BasePart, assigned by CharacterCollisionService) and WeaponProjectile (thrown charges, assigned by ServerProjectile). Because characters now live in their own group rather than Default, dropped materials and projectiles both pass through players while still colliding with world geometry. Any system that needs a new group or a new pair rule should edit CollisionGroups.luau, not call PhysicsService directly.  keepModel semantics: when keepModel = true (the DroppedToolService path), the registered part is the actual Tool that will go into the player's Backpack — RegisterItem will not destroy it. The callback sets tool.Parent = player.Backpack. When keepModel = false (the shredder path), the server clones the template, registers the clone, and the callback grants a fresh clone again; the floor handle is destroyed after claim.  Zone placement: pickup zones are parented to workspace.PickupZones (not to the item part). This prevents "trying to set locked parent!" physics warnings when the zone is destroyed at claim time while the item is still mid-float.  _TryMerge skips keepModel items: the merge logic will not absorb a keepModel item into another, because merging would destroy one of the actual inventory objects. Only non-keepModel handles (shredder clones) are eligible for merging.  Late-joining players: ProximityPickupServer has a Players.PlayerAdded listener that replays all currently "Unclaimed" PickupItemReady events to the new client, so items already on the floor will show their hover effect for late joiners.

searchDocs.title: Buckets​
searchDocs.content: Each period (Daily or Weekly) rotates in a fixed count of quests per category, set by QuestConfig.Counts:  Scope	Personal	PartyDaily	1	2 Weekly	1	1  Personal quests credit only the player who performed the action (e.g. collecting junk).Party quests credit every player in the server for ownerless world events (enemy kills, train distance) — a shared team objective, but the reward is still claimed and paid out per player.

searchDocs.title: Global rotation​
searchDocs.content: The active quest ids for a scope are never stored — they're recomputed deterministically by QuestState.selectQuests(scope, periodIndex) from the period index alone: a seeded Fisher-Yates shuffle (distinct large-prime seeds per category so Personal and Party picks don't correlate) over the sorted id pool for that scope+category, sliced to Counts, then re-sorted for stable display order. Given the same periodIndex, every machine — client or server, any server in the universe — produces the identical set. Only progress, claimed flags, period indices, and lifetime stats persist on the PlayerQuests profile; the set itself is derived, not saved.

searchDocs.title: Period math​
searchDocs.content: Period indices come from os.time() (UTC), never client input:  Daily rolls at 00:00 local (QuestConfig.DailyResetOffset): QuestState.dayIndex(now) = floor((now - DailyResetOffset) / 86400).Weekly rolls Monday 00:00 local (QuestConfig.WeeklyResetOffset, a 4-day base offset — the Unix epoch was a Thursday, so shifting 4 days aligns week starts to Mondays): QuestState.weekIndex(now) = floor((now - WeeklyResetOffset) / 604800).Both offsets are derived from QuestConfig.ResetTimezoneOffset — a fixed seconds-from-UTC offset that defines the timezone "midnight" is measured in (pre-launch default: US Eastern, -5 * 3600). It's a fixed offset, so it does not track daylight saving. Set it to 0 for pure UTC resets. DailyResetOffset = -ResetTimezoneOffset; WeeklyResetOffset = 345600 - ResetTimezoneOffset.QuestState.dailyExpiresAt / weeklyExpiresAt compute the unix timestamp the current period ends at, sent to the client for a live countdown (no client-side period math needed).

searchDocs.title: Season quests​
searchDocs.content: A fifth Scope = "Season" exists alongside Daily/Weekly, dedicated to feeding the Battle Pass. It doesn't rotate like the other scopes — QuestState.selectQuests("Season", periodIndex) returns the entire curated set (Personal ids then Party ids, each sorted), not a Counts-limited shuffle-and-slice — so every Season quest is active for the whole month. Its period index is BattlePassState.seasonIndex(now) (a calendar-month index), not a quest-owned index, so a season's quests reset in lockstep with the battle pass season itself: the profile's SeasonPeriod/SeasonProgress/SeasonClaimed fields follow the exact same ensureCurrent rollover/auto-grant-sweep pattern as Daily/Weekly. The shipped pool (SeasonJunk, SeasonKills, SeasonDistance) pays Coins = 0, Exp = 0 and a large BPExp (3000 each) — Season quests exist purely to move the battle pass track, not the coin/XP economy.  Any quest, of any scope, can additionally carry an optional Reward.BPExp: number? — daily/weekly quests in the shipped pool pay smaller BPExp amounts alongside their normal coins/exp, so ordinary questing keeps the pass moving too, not just the Season set.

searchDocs.title: Attribution​
searchDocs.content: Two entry points on QuestManager, mirroring XPManager.AddXP / AddPartyXP:  QuestManager.ReportProgress(actor, metricKey, amount) — an actor-driven metric (junk collection). Bumps the actor's own Lifetime metric total, advances the actor's Personal quests for that metric, and fans the same amount out to every online player's Party quests for that metric (a Personal action still counts toward the team's Party objectives).QuestManager.ReportPartyProgress(metricKey, amount) — an ownerless world metric (enemy died, train distance ticked). No single actor, so only Party quests advance, but every online player's own Lifetime metric total is bumped and every player is individually replicated.  Either path calls ensureCurrent first (rolls any elapsed period before applying progress) and only replicates (QuestStateSync) to players whose progress actually changed.

searchDocs.title: Claim + auto-grant sweep​
searchDocs.content: Manual claim — Packets.ReqClaimQuest(questId) invokes QuestManager.ClaimQuest(player, questId), which validates (profile loaded → quest exists → quest is in the currently active set for its scope → progress ≥ target → not already claimed) and returns (ok, reasonCode, coinsGranted, expGranted). The claimed flag is set before the reward is granted, so a re-entrant/duplicate call cannot double-pay — the second call fails fast with ALREADY_CLAIMED.Auto-grant sweep — ensureCurrent (called on join, before every progress report/claim, and on the periodic rollover tick) detects when a scope's stored period index differs from the current index. Before resetting that scope's Progress/Claimed maps to the new period, it walks the old set (QuestState.selectQuests(scope, oldPeriodIndex)) and grants the reward for any quest that was completed but never claimed. Nothing is lost — a player who finishes a quest right before rotation and never opens the claim UI is still paid.Both paths share one grantReward function, which — after paying coins/exp — fires Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted(player, quest.Reward). This is how the Battle Pass accrues EXP: BattlePassManager connects to this signal and reads reward.BPExp off the payload, so it sees every grant regardless of whether it came from a manual claim or an auto-grant sweep.

searchDocs.title: Sources​
searchDocs.content: QuestSourcesLoader.server.luau (gameplay-only — safe to run in the lobby place, where these events simply never fire) wires the three QuestConfig.Metrics to their gameplay triggers:  Metric	Category	TriggerEnemyKills	Party	Humanoid.Died on any CollectionService-tagged QuestConfig.ENEMY_TAG ("EnemyNPC") model — one Janitor per tracked enemy. DistanceTravelled	Party	A recurring task.wait(QuestConfig.DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS) loop credits QuestConfig.DISTANCE_PER_TICK while Signals.SetTrainState reports the train running. JunkCollected	Personal	Signals.OnJunkCollected — fired by JunkService once per successful finalized junk grab (collector, junkId).  Adding a quest that reuses one of these Metric keys needs no source code change — only a new entry in QuestConfig.Quests. Wiring a brand-new metric needs one new source hookup in QuestSourcesLoader (see Tune Quests).

searchDocs.title: Perk seam​
searchDocs.content: profile.Data.Lifetime is a { [key]: number } table that is never reset by rollover — distinct from the per-period Progress maps. advancePlayer bumps Lifetime["QuestsCompleted"] by 1 on every below-target → at-target transition, and both ReportProgress/ReportPartyProgress bump Lifetime["metric:" .. metricKey] by the raw reported amount. QuestManager.GetLifetimeStat(player, key) reads it (0 if absent). This is a deliberate seam for a future PerkConfig unlock criterion (e.g. "unlock this perk after QuestsCompleted >= 25) — not wired to any perk this cycle.

searchDocs.title: Client​
searchDocs.content: QuestClient.luau is a GUI-agnostic read-model, same shape as PerkClient: it caches the authoritative QuestStateSync snapshot, recomputes the active set client-side with the same QuestState.selectQuests the server uses (so client and server never disagree on which quests are active), and exposes QuestView descriptors (Id, Scope, Category, DisplayName, Description, Icon, Metric, Target, Progress, IsComplete, IsClaimed, IsClaimable, RewardCoins, RewardExp, ExpiresAt) via GetQuests/GetActiveQuests/GetCompletedQuests/GetQuest, plus GetLifetimeStat and a Claim(questId) fire-and-forget command. A Changed signal fires on every snapshot update for consumers to repaint. No GUI ships this cycle — a future screen requires QuestClient and subscribes to Changed, exactly like PerkClient.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: sequenceDiagram participant Source as QuestSourcesLoader participant Manager as QuestManager (server) participant Client as QuestClient (owning client) Note over Source,Manager: REPORT Source->>Manager: ReportProgress(actor, metric, amt) / ReportPartyProgress(metric, amt) Manager->>Manager: ensureCurrent() — roll elapsed periods first Manager->>Manager: advancePlayer() bumps Progress[questId] (clamped to Target) alt progress changed Manager->>Client: QuestStateSync(periods, expiry, progress, claimed, lifetime) end Note over Manager: COMPLETE (progress[questId] >= Target) Manager->>Manager: bumpLifetime("QuestsCompleted", 1) on the below→at-target transition Client->>Client: QuestView.IsClaimable becomes true (IsComplete and not IsClaimed) Note over Client,Manager: CLAIM Client->>Manager: ReqClaimQuest(questId) Manager->>Manager: validate (active set, progress >= Target, not claimed) Manager->>Manager: claimed[questId] = true (BEFORE grant — idempotent guard) Manager->>Manager: CoinManager.AddCoins(.., "Quest:"..questId); XPManager.AddXP(..); Signals.OnQuestRewardGranted:Fire(player, reward) Manager-->>Client: (ok, reasonCode, coinsGranted, expGranted) Manager->>Client: QuestStateSync (reconciled snapshot)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — QuestConfig.luau is the single tuning surface: STORE_NAME, period offsets, rollover/tick cadence, the Metrics key registry, Counts per scope/category, and the Quests pool (Scope — "Daily" | "Weekly" | "Season", Category, Metric, Target, DisplayName, Description, optional Icon, Reward { Coins, Exp, BPExp? }).  Shared — QuestState.luau is pure, side-effect-free: dayIndex/weekIndex/dailyExpiresAt/weeklyExpiresAt (period math) and selectQuests (deterministic global rotation), plus isComplete/isClaimable helpers. Both server and client require it directly so they never disagree.  Shared — QuestResultCodes.luau is the frozen result-code enum returned by ClaimQuest (OK=0, NO_PROFILE=1, UNKNOWN_QUEST=2, NOT_ACTIVE=3, NOT_COMPLETE=4, ALREADY_CLAIMED=5).  Server — QuestManager.luau owns the PlayerQuests ProfileStore profile (one session per player, key = UserId), place-agnostic like PerkManager (runs in both lobby and gameplay places so the lobby can display quests and pay out claims). Exposes ReportProgress, ReportPartyProgress, ClaimQuest, GetLifetimeStat, and Initialize (wires the profile lifecycle, the ReqClaimQuest handler, and the ROLLOVER_CHECK_SECONDS live-rollover tick). Registers a flush callback with PersistenceRegistry for BindToClose safety.  Server — QuestSystemLoader.server.luau calls QuestManager.Initialize() once per server (place-agnostic).  Server — QuestSourcesLoader.server.luau is gameplay-only: wires EnemyKills, DistanceTravelled, and JunkCollected into QuestManager.ReportProgress/ReportPartyProgress (see Sources). Does not call Initialize.  Client — QuestClient.luau is the GUI-agnostic data layer (see Client above).

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: All tuning lives in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/QuestConfig.luau. searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Changing STORE_NAME orphans saved quest data QuestConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerQuests") is the ProfileStore key for progress, claimed flags, and the never-reset Lifetime table. Changing it points every player at a brand-new, empty profile — all prior quest progress and lifetime stats are orphaned (not deleted, just unreachable). It must stay identical in the lobby and gameplay places for the cross-place session handoff to share the same record.  Personal progress from ReportProgress also advances Party quests ReportProgress(actor, metricKey, amount) is not Personal-only — it fans the same amount out to every online player's Party quests for that metric, then additionally advances the actor's Personal quests. A quest author reusing a Personal-sourced metric (JunkCollected) for a new Party quest gets it "for free" — no new source wiring needed.  The active set query needs the correct period index QuestState.selectQuests takes a periodIndex, not a timestamp. Always derive it via QuestState.dayIndex/weekIndex(os.time()) (server) or read it from the cached QuestStateSync snapshot (client, via QuestClient) — never hardcode or guess an index.

searchDocs.title: Core loop​
searchDocs.content: Enqueue — player spends materials immediately (pay-on-enqueue, not pay-on-complete) to queue the next level of an eligible node. If nothing is active, the job just enqueued starts immediately.Advance — a server tick burns bench fuel and advances the active job's elapsed time. Progress pauses whenever fuel hits 0; it resumes the instant fuel is added back.Complete — when elapsed >= duration, the node's level is recorded, Signals.OnResearchLevelUp fires, and the next queued job (if any) becomes active.Refuel — a player feeds a held Energy tool into the bench via a second ProximityPrompt; the tool's tier maps to a fuel amount (ResearchConfig.EnergyFuelValue).Cancel — a player cancels a specific level of a node (queued or active); see Cascade-cancel below — this is the trickiest part of the system.  Because there is one shared queue and one shared fuel pool for the whole server, this is explicitly a co-op system: any player at the bench can enqueue, cancel, or refuel, and progress benefits everyone.

searchDocs.title: Leveled nodes vs. recipe nodes​
searchDocs.content: Every entry in ResearchConfig.Nodes is a Node with MaxLevel and a Levels table ({ [1] = {Cost, Duration}, [2] = ..., ... }, one entry per level). Two shapes exist:  Leveled upgrade nodes have an Effect ({Type = "StatBuff", Key, PerLevel} or {Type = "FuelEfficiency", DrainPerLevel}). Each completed level contributes to a running total recomputed by ResearchEffectsDispatcher (see Buff/unlock folders).Recipe nodes have Effect = nil. Completing level 1 (recipe nodes are always MaxLevel = 1) writes only a ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> BoolValue; there is no buff to compute. The shipped example is RepeaterRifle, which demonstrates the shape of a pure recipe node but has no Workbench recipe wired to it yet in the shipped WorkbenchConfig. The one recipe gate actually in use — CraftSMG's RequiresNode = "Durability_T1" — instead points at a leveled StatBuff node, showing that any node id can gate a recipe, not just Effect = nil ones. See Workbench Crafting for the consumer side.  A node may declare Prereq (another node's id) and PrereqLevel (default 1) — the prereq node must have reached at least that level before this node accepts enqueues (ResearchState.isEligible).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Client (ResearchGuiController) Server (ResearchService) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ── OPEN ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player walks within INTERACT_DISTANCE ProximityPrompt fires (ResearchPromptPart) GUI opens; rows built from ResearchConfig.Nodes (grouped by Category, sorted by prereq depth then DisplayName) ──── ReqResearchSnapshot() ──────────────► return serialize(state) ◄── { levels, active, queue, fuel } ────── cache populated; all rows/queue/fuel repainted ── ENQUEUE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player clicks Enqueue on a node row ──── ReqResearchEnqueue(nodeId) ──────────► re-check bench + proximity ResearchState.validateEnqueue (unknown node / prereq locked / at max level / queue full) countMaterial(player, mat) for each cost entry (validate BEFORE consuming) consumeMaterial(...) for each ResearchState.enqueue(...) (starts immediately if idle) broadcast() ◄── (success, reasonCode) ───────────────── ◄── ResearchStateUpdate(state, serverTime) cache updated; rows/queue/fuel repainted ── TICK (every ResearchConfig.TICK_INTERVAL, server Heartbeat) ────────── ResearchState.advance(state, dt, FUEL_BURN_RATE) effectiveDt = min(dt, fuel / burnRate) (progress PAUSES at fuel == 0) active.elapsed += effectiveDt fuel -= effectiveDt * burnRate if elapsed >= duration: levels[nodeId] = targetLevel Signals.OnResearchLevelUp:Fire(nodeId, level) startNext() (pop next queued job) completed levels → always broadcast() otherwise → broadcast() at most every HEARTBEAT_BROADCAST_INTERVAL while active (drift correction only) Client interpolates elapsed/fuel locally between broadcasts using the known burn rate + synced server clock (Workspace:GetServerTimeNow()) ── LEVEL-UP EFFECT (ResearchEffectsDispatcher) ────────────────────────── Signals.OnResearchLevelUp:Fire(nodeId, level) ──► republish(): recompute ResearchBuffs from ResearchService.GetLevels() (StatBuff sums PerLevel*level per key; FuelEfficiency multiplies DrainPerLevel^level across all nodes with that effect type) publish ResearchUnlocked/<nodeId> BoolValue if level >= 1 Next tier becomes eligible because ResearchState.isEligible now passes ── CANCEL (see Cascade-cancel below) ──────────────────────────────────── Player clicks Cancel on the active job or a queued row ──── ReqResearchCancel(nodeId, fromLevel) ► ResearchState.cancel(state, nodeId, fromLevel) → (activeRefund?, queuedRefund) queuedRefund ejected at fraction 1.0 activeRefund (if any) ejected at ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION (0.5) broadcast() ◄── (success, reasonCode) ───────────────── ── REFUEL ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player clicks Refuel (or triggers RefuelPromptPart) ──── ReqResearchRefuel() ──────────────────► EnergyToolHelper.GatherEnergyTools(player) tier = EnergyToolHelper.GetEnergyTier(tool) value = EnergyFuelValue[tier] or 0 EnergyToolHelper.ConsumeTool(player, tool) ResearchState.refuel(state, value, FUEL_CAP) broadcast() ◄── (success, reasonCode) ─────────────────

searchDocs.title: Cascade-cancel​
searchDocs.content: Cancelling is keyed by (nodeId, fromLevel) — the target level of the specific job the player clicked Cancel on (the active job's targetLevel, or a specific queued row's targetLevel). ResearchState.cancel does not cancel just that one job:  Every queued job of the same node with targetLevel >= fromLevel is removed and its full cost refunded (fraction 1.0 — no penalty).If the active job belongs to the same node and active.targetLevel >= fromLevel, it is cancelled too, and its cost is refunded at ResearchConfig.ACTIVE_REFUND_FRACTION (0.5 — the "partial progress lost" penalty). If the active job was cancelled, the next queued job (of any node) immediately becomes active with elapsed = 0.  The reasoning: levels are sequential and dependent — you cannot legally hold "Durability_T1 level 3" without level 2 and level 1 having already resolved (pendingLevel stacks consecutively). Cancelling a lower level therefore must also cancel every already-queued higher level of that node, or the queue would contain an orphaned level 3 with no level 2 underneath it.  Concretely, with Durability_T1 active at level 1 and level 2 queued behind it:  Cancelling from level 1 (the active job's row) cancels both: the active level-1 job gets 50% of its cost back, the queued level-2 job gets 100% back, and the queue's next job (if any, possibly for a different node) starts immediately.Cancelling from level 2 (the queued row) cancels only the queued level-2 job (100% refund) — level 1 keeps advancing untouched, because active.targetLevel (1) >= fromLevel (2) is false.  If neither the queue nor the active job matches, ReqResearchCancel returns NOTHING_QUEUED and nothing is refunded. Refunds are ejected at the bench via MaterialEjector along the same TrajectoryPoints → SpawnPoint → scattered LandingPoint arc used by the old Tech Tree (ported verbatim into ResearchConfig).

searchDocs.title: Fuel and pause behavior​
searchDocs.content: Fuel is a single server-wide reserve, capped at ResearchConfig.FUEL_CAP (100).While a job is active, fuel burns at ResearchConfig.FUEL_BURN_RATE (1.0/sec) — burn only happens while a job is active; an idle bench (no active job) never burns fuel.ResearchState.advance clamps effectiveDt = min(dt, fuel / burnRate) so a job's elapsed only ever grows in step with fuel actually spent — the moment fuel reaches 0, elapsed stops advancing (the job pauses, it does not fail or lose progress). Refueling resumes it on the next tick.Refueling is Energy-tool based: ResearchService.Initialize's ReqResearchRefuel handler reuses the existing ServerStorage/SharedModules/EnergyToolHelper.luau (GatherEnergyTools/GetEnergyTier/ConsumeTool) — the same helper the Train Fuel and Train Shield recharge flows use — rather than hand-rolling Tool-attribute detection. It takes the first Energy tool found (backpack, then equipped), maps its Tier (1–5) through ResearchConfig.EnergyFuelValue (20/35/55/80/110), consumes the tool, and adds the value to fuel (clamped to FUEL_CAP).  Fuel and queue are shared, not per-player There is exactly one fuel value and one queue for the entire server. Any player at the bench can enqueue against the shared queue, refuel the shared reserve, or cancel any job — including jobs another player paid for. This is intentional (co-op resource pooling, same spirit as the old Tech Tree's shared pools) but means griefing-by-cancel is possible; there is no per-player ownership check.

searchDocs.title: Buff/unlock folders​
searchDocs.content: ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau is the sole writer of two ReplicatedStorage folders, both recomputed from scratch (not delta-accumulated) on every Signals.OnResearchLevelUp:  Folder	Shape	Written by	Read byReplicatedStorage/ResearchBuffs	Attributes on the folder itself: one numeric attribute per StatBuff.Key (summed PerLevel * level across all nodes with that key), plus FuelEfficiency (product of DrainPerLevel ^ level across all FuelEfficiency nodes; 1 = no effect)	ResearchEffectsDispatcher	TrainShieldManager (MaxHP), TrainFuelManager (FuelEfficiency) ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked	One BoolValue (named by nodeId, Value = true) per node at level ≥ 1 — recipe nodes included	ResearchEffectsDispatcher	WorkbenchService (server gate), WorkbenchGuiController (client greying)  Recompute-from-levels means totals are always correct with no drift risk, at the cost of iterating every node in ResearchConfig.Nodes on every level-up (cheap — the node count is small). ResearchEffectsDispatcher also seeds both folders once at server boot (before any player joins) so WaitForChild consumers never race an empty folder.

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — Configs/ResearchConfig.luau is the single tuning surface: bench tag/interaction distances, queue/fuel/refund constants, the ported refund-arc trajectory constants, and the Nodes table. See Config knobs.  Shared — ResearchResultCodes.luau is a frozen result-code enum (NONE, NO_BENCH, TOO_FAR, UNKNOWN_NODE, PREREQ_LOCKED, AT_MAX_LEVEL, QUEUE_FULL, NOT_ENOUGH_MATERIALS, NOTHING_QUEUED, NO_FUEL_ITEM, INVALID_REQUEST) shared by server and client so neither side uses raw string reasons.  Shared — ResearchState.luau is a pure, stateless module with no Roblox service calls: newState, levelOf, pendingLevel, isEligible, validateEnqueue, enqueue, cancel (cascade logic), advance (tick), refuel, serialize. Both the server (authority) and the client GUI (asState() cast over the cached snapshot, for greying/afford checks) call the same pure helpers, so the rules can never drift between sides. validateEnqueue deliberately does not check whether the player holds the materials — that check is server-only and layered on top by ResearchService.  Server — ResearchService.luau (ServerStorage/SharedModules/) is the authoritative owner of ResearchState.State. It is a ModuleScript, not a .server.luau Script — see ModuleScript + loader split below. Initialize() (idempotent, guarded by a boot flag) wires all four packet handlers plus the RunService.Heartbeat tick loop. GetLevels() exposes the live levels table for ResearchEffectsDispatcher to read.  Server — ResearchSystemLoader.server.luau (ServerScriptService/) is a one-line boot script: require(...ResearchService) then ResearchService.Initialize(). Mirrors PerkManager.luau / PerkSystemLoader.server.luau.  Server — ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau (ServerScriptService/) connects Signals.OnResearchLevelUp and republishes both buff/unlock folders from scratch. See Buff/unlock folders.  Client — ResearchGuiController.client.luau builds the entire ResearchGui ScreenGui in code (no Studio template) and opens it via the bench ResearchPromptPart ProximityPrompt. Node rows are grouped by Category (fixed order Train/Player/Equipment/Recipes) and sorted by prereq depth then DisplayName. A side panel shows the active job (MotionMaster-spring-driven progress bar, Cancel button) and the queue (each entry independently cancellable), plus a fuel gauge (also spring-driven) with a "PAUSED" badge shown whenever fuel is at 0 while a job is active, and a Refuel button. Between ResearchStateUpdate broadcasts, interpolated() fast-forwards the active job's elapsed time and the fuel gauge locally using the known burn rate and the synced server clock, so the bars move smoothly every frame rather than stepping only on broadcast. Uses a Janitor per GUI open/close lifecycle (springs + the per-frame RenderStepped connection are recreated on open and destroyed on close).

searchDocs.title: ModuleScript + loader split (caution)​
searchDocs.content: ResearchService is a ModuleScript, booted by a separate loader ResearchService.luau lives under ServerStorage/SharedModules/ as a ModuleScript, not ServerScriptService/ResearchService.server.luau. This is deliberate: Roblox's require() only accepts ModuleScript instances — a *.server.luau file compiles to a plain Script, which can never be required by another script. Because ResearchEffectsDispatcher.server.luau needs to call ResearchService.GetLevels(), ResearchService has to be a ModuleScript. The split mirrors the existing PerkManager.luau (ModuleScript, state + Initialize()) / PerkSystemLoader.server.luau (thin boot Script) pattern: ResearchService.luau defines state + an idempotent Initialize() that wires packets and the tick loop, but does nothing until Initialize() is called.ResearchSystemLoader.server.luau is the only script that calls ResearchService.Initialize(), exactly once per server. If you ever see require() fail on a *.server.luau/*.client.luau path in this codebase, this is the fix: split the requirable state into a ModuleScript and add a thin loader Script that calls its Initialize().

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Manual, one-time Studio work — none of this is created automatically by code:  Bench Model. One Model tagged ResearchBench (CollectionService) with its PrimaryPart set.Refund-arc trajectory. A child Model named TrajectoryPoints (tagged PlacementIgnore, per the Placement "tag the CollisionBox only" rule) holding two BasePart children: SpawnPoint (arc start, the bench's output mouth) and LandingPoint (arc end, the floor drop zone). If missing, MaterialEjector degrades gracefully and drops refunded pieces at the bench pivot instead of erroring.Research prompt. A child BasePart named ResearchPromptPart holding a ProximityPrompt — opens the GUI. MaxActivationDistance is set to ResearchConfig.INTERACT_DISTANCE by the client controller at runtime.Refuel prompt. A separate child BasePart named RefuelPromptPart holding a ProximityPrompt — feeds a held Energy tool into the bench.Material templates. ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials must hold Wood and Metal Tool templates with IsCraftMaterial = true and ItemType attributes set — shared with the Shredder and Workbench, no duplication needed.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Server re-checks proximity on every request The client's ProximityPrompt distance is never trusted. ReqResearchEnqueue, ReqResearchCancel, and ReqResearchRefuel all re-run isNearBench on the server using INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE. A player invoking from range receives TOO_FAR.  Validate-then-consume ordering on enqueue ReqResearchEnqueue calls countMaterial for every cost entry before calling consumeMaterial for any of them. If the player is short on any single material, nothing is consumed — there is no partial-payment state.  Cost is paid on enqueue, not on completion Unlike the old Tech Tree's pooled-contribution model, materials are deducted the instant a level is successfully enqueued — the queue holds already-paid-for jobs. Cancelling is therefore the only way to get materials back, and only at the refund fractions described in Cascade-cancel.  Cascade-cancel refunds every dependent queued level, not just the targeted one See Cascade-cancel in full above — cancelling a lower level of a node also cancels every already-queued higher level of that same node (100% refund each), because a higher level cannot legally exist without the lower one having resolved.  Fuel and queue are server-wide, not per-player See Fuel and pause behavior — any player at the bench can cancel a job another player paid for. There is no per-player ownership check by design (co-op pooling), but it is a known griefing surface.

searchDocs.title: Threat model​
searchDocs.content: A reserved server (created by the lobby via TeleportService:ReserveServerAsync) already blocks the normal server-list join and rejects follow-a-friend joins. Two vectors remain:  Launching the gameplay placeId directly, landing in a non-reserved public server (game.PrivateServerId == "").A non-roster user reaching a reserved server with a stale access code or an expired session.  JoinGuard closes both by validating every joiner against an authoritative roster keyed off the engine-set game.PrivateServerId, which cannot be spoofed from the client — so authorization can never be forged.

searchDocs.title: Cross-place contract​
searchDocs.content: Coordination between the lobby and gameplay places goes through two MemoryStore hash maps (fast, TTL-native, built for ephemeral cross-server state — unlike DataStore, which is slower, rate-limited, and has no native expiry). SessionStore is the only module that touches them.

searchDocs.title: Roster — keyed by privateServerId​
searchDocs.content: { partyId, authorizedUserIds: {number}, leaderUserId, createdAt }   The lobby writes this immediately before TeleportAsync, so it exists by the time the gameplay server boots. SessionStore.GetRoster reads it on boot with a short retry loop (GET_RETRIES × GET_RETRY_WAIT) to cover the boot/write race. SessionCoordinator mutates it via RemoveFromRoster when a grace window expires, and clears it entirely via ClearRoster on run end.

searchDocs.title: Session pointer — keyed by userId​
searchDocs.content: { placeId, accessCode, privateServerId, jobId, status, heartbeatAt }   This lets the lobby route a rejoiner back to the exact live server. The lobby seeds placeId/accessCode/privateServerId at teleport time, obtaining accessCode + privateServerId from the server-only TeleportService:ReserveServerAsync(gameplayPlaceId). Gameplay fills jobId and heartbeats the entry via SessionStore.RefreshPointer(userId, jobId), which uses UpdateAsync to stamp only jobId/status/heartbeatAt onto the already-seeded entry — it deliberately returns without creating a pointer if the lobby never seeded one, since gameplay never learns the raw accessCode and must not fabricate it.  jobId is informational/liveness only — it is not used to route the rejoin. On the lobby side, rejoin must set opts.ReservedServerAccessCode = accessCode alone; the current engine API forbids combining ReservedServerAccessCode with ServerInstanceId or ShouldReserveServer on the same TeleportOptions. The access code alone resolves to the one reserved server it was issued for.  TeleportData may additionally carry { partyId, rosterVersion } for diagnostics/logging — never trusted for authorization.

searchDocs.title: Components (this repo)​
searchDocs.content: JoinGuard (src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/JoinGuard.luau) — pure authorization decisions and the lobby-bounce. IsReservedServer() is true only for a non-empty PrivateServerId with PrivateServerOwnerId == 0 (rejects both a directly-launched public server and a VIP server). IsAuthorized(roster, userId) checks roster.authorizedUserIds. BounceToLobby(player) retry-teleports to DisruptionConfig.LOBBY_PLACE_ID, reusing the same config and retry count as the disruption system.SessionStore (src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/SessionStore.luau) — the pcall-wrapped MemoryStore I/O described above (GetRoster, RefreshRosterTTL, RemoveFromRoster, ClearRoster, RefreshPointer, ClearPointer). Holds no game logic.SessionState (src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/SessionState.luau) — in-memory (this-server-only) capture/restore of a player's ephemeral run state across a disconnect. RegisterProvider(name, capture, restore) lets other managers plug in (see Grace/restore flow below). Capture(player) must run synchronously from PlayerRemoving, before any deferred teardown clears state. HoldForGrace/HasGrace/TakeBundle/Discard manage the grace window via a Janitor per held entry.SessionCoordinator (src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/SessionCoordinator.luau) — wires everything: boot-time roster read + bypass decision, PlayerAdded/PlayerRemoving handlers, the heartbeat loop, and the leave-intent packet handler. The only module with Initialize().SessionClient (src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SessionClient.client.luau) — forwards Signals.LeaveToLobbyRequested (fired by a menu "Leave to lobby" button) to Packets.ReqLeaveToLobby. Does no teleporting itself; the server owns that.SessionSystemLoader (src/ServerScriptService/SessionSystemLoader.server.luau) — the entry point. Registers AmmoManager.Snapshot/RestorePool and HealthManager.GetHealth/SetHealth as SessionState providers (under the keys "ammo" and "health"), then calls SessionCoordinator.Initialize().

searchDocs.title: Grace/restore flow​
searchDocs.content: On an unexpected PlayerRemoving (no prior ReqLeaveToLobby), SessionCoordinator.handleLeave synchronously calls SessionState.Capture(player) — which clones every Tool from the player's Backpack and Character into a per-user folder under a ServerStorage.SessionToolCache folder, then runs every registered provider's capture (ammo pool snapshot, current health) — and holds the bundle via SessionState.HoldForGrace(userId, bundle, SessionConfig.GRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS, onExpire). The player stays on the roster while held.  Rejoin within the window — JoinGuard re-admits the player (still authorized); SessionCoordinator.handleJoin sees SessionState.HasGrace(userId) and calls scheduleRestore, which waits for CharacterAdded (or applies immediately if a character already exists) and, deferred one frame so HealthManager's full-health CharacterAdded reset runs first, calls SessionState.Restore(player, bundle). That reattaches the cached Tools to the (fresh) Backpack and runs every provider's restore (AmmoManager.RestorePool, HealthManager.SetHealth). The player respawns at the normal train/party spawn — character position is never captured or restored.Grace expires without a rejoin — the task.delay in HoldForGrace fires onExpire, which clears the session pointer and removes the user from the roster so they can no longer rejoin; the bundle's Janitor destroys the cached Tools folder.Clean leave (ReqLeaveToLobby) — SessionCoordinator marks the userId in cleanLeaving before bouncing, so the ensuing PlayerRemoving calls SessionState.Discard (no grace hold at all) and clears the pointer + roster entry immediately.Run end — when PlayerRemoving leaves the server empty (#Players:GetPlayers() <= 1, checked before removal completes) or on game:BindToClose, runEnded clears the roster and every remaining pointer for this privateServerId. No live-server rejoin is possible once the run has ended — a later rejoin attempt lands in the normal lobby flow instead.  SessionState's tools-folder cleanup uses an explicit Janitor index (Janitor:Add(toolsFolder, "Destroy", TOOLS_JANITOR_INDEX)), not the implicit form, specifically so TakeBundle can detach the folder without destroying it: it calls Janitor:RemoveNoClean(TOOLS_JANITOR_INDEX) (clears the index with no side effect) rather than Janitor:Remove (which runs the cleanup method immediately — that would destroy the very folder the caller is about to restore Tools from).  A SESSION_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS loop in SessionCoordinator periodically refreshes the roster TTL and every present, authorized player's pointer TTL, so a live run never expires while a dead run (crashed process, no clean shutdown) self-expires after ENTRY_TTL_SECONDS.  In Studio, SessionConfig.BYPASS_GUARD_IN_STUDIO makes SessionCoordinator authorize everyone unconditionally (no reserved server or lobby exists locally) while still exercising the grace/restore code paths.  sequenceDiagram participant Player participant Coordinator as SessionCoordinator participant State as SessionState participant Guard as JoinGuard participant Store as SessionStore (MemoryStore) Note over Player,Coordinator: UNEXPECTED DROP Player--xCoordinator: PlayerRemoving (no prior ReqLeaveToLobby) Coordinator->>State: Capture(player) — Tools + ammo + health Coordinator->>State: HoldForGrace(userId, bundle, GRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS, onExpire) alt Rejoin within GRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS Player->>Coordinator: PlayerAdded (still on roster) Coordinator->>Guard: IsAuthorized(roster, userId) Guard-->>Coordinator: true Coordinator->>State: HasGrace(userId) == true Coordinator->>State: scheduleRestore -> TakeBundle + Restore (on CharacterAdded) State-->>Player: Tools reattached; ammo + health restored at train spawn else Grace window expires State->>State: onExpire fires Coordinator->>Store: ClearPointer(userId); RemoveFromRoster(privateServerId, userId) Note over Player: A later join is now unauthorized -> Guard.BounceToLobby ejects them end

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: All tuning lives in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SessionConfig.luau. Its names and GAMEPLAY_PLACE_ID/map-name values are shared verbatim with the separate lobby project via this contract.  Field	EffectGRACE_WINDOW_SECONDS	How long (120s) a dropped player's slot + cached health/ammo/Tools are held for a live-server rejoin before being discarded. SESSION_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS	How often (30s) the live gameplay server refreshes the roster + session-pointer TTLs in MemoryStore. ENTRY_TTL_SECONDS	TTL (90s, 3× heartbeat) written on both MemoryStore structures; refreshed every heartbeat, so a server that dies unobserved self-expires roughly this many seconds later. GAMEPLAY_PLACE_ID	This place's PlaceId. Used by the lobby to reserve + teleport in; 0 = unset (fill in before launch). ROSTER_MAP_NAME	MemoryStore hash-map name for the roster ("EJ_SessionRoster"), shared with the lobby project. SESSION_MAP_NAME	MemoryStore hash-map name for the session pointer ("EJ_SessionPointers"), shared with the lobby project. BYPASS_GUARD_IN_STUDIO	When true (default), authorizes everyone in Studio so local playtests work without a reserved server, while still exercising grace/restore logic.

searchDocs.title: Non-goals​
searchDocs.content: Live-server rejoin only — rejoin works only while the reserved server stays alive (≥ 1 member keeps it running). If the server empties, the run ends and rejoiners return to the lobby fresh; there is no shared-world snapshot or run resurrection.No character-position restore — a rejoining player always respawns at the normal train/party spawn.No DataStore for ephemeral state — health/ammo/Tools grace-window state lives only in server memory (SessionState) and is lost if the server itself dies during the grace window; this is a deliberate scope cut, not an oversight.The lobby implementation (reserve, roster write, rejoin UI) is a separate project; only the contract above is specified here.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Join: SettingsManager.onPlayerAdded(player) └─> PlayerStore:StartSessionAsync (ProfileStore, STORE_NAME = "PlayerSettings") ├─> migrateLegacyVolumes(profile) -- copies old Volumes{bus} -> Settings{key}, idempotent ├─> profile:Reconcile() -- fills missing keys from SettingsConfig.GetDefaults() ├─> profile.Data.Settings = SettingsSchema.Sanitize(profile.Data.Settings) └─> Packets.SyncSettings:FireClient(player, profile.Data.Settings) └─> SettingsClient (Packets.SyncSettings.OnClientEvent) └─> for each key: SettingsSchema.Validate -> applyAndNotify ├─> SettingsAppliers.Apply(key, value) -- e.g. Groups.SetVolume └─> Signals.OnSettingChanged:Fire(key, value) (no re-save) Manual change (GUI calls SettingsClient.Set): SettingsClient.Set(key, value) └─> SettingsSchema.Validate(key, value) -- reject unknown key / wrong type / out of range └─> applyAndNotify(key, coerced) ├─> SettingsAppliers.Apply(key, coerced) -- immediate local effect └─> Signals.OnSettingChanged:Fire(key, coerced) └─> scheduleSave(key, coerced) -- debounced 0.25s, coalesces rapid changes └─> Packets.SaveSetting:Fire(key, coerced) └─> SettingsManager (Packets.SaveSetting.OnServerEvent) └─> SettingsSchema.Validate(key, value) -- server re-validates, never trusts client └─> profile.Data.Settings[key] = coerced -- ProfileStore autosaves

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — SettingsConfig (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SettingsConfig.luau)  Pure data, no client dependencies, so the server can require it directly. SettingsConfig.Definitions is the single registry — one entry per setting key, typed as:  export type Definition = { type: "number" | "boolean" | "enum", default: any, category: string, label: string, order: number, min: number?, max: number?, step: number?, options: { string }?, }   SettingsConfig.GetDefaults() returns a fresh { [string]: any } map of every key to its default — this seeds both a brand-new ProfileStore profile and profile:Reconcile() for existing ones. SettingsConfig.VolumeBusByKey maps the four volume setting keys (MasterVolume, MusicVolume, SFXVolume, AmbienceVolume) to their SoundConfig/Groups bus name (Master, BGM, SFX, Ambience) — the one place that mapping is declared, reused by both the migration step and SettingsAppliers. SettingsConfig.STORE_NAME ("PlayerSettings") is the ProfileStore name and must not change without a migration plan, since it is also where the legacy Volumes table is read from.  Shared — SettingsSchema (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SettingsSchema.luau)  The single validator, called identically by server and client so the two sides can never disagree on what's valid:  SettingsSchema.Validate(key, value): (boolean, any) — looks key up in SettingsConfig.Definitions (unknown key is rejected, acting as an allowlist). For "number", rejects non-numbers and NaN, then clamps to [min, max] (open-ended if either bound is nil). For "boolean", requires an exact boolean. For "enum", requires the value to be a member of options. Returns (true, coercedValue) on success, (false, nil) on failure.SettingsSchema.Sanitize(map): { [string]: any } — builds a complete settings map: starts from SettingsConfig.GetDefaults(), then overlays every entry in map that passes Validate. Anything invalid or no longer in the registry (a setting that was removed) is silently dropped. Used by SettingsManager on join so the synced map is never missing a key or carrying a stale one.  Server — SettingsManager (ServerStorage/SharedModules/SettingsManager.luau)  The authority. Owns one ProfileStore session per player (PlayerStore:StartSessionAsync(tostring(player.UserId), ...)), following the same lifecycle pattern as CoinManager/XPManager: kicks the player if the session fails to start, ends the session and re-kicks on OnSessionEnd, and ends the session on PlayerRemoving.  On join (onPlayerAdded), before profile:Reconcile() runs, migrateLegacyVolumes(profile) does a one-time, idempotent copy: for every key in SettingsConfig.VolumeBusByKey, if Settings[key] is still unset and the legacy profile.Data.Volumes[bus] is a valid number, it's validated and copied into Settings[key]. Once a key exists in Settings it is never overwritten from Volumes again, so this is safe to leave running indefinitely — it is a no-op for any profile that has already migrated or that never had legacy Volumes data. The legacy Volumes table itself is left in place (not cleared) after migration.  SettingsManager.Initialize() (called once per server) wires Packets.SaveSetting.OnServerEvent: looks up the player's profile (drops the message if none — e.g. a setting saved before session start finished), checks key is a string, re-validates (key, value) through SettingsSchema.Validate, and on success writes profile.Data.Settings[key] = coerced. There is no explicit save call — ProfileStore autosaves the profile. Any invalid or unknown-key message is silently dropped; the server never trusts the client's claim that a value is valid.  Client — SettingsClient (StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SettingsClient.luau)  The only module the settings GUI talks to. Holds a local cache of every setting's current value and exposes:  SettingsClient.Get(key): any — returns the cached value, or the definition's default if never set.SettingsClient.Set(key, value): boolean — validates via SettingsSchema; on success applies + announces immediately (see applyAndNotify below) and schedules a debounced save; returns false without any side effect if validation fails.SettingsClient.GetAll(): { [string]: any } — a full snapshot keyed by every key in SettingsConfig.Definitions.SettingsClient.GetDefinition(key): SettingsConfig.Definition? — the raw definition, for a GUI to read min/max/step/label/options when building a control.SettingsClient.GetByCategory(): { [string]: { { key, definition } } } — every definition grouped by category and sorted by order within each group; this is what a settings menu iterates to build its tabs/sections (today: "Audio" with 4 entries, order 1-4; "Controls" with 1 entry, CameraSensitivity at order 1).SettingsClient.Init() — connects Packets.SyncSettings.OnClientEvent once; idempotent (a second call is a no-op). Called once by SettingsController.client.luau at startup.  Internally, applyAndNotify(key, value) is the shared path for both the join-sync handler and Set: it writes the cache, calls SettingsAppliers.Apply(key, value), then fires Signals.OnSettingChanged:Fire(key, value). The join-sync path calls only applyAndNotify (never scheduleSave), which is what prevents applying the server's own synced values from looping back into another save.  scheduleSave(key, value) debounces persistence per key: the latest value for that key is stashed in a pending table, and a single task.delay(0.25, ...) per key sends the trailing value via Packets.SaveSetting:Fire(key, value). Rapid changes to the same key (e.g. dragging a volume slider) collapse into one network send 0.25s after the drag settles, rather than one send per frame.  Client — SettingsAppliers (StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SettingsAppliers.luau)  A client-only key -> (value) -> () registry, kept deliberately separate from SettingsConfig so the shared config module stays free of client-only dependencies (Groups, UserSettings()) that the server must never require. Built once at require time:  The four volume keys are wired generically by iterating SettingsConfig.VolumeBusByKey and calling Groups.SetVolume(bus, value) for each.  SettingsAppliers.Apply(key, value) looks up and calls the applier for key, or no-ops silently if the key has no client-side effect (a setting can exist purely for server-side or analytics purposes without ever needing an entry here). CameraSensitivity is a deliberate example of the no-entry-needed case: it has no SettingsAppliers applier because CameraController reads it directly via SettingsClient.Get("CameraSensitivity") at startup and stays live via Signals.OnSettingChanged, rather than reacting through this registry (see Camera).

searchDocs.title: Networking​
searchDocs.content: Packet	Direction	Payload	PurposeSyncSettings	S->C	{ [string]: any }	Full saved settings map, fired once per join by SettingsManager. SaveSetting	C->S	(key: string, value: any)	One setting change, fired by SettingsClient's debounced save; re-validated server-side before being written.  See the Networking Map for these alongside every other packet in the game.

searchDocs.title: Signals​
searchDocs.content: Signal	Producer	PurposeOnSettingChanged	SettingsClient (after every applied change — join-sync and manual Set)	(key: string, value: any). Fires once per key, after the value has already been applied via SettingsAppliers — a listener never observes a not-yet-applied value.  See the Signals Map for the full list.

searchDocs.title: Adding a new setting​
searchDocs.content: Two steps, at most:  Add one entry to SettingsConfig.Definitions — pick a unique key, a type ("number" | "boolean" | "enum"), a default, a category + label for the GUI, an order within that category, and the relevant bounds (min/max/step for "number", options for "enum"). That's enough for the setting to round-trip end to end: it will seed into new profiles, sync on join, validate, and persist.If the setting has a direct client-side effect, add a matching entry to SettingsAppliers's appliers table — a one-argument function that applies value. Skip this step entirely for settings with no client effect (e.g. a server-only gameplay toggle, or something a future system reads via SettingsClient.Get on demand instead of reacting to OnSettingChanged).  No packet, schema, or ProfileStore change is needed for a new setting — SettingsSchema.Validate and SettingsManager are fully generic over the Definitions table.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Never call SettingsAppliers or SettingsManager's internals directly GUI code should only ever call SettingsClient.Get/Set/GetAll/GetDefinition/GetByCategory and listen to Signals.OnSettingChanged. Calling SettingsAppliers.Apply directly skips validation, caching, and persistence — the value will apply visually but never save and will be wiped out by the next join-sync. Calling into SettingsManager from client code is not possible (it's a server-only module) and calling Packets.SaveSetting:Fire directly skips client-side validation and the cache, which desyncs SettingsClient.Get from what the server actually has.  The join-sync path never re-saves. SettingsClient.Init()'s Packets.SyncSettings.OnClientEvent handler calls applyAndNotify directly, not Set — this is intentional and must stay that way, or applying the server's own synced values would immediately re-fire a save back to the server in a feedback loop.SettingsManager.Initialize() re-validates every SaveSetting message. A modified or out-of-date client can fire any (key, value) pair; the server drops anything that fails SettingsSchema.Validate (unknown key, wrong type, out-of-range number) rather than trusting the client's own clamping.Legacy Volumes data is migrated, not deleted. migrateLegacyVolumes copies old per-bus volumes into the generic Settings map once, but the old Volumes table is left on the profile afterward. Don't write new code that reads profile.Data.Volumes — it is dead weight kept only for the migration step, not a second source of truth.Removing a Definitions entry doesn't delete saved data, but does stop syncing it. SettingsSchema.Sanitize drops any key no longer present in Definitions from the map it returns, so a removed setting simply disappears from SyncSettings/GetAll going forward — it does not actively scrub the old key from the ProfileStore document.CameraSensitivity scales GetMouseDelta(), not an engine property. Early exploration considered UserGameSettings.MouseSensitivity, but that property is gated behind the RobloxScript capability (CoreScript-only) and throws "lacking capability RobloxScript" if a game LocalScript writes it. UserInputService.MouseDeltaSensitivity is settable but only scales GetMouseDelta() consumers — it would have had no effect on the old default Roblox camera, which didn't consume GetMouseDelta() for look/rotation at all. That constraint is why the camera itself was rewritten: CameraController is now a fully script-owned Scriptable camera that reads raw UserInputService:GetMouseDelta() every frame and scales it by CameraConfig.MouseLookBaseSpeed * sensitivity, where sensitivity is SettingsClient.Get("CameraSensitivity"), kept live via Signals.OnSettingChanged. See Camera for the consuming side.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Client (ShredderClient) Server (ShredderServer) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── PromptButtonHoldBegan countNonEnergyJunks() > 0 ──── ReqShredderStart(bench) ────► validate: workbench tag, proximity, workbench not locked, cooldown, junk count ShredderMath.ComputeHoldDuration() record session + StartTime ◄── (isValid, duration, code) ─── prompt.HoldDuration = duration PromptButtonHoldEnded → nonce bump (cancels armed session) Prompt.Triggered (hold complete) armedNonce check passes ──── ReqShredderComplete(bench) ──► re-validate: session, workbench match, elapsed >= duration - TOLERANCE, proximity, workbench not locked re-verify junk still owned buildMaterialSequence(junks) destroy junk Tools lock workbench task.spawn(ejectMaterials) ◄── (success, woodCount, metalCount, code) ────────── ejectMaterials(): SplineMove handle P0→arcPeak→landing ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem() CollectionService tag "CraftMaterial" auto-collect loop (0.5 s poll) unlock workbench after ARC_DURATION Shared: ShredderMath (hold duration), ShredderResultCodes (error enum)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (ShredderClient.client.luau)Watches CollectionService for Workbench-tagged models. On each workbench it finds a ProximityPrompts/ShredPromptPart/ProximityPrompt, sets ActionText, HoldDuration, and MaxActivationDistance from config, and wires three connections: PromptButtonHoldBegan (fires ReqShredderStart), PromptButtonHoldEnded (bumps the nonce to cancel), and Triggered (fires ReqShredderComplete only when the nonce matches the armed value). A Backpack and Character Janitor pair keeps HoldDuration in sync whenever junk is added or removed. If the player holds the prompt with zero non-Energy junk, a "info" notification fires and the prompt is briefly disabled.  Server (ShredderServer.server.luau)ReqShredderStart validates the workbench tag, proximity (INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE), workbench lock state, per-player cooldown, and junk availability. It stores a session record (workbench, start time, computed duration, junk snapshot). ReqShredderComplete re-checks all constraints plus timing (elapsed >= duration - HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE), re-validates junk still belongs to the player from the snapshot, builds a shuffled material sequence, destroys all junk Tools, locks the workbench, then spawns ejectMaterials. Ejection animates each handle along a Catmull-Rom spline (MotionMaster.SplineMove) with uniform-disk scatter around LandingPoint, then calls ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem. Overflow beyond MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS is granted directly in scheduler batches. A 0.5 s auto-collect loop sweeps droppedMaterials; after AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY the item is force-claimed to the owner.  Shared (ShredderMath, ShredderResultCodes)ShredderMath.ComputeHoldDuration linearly interpolates hold time between MIN_HOLD_DURATION (1 item) and MAX_HOLD_DURATION (MAX_JUNK_COUNT items). Both client and server call it so the prompt ring and the server timing check always agree. ShredderResultCodes is a frozen enum used by both sides for unambiguous rejection reasons.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Anti-exploit thresholds are sensitive INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE, HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE, and PER_PLAYER_COOLDOWN are the primary barriers against timing exploits and teleport-shredding. Increasing tolerances too far removes protection; tightening them too far breaks legit high-latency players.  Studio asset requirements — all three must be present or the server will warn and abort ejection:  Each workbench Model must be tagged "Workbench" with a PrimaryPart set.Each workbench must contain a child Model named "TrajectoryPoints" (tag it PlacementIgnore) with two invisible, anchored, non-collidable BasePart children: "SpawnPoint" (at the shredder output mouth) and "LandingPoint" (floor landing target).In ReplicatedStorage, a Folder named "CraftingMaterials" must contain Tool templates named "Wood" and "Metal", each with a BasePart child named "Handle". Set CanBeDropped = false on each template.  Nonce guard: the client uses a per-workbench nonce pair (holdNonce, armedNonce) to drop stale ReqShredderComplete calls when the player releases early or changes workbenches mid-hold. Modifying the hold flow must preserve this guard or the server's NO_SESSION rejection will fire spuriously.  Junk snapshot: the server snapshots junk at ReqShredderStart time. ReqShredderComplete re-filters that snapshot to tools still in the player's possession — it does not re-scan the Backpack. This prevents inflation from picking up new junk during the hold.  Energy junk exclusion: only Metal and Wood junk types are consumed and yield output. Energy junk is excluded from both the client count and the server's junk collection helpers.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Player holds Shift (or mobile toggle) │ ▼ SprintController (client) • applySprintIntent() → Packets.StaminaSprintIntent:Fire(true) ──► StaminaManager (server) • sets record.SprintIntent • runs Heartbeat drain/regen • syncs via StaminaStateSync ◄── Packets.StaminaStateSync (serverStamina, serverIsSprinting) ─── • currentStamina = serverStamina • if !serverIsSprinting → setSprinting(false) • Signals.OnStaminaValueChanged:Fire(currentStamina) ──► HUD bar (RenderStepped — every frame) • setSprinting(sprintIntent AND canSprintNow()) • humanoid.WalkSpeed = SprintSpeed / WalkSpeed • tweenFov(SprintFOV / DefaultFOV) • Signals.OnSprintToggled:Fire(isSprinting) ◄── Packets.StaminaBuffSync (infinite, regenMult, usageMult) ────── • Signals.OnStaminaBuffsChanged:Fire(...) ──► HUD / buff icons

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (SprintController.client.luau)  Binds sprint to LeftShift and ButtonB (gamepad) via ContextActionService; a separate MobileSprintToggled signal handles the mobile toggle button.On each RenderStepped tick calls canSprintNow() (wraps SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint) and calls setSprinting accordingly.setSprinting sets humanoid.WalkSpeed, tweens FieldOfView via TweenPlus, and fires Signals.OnSprintToggled.WalkSpeed is set client-side only; there is no server-side speed reconciliation (see audit note S3 in the source).On StaminaStateSync: clamps received stamina, forces sprint off if the server says so, fires Signals.OnStaminaValueChanged for the HUD.On StaminaBuffSync: forwards buff state to Signals.OnStaminaBuffsChanged for UI and icon updates.Resets sprint intent on CharacterRemoving and on WindowFocusReleased.  Server (StaminaManager.luau)  Maintains a StaminaRecord per player (Stamina, IsSprinting, SprintIntent, LastSprintTime, LastSyncTime).On StaminaSprintIntent packet: immediately updates sprint state and calls syncPlayer.Heartbeat loop: clamps dt to MAX_STAMINA_STEP_DT = 0.1 s to prevent large delta spikes. Drains stamina at StaminaDrain * dt * UsageMultiplier while sprinting; regenerates at StaminaRegen * dt * RegenMultiplier after RegenDelay seconds of not sprinting.Syncs to the client when: sprint state changes, stamina hits 0 (forced stop), stamina refills to max, or periodic sync interval (STAMINA_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 s) elapses while stamina is changing.Consults StaminaBuffManager each tick for buff multipliers; resyncs immediately on Signals.OnServerStaminaBuffStateChanged.StaminaManager.RestoreStamina(player, amount) is available for pickup items but has no caller yet.  Shared (SprintValidation.luau)  SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint(humanoid, rules) — returns false if health is 0, MoveDirection magnitude is below MinMoveDirection, the character is moving backward beyond MaxBackwardComponent, or horizontal speed is below MinHorizontalSpeed.Called on both client (canSprintNow) and server (canPlayerSprint) to keep the gate condition identical.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Sprint logic must be mirrored on both sides SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint is the shared gate. If you add a new sprint-blocking condition (e.g. stun), add it to SprintValidation and verify it is called by both SprintController (client) and StaminaManager (server). A condition added only to one side will cause desyncs.  WalkSpeed is client-only. The server does not validate movement speed; a cheating client can move at any speed. If movement integrity becomes necessary, add a server-side speed sanity check.STAMINA_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 s (10 Hz). The server only sends a sync when stamina is actively changing. If stamina is full and the player is standing still, no sync is sent — this is intentional.MAX_STAMINA_STEP_DT = 0.1 s clamp. The server caps the Heartbeat delta so a lag spike cannot drain or regen an unrealistic amount of stamina in one tick. Do not remove this clamp.Buff state is authoritative on the server. StaminaBuffSync pushes the current multipliers to the client for display only; the client never applies buffs directly to the drain/regen calculation.StaminaManager.Initialize() must be called once. It is called by StaminaSystemLoader.server.luau; do not call it from a second script.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Client code calls SoundManager.PlaySFX / PlaySFXAt / PlayLooped / PlayMusic / SetAmbience └─> SoundManager facade delegates to the appropriate submodule ├─ SFX.Play -> creates transient Sound in SoundService (2D one-shot) ├─ SFX.PlayAt -> Pool.Acquire(position) -> pooled part+Sound in workspace │ (Replicate=true) -> Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation:Fire -> server relay ├─ SFX.PlayLooped -> long-lived Sound in SoundService + LoopHandle returned ├─ Music.Play -> context playlist shuffle, gapped or crossfaded (MotionMaster volume fades) └─ Ambience.Set -> 2D bed Sounds in SoundService (MotionMaster fade in/out) Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation (client -> server -> other clients) └─> ReplicatedSoundService validates against ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS allowlist └─> FireClient to all players except sender └─> SFX.ConnectReplication handler -> Pool.Acquire positional playback Packets.SetMusicContext (server -> one client) └─> MusicService.SetContext(player, context) fires the packet └─> MusicDirector.client.luau resolves Combat > LowFuel > Normal └─> SoundManager.PlayMusic(context) -> Music.Play swaps/crossfades the playlist Signals.OnTrainStateChanged (client-local) └─> MusicDirector compares fuel / TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL against SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct └─> toggles the LowFuel context (no server involvement) SoundGroup bus hierarchy (Groups submodule): SoundService └─ Master SoundGroup ├─ SFX SoundGroup ├─ BGM SoundGroup └─ Ambience SoundGroup

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client — SoundManager (facade + submodules)  SoundController.client.luau calls SoundManager.Init() once at startup. Init creates the SoundGroup bus hierarchy (via Groups.Ensure), warms the positional sound pool (via Pool.Ensure and per-asset pre-warm), connects the replication receiver (SFX.ConnectReplication), preloads all configured asset IDs via ContentProvider:PreloadAsync, and autostarts any ambience beds listed in SoundConfig.Ambience.Autostart.  After Init, any client script or tool may require(SharedModules.SoundManager) and call the facade. The submodules (Groups, Pool, SFX, Music, Ambience) are internal and should not be required directly.  Client — MusicDirector.client.luau  A separate bootstrap script that owns the BGM context state machine. It holds two pieces of local state — combatContext (set by the server) and lowFuelActive (derived locally) — and resolves the active context by priority Combat > LowFuel > Normal every time either input changes, calling SoundManager.PlayMusic(context) only when the resolved context actually changes.  Server — MusicService.luau  Stateless server-side entry point for switching one player's BGM context: MusicService.SetContext(player, context) just fires Packets.SetMusicContext:FireClient(player, context). Gameplay code (combat events, outpost/enemy-camp zones) calls this directly; it holds no state of its own — the client tracks combat-vs-not and combines it with its own low-fuel detection.  Server — ReplicatedSoundService.server.luau  Listens on Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation.OnServerEvent. The server does not play audio itself — it acts only as a validated relay:  Per-player rate limit (MIN_INTERVAL = 0.05 s) rejects bursts.Payload shape is validated (data.SoundConfig.Id must be a string).The sound ID must be in ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS, which is built at startup from SoundConfig.GetReplicatedIds() — any SFX entry with Replicate = true is automatically included.Passes the original payload to all other connected players via FireClient.
