searchDocs.content: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/init.luau — public facade; the only module other scripts should requiresrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/Groups.luau — creates and manages the Master → SFX / BGM / Ambience SoundGroup hierarchy under SoundServicesrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/Pool.luau — per-asset pool of BasePart + Sound pairs used by PlaySFXAt for positional audiosrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/SFX.luau — Play (2D), PlayAt (positional pooled), PlayLooped (looped handle), and replication receiversrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/Music.luau — context playlist manager: shuffle, FadeIn/FadeOut, gapped silence (GapMin/GapMax) or continuous overlapping crossfadesrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/Ambience.luau — global 2D ambience bed management with MotionMaster fadesrc/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SoundController.client.luau — thin bootstrap; calls SoundManager.Init() oncesrc/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/MusicDirector.client.luau — resolves the active BGM context (Combat > LowFuel > Normal) and drives SoundManager.PlayMusicsrc/ServerStorage/SharedModules/MusicService.luau — server API (SetContext) for gameplay code to switch a player's combat music contextsrc/ServerScriptService/ReplicatedSoundService.server.luau — server relay with allowlist and rate-limit validationsrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luau — single source of truth for all asset IDs, volumes, pitch ranges, pool sizes, bus volumes, playlists, and ambience beds

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: Everything audio lives in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luau.  Bus volumes (SoundConfig.GroupVolumes):  Bus	DefaultMaster	1.0 SFX	1.0 BGM	0.6 Ambience	0.5  Per-SFX definition fields (SoundConfig.Sfx):  Field	DescriptionId	Roblox asset ID string; empty string disables the entry Volume	Default playback volume (0–1) Pitch	Fixed pitch multiplier PitchRange	Two-element array {min, max}; randomises pitch per play Group	Bus name ("SFX", "BGM", "Ambience"); defaults to "SFX" Replicate	true to include in the server relay allowlist Debounce	Minimum seconds between plays of this entry (anti-spam) PoolInitial	Pre-allocated pool slots warmed at Init (positional only) PoolMax	Hard cap on the per-asset pool size (positional only)  Adding a new replicable SFX: add the entry to SoundConfig.Sfx with Replicate = true. SoundConfig.GetReplicatedIds() and ReplicatedSoundService pick it up automatically on next server start — no changes needed in the server script.  Music playlist fields (SoundConfig.Music.Playlists):  Field	DescriptionTracks	Array of asset IDs; played in Shuffle order if set, else array order Shuffle	Randomise track order each time the playlist (re)starts FadeIn	Seconds to fade a new track up from 0 at start FadeOut	Seconds to fade a track down to 0 at its end; also the crossfade overlap window when continuous GapMin / GapMax	Random silence range (seconds) between tracks; GapMax <= 0 means continuous (overlapping crossfade, no silence) Volume	Target playback volume for tracks in this playlist  SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct (default 0.25) is the fuel-fraction threshold below which MusicDirector activates the LowFuel context.

searchDocs.title: BGM contexts​
searchDocs.content: SoundConfig.Music.Playlists defines exactly three named playlists — Normal, Combat, LowFuel — one per BGM context. There is no generic/default playlist; Music.Play falls back to "Normal" only when called with no argument.  Normal — default context. Gapped: GapMin = 60, GapMax = 300 seconds of silence between tracks.Combat — server-driven via MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat"). Continuous: GapMin = 0, GapMax = 0, so the next track starts before the current one ends (overlapping crossfade).LowFuel — client-derived automatically when fuel / TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL drops below SoundConfig.Music.LowFuelPct. Also continuous.  Priority when multiple conditions are true: Combat > LowFuel > Normal. MusicDirector.client.luau recomputes this on every change to either input (Packets.SetMusicContext.OnClientEvent for combat, Signals.OnTrainStateChanged for fuel) and only calls SoundManager.PlayMusic when the resolved context actually changes, so a low-fuel state during combat is suppressed without losing track when combat ends.  Driving combat from gameplay code (server-side, e.g. an event or outpost zone):  local MusicService = require(game.ServerStorage.SharedModules.MusicService) MusicService.SetContext(player, "Combat") -- on event/outpost enter MusicService.SetContext(player, "Normal") -- on event/outpost leave   MusicService.SetContext is stateless — it only fires Packets.SetMusicContext to the targeted player. All context resolution and the resulting PlayMusic call happen client-side in MusicDirector. See the Add a Sound playbook for adding tracks to a context playlist.

searchDocs.title: Volume persistence​
searchDocs.content: The four buses (Master, SFX, BGM, Ambience) persist across sessions as part of the generic user preferences system, not inside SoundManager itself. SoundManager.SetVolume(group, volume) / GetVolume(group) remain the immediate-apply primitives — they read/write the Groups bus hierarchy directly and do nothing else — but UI code that needs the change to be saved calls SettingsClient.Set("MasterVolume" | "MusicVolume" | "SFXVolume" | "AmbienceVolume", value) instead of SoundManager.SetVolume directly.  SettingsClient.Set validates the value via SettingsSchema, applies it (SettingsAppliers looks the key up in SettingsConfig.VolumeBusByKey and calls Groups.SetVolume on the mapped bus), fires Signals.OnSettingChanged(key, value) for any reactive listener, and schedules a debounced save that fires Packets.SaveSetting after coalescing rapid changes (e.g. a slider drag) into a single trailing send. On join, SettingsManager delivers the player's saved settings map via Packets.SyncSettings, and SettingsClient applies each valid entry the same way (SettingsAppliers.Apply, then Signals.OnSettingChanged) — but never re-saves a synced value, so applying it does not create a feedback loop. See the Settings system page for the full validate/apply/persist flow and how to add a new persisted setting.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Never create ad-hoc Sound instances All Sound creation must go through SoundManager. Creating Sound instances by hand bypasses the bus groups (so volume controls have no effect), skips the positional pool (causing memory churn), and may produce sounds that persist across character reloads without a cleanup path.  SoundManager.Init() must be called before any Play* call. It is called once by SoundController.client.luau; do not call it again from other scripts.PlaySFXAt is positional — it parents a pooled BasePart at the given Vector3 in the workspace. The pool releases the part after sound.TimeLength + 0.05 seconds. Do not hold references to the part or sound after the call.PlayLooped returns a LoopHandle. The caller is responsible for calling handle:Stop() or handle:Destroy() when the sound is no longer needed. Abandoning a handle leaks a live Sound instance under SoundService.A sound entry with Replicate = true and an empty Id string ("") is excluded from the allowlist automatically by GetReplicatedIds(). The pool warm step also skips empty IDs. Fill in the asset ID when the sound is ready — no further config changes are required.The BGM and Ambience buses default to volumes below 1.0. SFX entries authored at Volume = 0.5 will be audibly louder than music at the same numeric volume because the bus multipliers differ.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Server (TrainFuelManager) Client (TrainClient / TrainFuelGuiController) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Initialize(): fuelAtLastEvent = INITIAL_FUEL (80) isBraked = INITIAL_BRAKED (true) ──── TrainStateSync:Fire(fuel, rate, hasStarted = false isBraked, isStalled, serverTime) ──► currentRate = 0 (frozen until un-brake) reschedule() ← no task.delay while frozen Signals.OnTrainStateChanged:Fire(...) snap = { fuel, rate, isBraked, isStalled, serverTime } PlayerAdded: ──── TrainStateSync:FireClient(player, ...) ──────────────────────────────────► ── BRAKE TOGGLE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player triggers lever ProxPromptPart prompt ──── ReqToggleBrake(lever) ──────────► validate: lever tag, proximity isBraked = !isBraked if first un-brake: hasStarted = true Signals.SetTrainStarted:Fire(true) commitEvent() snapshot fuel currentRate = rateForState() scheduleNonce++ reschedule() → task.delay(timeToEmpty) TrainStateSync:Fire(...) Signals.SetTrainState:Fire(running) ◄── (success, isBraked, code) ──────── update lever ActionText ("Stop Train" / "Resume Train") ── REFUEL ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player triggers engine ProxPromptPart prompt ──── ReqRefuelTrain(engine) ─────────► validate: engine tag, proximity, not full gather Energy tools, sort smallest first consume tools until MAX_FUEL if stalled & fuel > 0: clear stall commitEvent(newFuel) ◄── (success, fuelAdded, code) ──────── ── STALL / GAME OVER (natural) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── task.delay(timeToEmpty) fires → onStall() isStalled = true commitEvent(0) ← exact 0, no float drift reschedule() → task.delay(GAME_OVER_DELAY) bar color = STALLED_COLOR task.delay(GAME_OVER_DELAY) fires → onGameOver() TrainGameOver.Trigger(TrainGameOverReason.FUEL_DEPLETED) ← reason 1 Signals.OnTrainGameOver:Fire(1) ── COMBAT FUEL-KILL (immediate, no grace) ────────────────────────────────────────── TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage(amount) while currentShield == 0: ApplyFuelDamage(amount * TrainConfig.FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR, source) guard: hasStarted, not HasFired(), amount > 0 newFuel = max(0, getFuel() - amount) if newFuel > 0: commitEvent(newFuel) ← just lowers fuel, natural stall timer shortens else: isStalled = true; gameOverFired = true ← suppress the natural grace timer commitEvent(0) TrainGameOver.Trigger(TrainGameOverReason.FUEL_DESTROYED_BY_ATTACK) ← reason 2, immediate Signals.OnTrainGameOver:Fire(2) ── CLIENT HUD LOOP ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── RunService.RenderStepped: predicted = snap.fuel - snap.rate * (serverTime_now - snap.serverTime) displayedFuel ≈ predicted (exponential smoothing, k=8) bar.Size = UDim2.new(pct, 0, 1, 0) bar color: green (running) / amber (braked) / red (stalled)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client — TrainClient.client.luauRegisters engine (TrainEngine-tagged) and lever (TrainBrakeLever-tagged) models via CollectionService. On engine Triggered it calls ReqRefuelTrain; surfaced error codes NO_ENERGY and FUEL_FULL fire Signals.RequestNotification toasts (warn / info respectively). On lever Triggered it calls ReqToggleBrake fire-and-forget — brake state replicates back via TrainStateSync. On PromptButtonHoldBegan it checks whether the player holds an Energy tool and shows a warning toast if not. Receives TrainStateSync and bridges it to Signals.OnTrainStateChanged.  Client — TrainFuelGuiController.client.luauReads the authored StarterGui.TrainFuelGui (never creates UI). Subscribes to Signals.OnTrainStateChanged to update snap. On every RenderStepped it computes predictedFuel from snap.fuel - snap.rate * elapsed and smooths displayedFuel toward it with frame-rate-independent exponential smoothing (k = 8). Sets FuelBar.Size and FuelText.Text, and colors the bar green/amber/red based on snap.isBraked / snap.isStalled.  Server — TrainFuelManager.luauInitialize() is called by TrainFuelSystemLoader.server.luau. All fuel arithmetic is algebraic: getFuel() = fuelAtLastEvent - currentRate * elapsed. commitEvent snapshots fuel under the old rate before switching, so the transition is seamless. A scheduleNonce guards task.delay callbacks — any subsequent commitEvent increments the nonce, and stale callbacks no-op when their captured nonce no longer matches. isRefueling is a boolean mutex that serializes concurrent refuel requests so two simultaneous players cannot both read the same pre-commit snapshot. On SetTrainState, JunkService is notified to adjust floating junk speed. ApplyFuelDamage(amount, source?) is the combat fuel-damage sink called by TrainShieldManager once the shield is down — see Game-over reasons below.  Server — TrainGameOver.luau (shared with shield)HasFired(), Trigger(reason: number?), GetReason(), Reset() — idempotent game-over gate. Trigger stores the TrainGameOverReason code (default NONE if omitted) and fires Signals.OnTrainGameOver(reasonCode) exactly once; subsequent calls are no-ops. Reset clears the fired flag and stored reason for a future round restart (not yet wired).  Shared — TrainGameOverReason.luauFrozen numeric enum identifying how a round ended: NONE = 0, FUEL_DEPLETED = 1 (natural fuel-out), FUEL_DESTROYED_BY_ATTACK = 2 (combat fuel-kill). Lives in ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules so both client and server can read it.  Shared — TrainConfig.luauSingle config table for fuel rates, tier recharge values, collision tags, and prompt names. Both client and server require it.

searchDocs.title: Game-over reasons​
searchDocs.content: There are exactly two ways a round ends, both funneled through the shared TrainGameOver.Trigger(reason) so the game-over sequence fires exactly once regardless of which path gets there first:  Reason	Code	Trigger path	Grace?FUEL_DEPLETED	1	Natural fuel-out. Fuel algebraically reaches 0 → onStall() marks the train stalled and broadcasts the 0 → after TrainConfig.GAME_OVER_DELAY (180s) elapses with no refuel, onGameOver() calls TrainGameOver.Trigger(TrainGameOverReason.FUEL_DEPLETED).	Yes — GAME_OVER_DELAY seconds to refuel before it's final. FUEL_DESTROYED_BY_ATTACK	2	Combat fuel-kill. TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage routes hits to TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage once the shield is at 0; if that hit drives fuel to exactly 0, TrainGameOver.Trigger(TrainGameOverReason.FUEL_DESTROYED_BY_ATTACK) fires immediately.	No — immediate, no GAME_OVER_DELAY.  TrainGameOverReason is a frozen enum module (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/TrainGameOverReason.luau). TrainGameOver.Trigger(reason: number?) records the reason (GetReason() returns it) and fires Signals.OnTrainGameOver(reasonCode) — a Signal.Signal<number> — exactly once per round; the events system is the intended consumer. Both code paths still only log and fire the signal — the real game-over mechanic (round reset / respawn / UI) remains out of scope and is a placeholder, same as before.

searchDocs.title: ApplyFuelDamage​
searchDocs.content: TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage(amount: number, source: any?) is the combat fuel-damage sink. amount is fuel units already converted by TrainConfig.FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR — callers (currently only TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage, once the shield is at 0) multiply the raw attack damage by the factor before calling.  Guards (all must pass or the call is a no-op):  hasStarted must be true (pre-game freeze, same as ApplyDamage)TrainGameOver.HasFired() must be falseamount must be > 0 and not NaN  If the hit leaves fuel above 0, it just commits the new (lower) level — the natural stall timer simply shortens, no special-casing needed. If the hit drives fuel to exactly 0, it's an immediate game over: isStalled and gameOverFired are set before commitEvent(0) so reschedule() arms no grace timer and rateForState() returns 0, then TrainGameOver.Trigger(TrainGameOverReason.FUEL_DESTROYED_BY_ATTACK) fires with no GAME_OVER_DELAY wait.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Frozen-start phase While hasStarted = false (before the first brake release), the drain rate is forced to 0 and no task.delay stall timer is scheduled. Any code path that reads currentRate or calls getFuel() before the first un-brake will see a frozen value — this is intentional. Do not bypass the hasStarted gate.  Game-over is a placeholder Both onGameOver() (natural) and the immediate combat-kill path in ApplyFuelDamage funnel through TrainGameOver.Trigger, which only logs and fires Signals.OnTrainGameOver. No round reset, respawn, or UI is triggered. Do not ship this system without replacing the placeholder with a real mechanic.  Combat fuel-kill skips the grace delay Unlike natural stall-out, a fuel-zeroing hit via ApplyFuelDamage ends the round immediately — GAME_OVER_DELAY is not consulted on that path. There is no window for the player to refuel after the killing blow. See Game-over reasons.  Algebraic drift note: commitEvent captures now() once and uses it for both lastEventTime and the serverTime field broadcast in TrainStateSync. If you add any task.wait or async work between the snapshot and the broadcast, the client's extrapolation baseline will drift. Keep commitEvent synchronous.  Nonce guard: every commitEvent increments scheduleNonce. Stall and game-over task.delay callbacks capture the nonce at schedule time and return early if it has changed. Do not call reschedule directly — always go through commitEvent.  Refuel mutex (isRefueling): the mutex is a simple boolean, not a queue. A second refuel request while one is in-flight returns NO_ENERGY even if the player has tools. This is intentional to avoid double-spending; the player can try again immediately after.  Studio model requirements: the TrainEngine-tagged and TrainBrakeLever-tagged roots (each a Model or BasePart) must contain a BasePart named "ProxPromptPart" with a child ProximityPrompt. The prompt's MaxActivationDistance and the engine's ActionText are authored in Studio; only the lever's ActionText is set by script. Both client and server resolve the prompt part recursively via ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PromptResolver, so it may be nested at any depth, not only as a direct child. The part's Studio name must match TrainConfig.PROMPT_PART_NAME.

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client — TrainShieldController.client.luauReceives TrainShieldSync from the server and bridges it to Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged. Also surfaces the ShieldConsole-tagged model's ProximityPrompt so players can interact — on Triggered it calls ReqRechargeShield: on success it plays SoundManager.PlaySFX("ShieldRecharge"); NO_ENERGY and SHIELD_FULL error codes fire Signals.RequestNotification toasts (warn / info respectively).  Client — TrainShieldGuiController.client.luauDrives the diegetic shield monitor — a SurfaceGui clone parented onto every BasePart tagged TrainConfig.SHIELD_MONITOR_TAG ("TrainShieldMonitor"), discovered via CollectionService. This replaces the old on-screen shield HUD entirely. See Shield monitor (SurfaceGui) below for the full behavior.  Server — TrainShieldManager.luauInitialize() is called by TrainShieldSystemLoader.server.luau. Owns the authoritative currentShield and maxShield values. Handles ReqRechargeShield.OnServerInvoke with an isRecharging boolean mutex. ApplyDamage is the single damage entry point for the shield; it is a no-op before hasStarted and after TrainGameOver.HasFired(). See ApplyDamage below for the absorb/bleed-through split. subscribeBuffs uses WaitForChild to attach GetAttributeChangedSignal listeners to both buff folders, and calls recomputeMax once after attach to catch any missed signals during the WaitForChild window.  Server — TrainShieldSystemLoader.server.luauThin bootstrap that calls TrainShieldManager.Initialize() once per server.  Server — EnergyToolHelper.luau (shared with fuel)GetEnergyTier(tool), GatherEnergyTools(player), ConsumeTool(player, tool) — server-only helpers shared by both TrainFuelManager and TrainShieldManager. Single source of truth for Energy tool scanning and consumption. No duplication between the two systems.  Server — ProximityValidation.luau (shared with fuel)FindPromptPart(root, partName), IsPlayerNear(player, promptPart, prompt, tolerance) — server-only helpers for console/engine proximity checks. Shared between refuel and shield recharge.  Server — TrainGameOver.luau (shared with fuel)HasFired(), Trigger(reason: number?), GetReason(), Reset() — idempotent game-over gate shared by both fuel-out paths. Shield depletion no longer triggers game over directly — only TrainFuelManager (natural stall-out or combat fuel-kill via shield bleed-through) calls Trigger. Trigger stores the TrainGameOverReason code, fires Signals.OnTrainGameOver(reasonCode) exactly once, and is a no-op on subsequent calls; Reset clears the flag and reason for round restart. See Train Fuel for the two reason codes.  Shared — TrainConfig.luauShield knobs alongside fuel knobs. See Config knobs below.

searchDocs.title: Shield monitor (SurfaceGui)​
searchDocs.content: The shield HUD is diegetic, not on-screen: TrainShieldGuiController clones the ReplicatedStorage.GuiAssets.TrainShieldGui SurfaceGui template onto every BasePart tagged TrainConfig.SHIELD_MONITOR_TAG ("TrainShieldMonitor"), discovered via CollectionService:GetTagged plus GetInstanceAddedSignal/GetInstanceRemovedSignal for live tag changes. The clone is created client-side, so each player drives their own independent copy of the monitor face on the same shared surface — there is no server/replication involvement in the GUI itself. Each registered monitor owns a Janitor that destroys the clone and disconnects its RunService.RenderStepped render loop when the tag is removed from the part.  The monitor drives two readouts:  Shield — displayedShieldPct is eased every frame toward the latest Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged snapshot (current / max, exponential smoothing). The status reads "Online" (cyan) while above 25%, and flips to "Critical" (red) at or below 25%, with hysteresis: once Critical, it doesn't return to Online until the displayed percentage rises back above 28%. Entering/exiting Critical also swaps the Shield ImageLabel's asset between a normal and a critical image, in addition to recoloring the percentage text and status label.Fuel reserve — extrapolated from Signals.OnTrainStateChanged exactly like the separate on-screen TrainFuelGui HUD (server snapshot + drain rate, predicted forward from workspace:GetServerTimeNow()). Cyan normally, turning red at or below 25% fuel. This is purely a second readout on the same monitor face — it does not replace or change TrainFuelGui.  The on-screen TrainFuelGui HUD (StarterGui, ScreenGui) is unchanged by this rework; it continues to run independently. No server, packet, or signal changes were made — the monitor consumes the same Signals.OnTrainShieldChanged and Signals.OnTrainStateChanged signals the old HUD and TrainFuelGui already used.

searchDocs.title: Max formula​
searchDocs.content: maxShield = (BASE_SHIELD + ResearchBuffs.MaxHP) * (1 + PartyPerkBuffs.TrainShieldBonus)   Research Bench additive: each completed level of Durability_T1 accumulates onto ResearchBuffs.MaxHP (+50 per level, up to MaxLevel = 3 for +150 total). This is added to BASE_SHIELD before the perk multiplier.Party perk multiplicative: TrainShieldBonus = 0.05 * maxLevel across all players (server-max resolution). Applied as a multiplier on top of the Research Bench + base sum.Ratio-preserving recompute: when either buff changes, recomputeMax preserves the current fill ratio (currentShield / oldMax) and rounds to the nearest integer. A player at 60% shield before an upgrade stays at ~60% after.  See Research Bench and Perks for the upstream buff systems.

searchDocs.title: ApplyDamage / fuel bleed-through​
searchDocs.content: TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage(amount, source?) is the single damage entry point for the train — all incoming attack/hazard damage, whether it lands on the shield or bleeds through to fuel, is routed through this one call. It is designed for future combat or hazard systems to call; no system calls it yet.  Guards (all must pass or the call is a no-op):  hasStarted must be true (pre-game freeze — shield cannot be damaged before first brake release)TrainGameOver.HasFired() must be false (no double-trigger after game over)amount must be > 0 and not NaN  Behavior branches on the current shield value:  Shield > 0 (absorbs): currentShield = max(0, currentShield - amount), then broadcasts. The hit that drives the shield exactly to 0 discards its excess — none of that hit's damage carries over to fuel. Reaching 0 this way does not end the round; the round continues with the shield depleted.Shield == 0 (bleeds through): the entire hit converts to fuel damage: TrainFuelManager.ApplyFuelDamage(amount * TrainConfig.FUEL_DAMAGE_FACTOR, source). See Train Fuel — Combat fuel-kill for what happens when this drains fuel to 0 (immediate game over, no grace).  This replaces the old behavior where the shield reaching 0 triggered TrainGameOver.Trigger("shield depleted") directly. Shield depletion is no longer a game-over condition by itself — it just removes the train's damage buffer, exposing fuel to combat damage.  The TrainCore tag (TrainConfig.CORE_TAG = "TrainCore") is reserved for the physical train model that future combat systems will tag; ApplyDamage does not read it directly — callers are expected to check that damage originated from a TrainCore-adjacent event before calling.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Recharge mutex is not a queue isRecharging is a boolean, not a queue. A second recharge request while one is in-flight returns SHIELD_FULL or NO_ENERGY (whichever applies) — not a queued success. The player can try again immediately after. This matches the fuel system's isRefueling behavior.  Pre-game freeze hasStarted is false until Signals.SetTrainStarted fires (i.e. the first brake release on the fuel side). ApplyDamage is a no-op until then. This matches the fuel system's freeze behavior. Do not try to damage the shield before the train is started.  Passive regen is off by default SHIELD_REGEN_ENABLED = false and SHIELD_REGEN_PER_SEC = 0. No regen loop exists yet. To add passive regen, implement a RunService.Heartbeat-based loop in TrainShieldManager gated on SHIELD_REGEN_ENABLED. Do not add regen without also updating this page and the config map.  Shield depletion is no longer a game over Reaching 0 shield used to call TrainGameOver.Trigger("shield depleted") directly — it no longer does. The shield can sit at 0 indefinitely; only fuel reaching 0 (natural stall-out or combat bleed-through) ends the round. See Train Fuel — game-over reasons.  Game-over is still a placeholder TrainGameOver.Trigger (invoked from the fuel side) currently only prints to output and fires Signals.OnTrainGameOver. No round reset, respawn, or UI is triggered. Do not ship without replacing it with a real mechanic.  typeof guard on OnServerInvoke ReqRechargeShield.OnServerInvoke receives (player, console) where console is client-supplied. The handler runs a typeof(console) == "Instance" guard before attempting to acquire the isRecharging lock, so a malformed invocation (e.g. nil or a non-Instance) is rejected cleanly without erroring.

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client — WeaponController.client.luauBootstrap that watches the local character for Tool equip/unequip events. Looks up WeaponConfig[tool.Name].Category and dispatches to the matching category handler (MeleeHandler, GunHandler, or ThrowableHandler). Creates one Janitor per equipped Tool (and one per character) so all connections clean up correctly on unequip, death, or weapon switch. Fires Signals.WeaponEquipped / Signals.WeaponUnequipped for the HUD, and Signals.RequestShootingCamera on equip/unequip to toggle the aim camera mode. Binds R to OnReload and G to OnDetonate for handlers that declare those callbacks.  Client — WeaponHandlers/MeleeHandler.luauCombo stepping: on each left-click it calls WeaponValidation.resolveComboSwing (tolerance 0) to determine the next step. If the click arrives during recovery it buffers one keyed retry via Janitor rather than dropping the input. Executes the predicted step: swing sound (SoundManager), optional AnimationTrack, local hitbox query (WeaponValidation.queryMeleeTargets) for an instant hitmarker (Signals.WeaponLocalHit), debug box draw, Signals.WeaponComboChanged, then fires payload-less ReqMeleeSwing. Client combo state is cleared on unequip.  Client — WeaponHandlers/GunHandler.luauHitscan + rocket cosmetic + ammo prediction. On activate, gates on a client-local fire-rate check and predicted magazine count (via AmmoApi), then fires ReqFireWeapon(origin, dir). Draws the shooter's own tracer (hitscan only; rocket has no local projectile). Supports semi and automatic fire. OnReload fires ReqReloadWeapon and predicts the ammo transition after the server-confirmed reload window. Authoritative ammo is reconciled via WeaponMagSync → Signals.WeaponMagChanged and AmmoPoolSync → Signals.AmmoPoolChanged.  Client — WeaponHandlers/ThrowableHandler.luauGrenade and C4. On activate, gates on the throw cooldown, plays throw sound, and fires ReqThrowProjectile(origin, dir). No local projectile cosmetic — the server-spawned instance replicates to all clients. For C4 (Detonation == "Manual"), OnDetonate fires ReqDetonate. Grenade ignores G.  Client — WeaponHandlers/TrajectoryPreview.luauClient-local green-neon ballistic arc shown while any throwable is equipped. Uses a fixed pool of reused BasePart segments updated every RenderStepped. Origin offset (SPAWN_OFFSET = 2.5) and upward aim bias match ServerProjectile / ThrowableHandler exactly so the preview arc matches the real projectile path. Purely cosmetic — no packets sent.  Client — WeaponEffectsController.client.luauConsumes replicated combat FX packets. WeaponFired: ignored for the local shooter (who already drew its own tracer); renders tracer + impact spark for other players' shots. WeaponImpact: impact spark + sound for all melee/gun hits. ExplosionAt: expanding neon sphere + sound for rocket, grenade, and C4 detonations — fires for everyone, including the shooter.  Shared — WeaponValidation.luauPure math run on both client (prediction) and server (authority):  canFire(lastFireTime, cooldown, now) — fire-rate gate.meleeHitbox(rootCFrame, range, hitboxSize) — single source of truth for the oriented swing box CFrame and size.queryMeleeTargets(rootCFrame, range, hitboxSize, ignore) — box overlap returning unique Humanoid-bearing Models.resolveComboSwing(state, combo, now, tolerance) — pure combo step resolution; shared so client and server stay in sync.resolveStep(config, step) — merges step overrides with weapon-level defaults into a ResolvedStep.applySpread(direction, spreadDegrees) — applies a random spread cone to an aim direction (cosmetic on client; server does its own authoritative ray).isWithinRange(origin, hitPos, maxDistance) — range cap check.ammoAfterShot(mag) / ammoReloadFromPool(mag, pool, magazineSize) — pure ammo transitions. ammoReloadFromPool returns (newMag, taken) where taken is the pool amount consumed.aoeFalloff(center, hitPos, radius, maxDamage) — linear AOE falloff.queryAOEModels(center, radius, ignore) — sphere overlap returning { model, humanoid, distance } for AOE application.  Server — WeaponServer.server.luauReceives all weapon packets. Per-category validation (fire-rate, ammo, origin tolerance, direction validity) before any damage or projectile spawn. Manages gun ammo initialisation on equip via WeaponState.EnsureAmmo + WeaponMagSync. On reload, waits ReloadTime, calls ammoReloadFromPool, consumes the drawn ammo from AmmoManager, then fires WeaponMagSync + AmmoPoolSync (the latter emitted by AmmoManager.ConsumeAmmo). On a successful throwable throw, the server destroys the player's matching Tool (onThrowProjectile — 1 Tool = 1 throw). Drives the FastCast2 rocket caster (rocketServerCaster) — its LengthChanged callback steps the cosmetic part, its Hit callback calls CombatService.ApplyAOE and broadcasts ExplosionAt. Handles throwable throw (onThrowProjectile) and detonate (onDetonate).  Server — CombatService.luauSingle damage router. Two primary entry points:  ApplyToModel(model, humanoid, amount, attackType, attacker, aoeVariant?) — applies damage to a resolved Model. Players route through HealthManager.ApplyDamage (keeping the HUD-tracked record correct); faction-tagged NPCs ("EnemyNPC" / "FriendlyNPC") take direct humanoid:TakeDamage. Anything without a recognized faction is ignored. Friendly-fire is enforced via Factions.canDamage: only Player↔Enemy damage lands; players never hurt players or friendly NPCs. A nil attacker is treated as environmental and bypasses the faction gate. Self-damage from one's own AOE is exempt.ApplyAOE(center, radius, maxDamage, attackType, attacker, ignore) — calls queryAOEModels, applies aoeFalloff to each target, and routes through ApplyToModel with aoeVariant = "Explosion".  Also available: ApplyToPart(part, amount, attackType, attacker, aoeVariant?) — resolves a hit part to its Humanoid-bearing Model then calls ApplyToModel.  Server — WeaponState.luauPer-player authoritative state. Fields per player record:  lastFire: { [weaponName]: number } — os.clock() of last shot/swing per weapon; gates fire-rate.combo: { [weaponName]: { index, lastHitTime } } — authoritative combo progress.ammo: { [weaponName]: { mag, reloadEndsAt } } — magazine count and reload window (reloadEndsAt is the os.clock() timestamp when a reload finishes; 0 means not reloading). Reserve is no longer stored here — pool ammo is owned by AmmoManager.active: { ActiveCharge } — active manual throwables (C4) awaiting detonation.  Key functions: EnsureAmmo (seeds magazine from config), GetMag/SetMag, GetLastFire/SetLastFire, GetCombo/SetCombo, IsReloading, SetReloadEnd, GetActiveCount, AddActive, TakeAllActive. Clear destroys all active charges and removes the player's record on PlayerRemoving.  Server — ServerProjectile.luauSpawns and owns server-authoritative, replicated projectile instances cloned from ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets into workspace/ServerProjectiles. Two spawn paths:  spawnRocket(templateName, cframe) — anchored, non-collidable cosmetic part; the caller (WeaponServer) steps its CFrame along the FastCast2 cast.spawnThrowable(templateName, origin, direction, speed, rest, ignore) — server-owned physics rigid body. prepareAssembly un-anchors all parts, sets the WeaponProjectile collision group (passes through characters), and applies per-mode elasticity: "Stick" (C4) elasticity = 0 (lands dead); "Bounce" (Grenade) elasticity = 0.15 (one small hop). installSettle polls until the charge has contacted a world surface and come to rest, then anchors it flat. Network ownership is kept server-side via root:SetNetworkOwner(nil).

searchDocs.title: HUD integration contract​
searchDocs.content: This system ships no UI. A HUD widget that wants to display ammo or combat feedback must consume:  Packets (server → owning client, handled by AmmoApi): WeaponMagSync(weaponName, mag) — authoritative magazine count sent on equip, after each shot, and after reload completion.AmmoPoolSync(ammoType, amount) — authoritative pool count for a given ammo type sent whenever the pool changes (shot, reload, craft). AmmoApi read surface (preferred over raw packets): AmmoApi.GetMag(weaponName) → (mag, magSize) — current magazine and max size.AmmoApi.GetPool(ammoType) → (amount, capacity) — current pool and capacity cap.AmmoApi.GetEquippedAmmo() → (mag, magSize, pool, cap)? — combined ammo for the equipped gun; nil for non-guns.AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount(toolName) → count — counts matching Tools in the Backpack + equipped slot. Signals (client-side): WeaponEquipped(toolName, category) — fired on equip.WeaponUnequipped(toolName) — fired on unequip.WeaponMagChanged(weaponName, mag) — fired by AmmoApi on predicted mag update and on WeaponMagSync reconciliation.AmmoPoolChanged(ammoType, amount) — fired by AmmoApi on AmmoPoolSync or local prediction.ThrowableCountChanged(toolName, count) — fired by AmmoApi when the backpack throwable count changes.WeaponReloadStarted(weaponName, reloadTime) — fired when a reload request is sent.WeaponReloadComplete(weaponName) — fired when the reload window elapses or reload is rejected.WeaponLocalHit(model) — fired on a predicted melee/hitscan hit for hitmarker display.WeaponComboChanged(toolName, stepIndex, totalSteps) — fired on each combo step advance.  See Signals Map for the full signal registry.

searchDocs.title: Ammo HUD​
searchDocs.content: AmmoHudController (client) drives the authored AmmoGui (bottom-rightScreenGui). It shows the equipped weapon's DisplayName and, for guns, the loaded magazine over the reserve pool (mag / pool); for throwables, the carried count. It is hidden for melee and when nothing is equipped. All data comes from AmmoApi + the weapon/ammo Signals; the HUD never talks to the server.

searchDocs.title: Pool and magazine model​
searchDocs.content: Ammo is split into two distinct layers:  Magazine (WeaponState, server) — per-gun in-memory count representing what is currently loaded. The magazine is seeded to MagazineSize rounds on the gun's first equip (EnsureAmmo) and then persists across deaths within the session (it is not refilled on every equip or on respawn). On each shot the magazine decrements by one. On reload, the magazine refills from the pool. The magazine is the only ammo state WeaponState owns; there is no longer a reserve field per gun.Pool (AmmoManager, server) — per-player, per-type in-memory count of unloaded ammo. Entirely session-only — nothing is persisted to a DataStore. The pool is seeded to each type's Starting value on the player's first spawn only; it then persists across deaths for the rest of the session (dying never refills reserve ammo). Every type's Starting is 0: players are never given free reserve ammo — all reserve ammo is crafted (see Crafting ammo). AmmoManager.EnsureStarting re-syncs the current pool to the owning client on each respawn so the HUD shows the correct value after the character and Backpack rebuild. The pool is shared across all guns of the same ammo type.  A freshly crafted weapon still spawns with one full magazine (the magazine is seeded to MagazineSize on first equip), so it can fire immediately. But once that magazine is emptied the gun cannot be reloaded until the player crafts ammo into the reserve pool.

searchDocs.title: Reload flow​
searchDocs.content: Client fires ReqReloadWeapon.Server checks mag < magSize and pool > 0; rejects otherwise (returns 0 reload time).Server waits ReloadTime, then calls ammoReloadFromPool(mag, pool, magSize) (in WeaponValidation), which returns (newMag, taken).AmmoManager.ConsumeAmmo(player, ammoType, taken) is called atomically; it clamps, deducts, and fires AmmoPoolSync to the owning client.Server sets the new magazine via WeaponState.SetMag and fires WeaponMagSync to the owning client.

searchDocs.title: Throwables​
searchDocs.content: Throwables are physical Roblox Tools in the player's Backpack. Each throw consumes exactly one Tool: WeaponServer.onThrowProjectile destroys the equipped throwable Tool server-side on a successful throw. There is no numeric reserve or CarryCount in WeaponState — count is inferred by AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount by scanning the Backpack and equipped slot.  C4 detonation is intentionally decoupled from holding the Tool: ThrowableDetonateController.client.luau listens for the global G keybind and fires ReqDetonate regardless of what is currently equipped. The server no-ops if the player has no active charges. This design handles the edge case where the last C4 was thrown (destroying its Tool) but live charges are still stuck to surfaces awaiting detonation.

searchDocs.title: Crafting ammo​
searchDocs.content: See Workbench Crafting for the full crafting flow; the recipe values below are illustrative — WorkbenchConfig.Recipes is canonical.  Ammo can be replenished at a Workbench. Crafting recipes in the "ammo" category call AmmoManager.AddAmmo (which clamps to Capacity). Available ammo recipes:  Recipe	OutputCraftLightAmmo	+60 Light Rounds CraftHeavyAmmo	+12 Heavy Rounds CraftRocketAmmo	+2 Rockets CraftGrenade	3 Grenade Tools CraftC4	1 C4 Tool  Weapon Tool recipes clone the template from ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates directly into the player's Backpack.

searchDocs.title: Client read surface (AmmoApi)​
searchDocs.content: AmmoApi (src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/AmmoApi.luau) is the single client-side cache and read surface for all ammo data. HUD widgets and handlers should call AmmoApi rather than listening to raw packets.  Method	Returns	NotesGetMag(weaponName)	(mag, magSize)	Current magazine count and magazine capacity. GetPool(ammoType)	(amount, capacity)	Current pool count and pool capacity cap. GetEquippedAmmo()	(mag, magSize, pool, cap)?	Combined view for the equipped gun; nil for non-guns or unarmed. GetThrowableCount(toolName)	count	Counts matching Tool instances in Backpack + equipped slot.  AmmoApi listens to WeaponMagSync and AmmoPoolSync packets, updates its cache, and fires the corresponding Signals. It also watches the player's Backpack for tool additions/removals (rebinding per-character via Janitor) to keep GetThrowableCount accurate. Bootstrapped once by AmmoController.client.luau.

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: WeaponConfig.luau is the per-weapon registry. Edit stats here — never in handler or server code.  Common fields (all weapons):  Category — "Melee" | "Gun" | "Throwable".DisplayName — human-readable label.ToolName — must match the in-game Tool's Name exactly (used as a packet/state key).Damage — base damage per hit (melee: default per-step; gun: per bullet; throwable: 0, AOE only).DamageType — "Melee" | "Bullet" | "AOE".HeadshotMultiplier? — optional multiplier applied by the server when the ray hits a part named "Head" (gun only).  Melee fields:  Range — forward reach in studs (also hitbox depth).HitboxSize — Vector3 width × height (Z ignored; depth = Range).SwingSound / ImpactSound — SoundConfig.Sfx keys.SwingAnimId? — optional rbxassetid for a swing animation track.Combos — map keyed by input ("Primary" = left-click; "Secondary" reserved). Each ComboDef has: Steps[] — ordered ComboStep array; combo length = #Steps. Each step: Recovery (min seconds before next hit), ChainWindow (seconds to keep combo alive past this hit), optional overrides Damage?, Range?, HitboxSize?, AnimId?, SwingSound?, ImpactSound?.ResetCooldown — brief lockout after the finisher before restarting at hit 1.  Gun fields:  FireMode — "Hitscan" | "Projectile".RPM — rounds per minute; fire interval = 60 / RPM.Automatic — true = hold-to-fire; false = semi-auto.MagazineSize — rounds loaded per magazine. Reserve pool is not stored here; it is owned by AmmoManager and keyed by AmmoType.AmmoType — ammo-pool key ("Light" | "Heavy" | "Rocket"); maps this gun to its shared pool in AmmoConfig.ReloadTime — seconds.Spread — max cone half-angle in degrees.MaxDistance — hit range cap (studs).FireSound / ReloadSound / DrySound / ImpactSound — SoundConfig.Sfx keys.Projectile-only additions: ProjectileSpeed (studs/sec), Gravity (Vector3 acceleration), AOERadius, AOEDamage (center damage, linear falloff to 0 at radius), CosmeticTemplate (name in ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets).  Throwable fields:  Detonation — "Fuse" (auto after FuseTime) | "Manual" (all charges detonate on ReqDetonate).Rest — "Bounce" (small hop, settles) | "Stick" (lands dead on first contact).ThrowSpeed — initial velocity (studs/sec).FuseTime — (Fuse only) seconds from throw to detonation.MaxActive — (Manual only) max simultaneously active charges per player.AOERadius / AOEDamage — explosion radius and center damage (linear falloff).CooldownTime — seconds between throws.CosmeticTemplate — name in ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets.ThrowSound / ExplodeSound — SoundConfig.Sfx keys.  Note: CarryCount has been removed. How many throwables a player carries is determined by how many matching Tool instances are in their Backpack (crafted or spawned). AmmoApi.GetThrowableCount reads this count at runtime.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Fire-rate enforcement Guns enforce 60/RPM intervals via WeaponState.GetLastFire; melee enforces Recovery, ChainWindow, and ResetCooldown per combo step via WeaponValidation.resolveComboSwing (server tolerance = 0.05 s). Requests that arrive too early are silently dropped.  Server-authoritative ammo and reload Magazine counts and reload timing are owned by WeaponState on the server; pool ammo is owned by AmmoManager. Firing at an empty magazine is rejected. Firing while a reload window is active (reloadEndsAt > now) is rejected. Reloading with an empty pool is rejected. Neither the magazine count, pool count, nor the reload timer is read from the client.  Origin, spread, and distance validation The claimed muzzle origin for guns and throw origin for throwables must be within 14 studs of the server-side HumanoidRootPart position and must be a finite (non-NaN) vector. Claimed directions with zero or non-finite magnitude are rejected before normalization. The server caps hitscan range at MaxDistance on its authoritative ray; applySpread is applied client-side for feel only — the server recasts from the validated origin and does not verify the spread angle.  Friendly-fire prevention Enforced in CombatService.ApplyToModel via Factions.canDamage. Only Player↔Enemy damage lands. Players never damage other players or friendly NPCs; enemies never damage other enemies or friendly NPCs. Self-damage from one's own AOE is exempt — the self-check bypasses the faction gate so a player's own rocket can still hurt them if they walk into the blast.  NPC pass-through via CollectionService tag: the "EnemyNPC" / "FriendlyNPC" CollectionService tag is the dual-purpose NPC marker. It gates damage routing in CombatService (only tagged NPCs with a Humanoid take weapon damage) and, via NpcCollisionService, places NPC parts in the Character collision group so thrown charges physically pass through them. A Model without a recognized faction tag receives no damage and does not block thrown projectiles — tag it or it is invisible to the weapon system.  HealthManager routing via CombatService: HealthManager writes record.Health → humanoid.Health but never reads back from the Humanoid. Any external write that bypasses HealthManager.ApplyDamage (via CombatService) will leave the HUD showing a stale record value. Never write to humanoid.Health directly for player damage.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Client (WorkbenchGuiController) Server (WorkbenchService) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ── OPEN ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player walks within INTERACT_DISTANCE ProximityPrompt fires (CraftPromptPart) GUI opens; recipe grid populated from WorkbenchConfig.Recipes ResearchUnlocked folder checked → grey any gated recipe whose RequiresNode value is not yet in the folder ── SELECT RECIPE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player clicks a recipe tile Detail panel shows DisplayName, Description, Tier badge, Cost rows (Wood / Metal — exactly two rows max), RequiresNode note ── CRAFT ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player clicks Craft button ──── ReqCraft(bench: Instance, recipeId: String) ─────────────► Server (WorkbenchService) validates, in order: look up recipe in WorkbenchConfig (else UNKNOWN_RECIPE) verify bench is a tagged Workbench Model (else INVALID_TARGET) re-check proximity (INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE) (else TOO_FAR) CRAFT_COOLDOWN gate (per-player timestamp) (else COOLDOWN) check RequiresNode gate in ResearchUnlocked (else LOCKED) CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(recipe.Output) → verify output slot is usable BEFORE consuming any materials (else OUTPUT_FAILED) player holds enough cost materials (else INSUFFICIENT_MATERIALS) on pass: consume materials from player Backpack, then CraftOutputDispatcher.grant(player, recipe.Output) Kind == "Weapon" → clone from WeaponTemplates Kind == "Armor" → ArmorManager.SetTier(player, output.Tier) Kind == "Placeable" → grant PlaceableTools Tool record cooldown timestamp ◄── (success: Boolean8, code: NumberU8) ────────────────────────── if success: Signals.OnItemCrafted:Fire(recipeId) GUI shows success FX / SoundManager.PlaySFX(CraftSuccess) else: show failure toast / SoundManager.PlaySFX(CraftFail)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — WorkbenchResultCodes.luau (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/) is a frozen result-code enum identical in role to ResearchResultCodes. Every reject reason (NONE, UNKNOWN_RECIPE, INVALID_TARGET, TOO_FAR, COOLDOWN, LOCKED, OUTPUT_FAILED, INSUFFICIENT_MATERIALS) is defined here so neither side ever uses bare string literals in business logic.  Shared — Configs/WorkbenchConfig.luau (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/) is the single tuning surface: interaction constants, output template folder names, category lists, sound keys, and the Recipes table. See Config knobs below.  Shared — WorkbenchValidation.luau (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/) is a pure, stateless validator with no Roblox service calls. It runs on both client (button-greying, cost display) and server (authority). Exported functions mirror the pattern from ResearchState: recipe existence, gate check, material sufficiency.  Server — WorkbenchService.server.luau (ServerScriptService/) is the sole owner of the authoritative ReqCraft handler. It resolves the bench instance, re-checks proximity, runs WorkbenchValidation, calls CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible before touching any materials, then consumes materials and calls CraftOutputDispatcher.grant. Manages the per-player cooldown timestamp.  Server — CraftOutputDispatcher.luau (ServerStorage/SharedModules/) handles the three output kinds:  Kind == "Weapon" — clones the named Tool from ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates into the player's Backpack.Kind == "Armor" — calls ArmorManager.SetTier(player, output.Tier), updating ArmorState/<UserId>.ArmorBaseReduction in ReplicatedStorage.Kind == "Placeable" — grants the named Tool from ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> into the player's Backpack.  isFeasible(output) verifies the target output slot is usable (e.g. the template exists, the tier is valid) before materials are consumed. A misconfigured recipe never costs the player materials.  Client — WorkbenchGuiController.client.luau (StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/) opens via the bench CraftPromptPart ProximityPrompt. Builds the recipe grid from WorkbenchConfig.Recipes and greys any recipe whose RequiresNode is not present in ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked. Fires ReqCraft on the Craft button and fires Signals.OnItemCrafted on a confirmed success. The CloseButton closes the GUI. The DropdownButton is driven by the reusable Dropdown widget, which fires Signals.RequestWorkbenchCategory on selection to re-filter the grid. Uses a Janitor per GUI open/close lifecycle.

searchDocs.title: Recipe schema​
searchDocs.content: Recipes are declared in WorkbenchConfig.Recipes as a { [string]: Recipe } table keyed by a string recipe ID.  export type Output = { Kind: "Weapon", ToolName: string } | { Kind: "Armor", Tier: number } | { Kind: "Placeable", PlaceableName: string } export type Recipe = { Category: string, -- one of RecipeCategories ("weapons"|"ammo"|"armor"|"workstation") DisplayName: string, Description: string, Tier: number, -- 1..5 flavor/quality badge only; NOT a prerequisite ladder Icon: string, -- rbxassetid:// string for the grid tile and detail panel Cost: { Wood: number?, Metal: number? }, RequiresNode: string?, -- Research Bench nodeId gate; nil = always available Output: Output, }   Tier is a purely cosmetic quality badge displayed as a star rating in the GUI. It has no prerequisite chain and imposes no unlock order — any recipe with RequiresNode = nil is available to craft at any time regardless of Tier. The only unlock gate is RequiresNode.  The Cost table is limited to Wood and Metal because the GUI renders exactly two material rows. Adding a third material requires a GUI layout change and a matching config key.

searchDocs.title: Research gate seam​
searchDocs.content: ResearchEffectsDispatcher publishes leveled-up node IDs into a ReplicatedStorage/ResearchUnlocked folder (a BoolValue per node at level ≥ 1, named by nodeId) in parallel to the ResearchBuffs folder. This folder is written by the server whenever a node reaches level 1 and is read by:  WorkbenchService (server): authoritative gate check. A craft request whose recipe has a non-nil RequiresNode is rejected with LOCKED if the corresponding BoolValue is absent or false. Because the folder is written by the server, clients cannot forge an unlock.WorkbenchGuiController (client): greying. Recipes with a locked RequiresNode are rendered as unavailable in the grid so players know they need to research the gating node first. The client reads this folder but never writes it.  Unlike the old Tech Tree (where a node auto-unlocked the instant its pooled material cost was met), a gating Research Bench node now also costs time: the player pays materials on enqueue, then the node's level advances in real time (gated by bench fuel) before ResearchUnlocked is written. Recipes behind a RequiresNode are therefore no longer available the moment materials are gathered — see Research Bench for the full enqueue/advance/complete flow and the ResearchBuffs/ResearchUnlocked folder contract.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: Tag the Workbench Model. In ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/Workbench, tag the root Model with the CollectionService tag Workbench (the same tag the Shredder scans for — one Model serves as both crafting station and shredder). Give it a BasePart named CraftPromptPart (anywhere under the Model — PromptResolver finds it recursively) containing a ProximityPrompt. Set the Model's PrimaryPart. The shredder half uses a sibling ShredPromptPart. Create ServerStorage/WeaponTemplates. Add a folder named WeaponTemplates inside ServerStorage. Place craftable weapon Tools here (e.g. clones of Pistol and SMG from StarterPack). These are separate from the StarterPack copies — the Workbench clones from here into the player's Backpack, so stat changes or visual differences can live here independently. Ensure craftable placeables exist. Each recipe with Output.Kind == "Placeable" needs a Tool at ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<PlaceableName>. The Workbench itself already follows this convention as a grid-placeable item. Material templates are shared. ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials already holds Wood and Metal Tool templates (shared with the Shredder and Research Bench systems). No duplication is needed. Wire ResearchUnlocked. ResearchEffectsDispatcher creates and writes this folder automatically at runtime. No manual Studio setup is required for the gate to function. If testing in isolation (without a running ResearchService/ResearchEffectsDispatcher), create a Folder named ResearchUnlocked in ReplicatedStorage and add BoolValue children named after whichever node IDs you want to treat as unlocked.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas / anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Server re-checks proximity on every craft The client proximity prompt is never trusted. WorkbenchService re-runs the distance check using INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE on every ReqCraft call. A player exploiting from range receives TOO_FAR.  Feasibility is checked before materials are consumed CraftOutputDispatcher.isFeasible(recipe.Output) runs (and must succeed) before any material Tool is removed from the player's Backpack. A recipe that references a missing weapon template or an invalid armor tier therefore fails without costing the player anything. Misconfigured recipes are safe to ship; they only result in a visible craft failure.  Research gate is read from server-written state The ResearchUnlocked folder is written exclusively by ResearchEffectsDispatcher on the server. A client cannot create or modify entries in that folder. The server re-reads the folder on every ReqCraft call, so a client that somehow fakes the UI greying cannot bypass the gate.  Cost is limited to Wood and Metal The GUI renders exactly two material rows. Cost may only specify Wood and/or Metal. Adding a third material type (e.g. Energy) requires a GUI layout change alongside the config key — otherwise the cost is silently unchecked on the client (though the server will still validate it).  Tier is a flavor badge, not a prerequisite ladder Tier (1–5) drives the star-rating display only. There is no inter-recipe prerequisite chain derived from Tier values. The sole unlock gate is RequiresNode. Do not attempt to use Tier as a crafting order enforcer — it will not work without code changes.  Known edge case: respawn mid-craft (v1) If a player's Backpack disappears between the feasibility check passing and CraftOutputDispatcher.grant executing (e.g. the player respawns during that narrow window), materials may be consumed but the grant returns OUTPUT_FAILED. The client receives a failure response and the player loses the materials. This is an accepted v1 limitation — the window is sub-frame in practice. A future refund path or a pre-grant Backpack re-check is the recommended fix.
